1. Introduction
This user's guide covers the CAM editing functions. For information on the CAD functions, please refer to
the corresponding software documentation.
hyperMILL: integrated CAM Application.
The
hyperMILL CAM solution requires you to have installed a working version of a CAD application or the
Geometric Engine from
hyperMILL, into which it is fully integrated..
hyperMILL is available as an integrated
application for the following CAD systems:
•
hyperMILL CAD
•
hyperMILL for Autodesk® Inventor®
•
hyperMILL for SOLIDWORKS
Note that some of the functions described in this guide are not available in your installation. The range of
functions depends on the licenses obtained and the configuration of the software purchased.
SHOP Viewer
The SHOP Viewer allows you to display, analyse and document processed CAD/CAM data. The following
software documentation explains all the features of
hyperMILL. The functions described may not be
available or may not be available to the extent described, in SHOP Viewer.
Save data
When data is saved as a SHOP Viewer document ( *.hmc), the following options can be enabled
and included as components in the file in the Setup dialog: stock data, toolpath entities, postprocessor
configuration, prepared geometry.
Reusing SHOP Viewer data (also called SHOP Viewer Pack & Go data) in
hyperMILL is intended for
OPEN MIND support and analysis purposes only. If Pack & Go data are changed in
hyperMILL and then
saved with the Save as function, the usability of the resulting file can not be guaranteed.
Supported CAD formats
Supports a wide range of geometry formats (for example, DXF, DWG, IGES, VDA), which enable data
exchange with the majority of CAD construction programs. Data conversion takes place in the background,
while the model is loading.
During conversion, a log window with status information is displayed. The corresponding log file (*.log) can
be opened and viewed later on from within the directory of the associated model file.
Direct interfaces are provided as modules for the following data formats: CATIA V4,
CATIA V5, PTC CREO, Siemens NX, Parasolid and SolidWorks. Please contact your
dealer.
The following formats are supported for saving model data and for CAM editing:
CAM
7

-- 7 of 1632 --

• *.hmc:
hyperMILL document format,
• *.hcplain: Uncompressed
hyperMILL document format,
• *.hmct: Format for saving a geometry as a template for a new document,
• *.hmcgeom: Native format. Contains only geometric and topological data in binary, uncompressed
format including information on solids and meshes, but no colours,attributes and so on.
• *.e2 and *.e3: Formats that can be imported with
hyperMILL CAD,
• *.ipt:
hyperMILL for Autodesk® Inventor®.
• *.sldprt and *.sldasm:
hyperMILL for SOLIDWORKS.

2. User interface
hyperMILL and CAD program
hyperMILL is a CAM module that is fully integrated into the CAD program and is used for generating 2D,
3D, 5-axis, milling and turning programs. Individual machining steps (jobs) are created on the basis of
machining cycles with the open CAD model in the form of one or more work schedules (joblists).
All functions of the
hyperMILL toolkit, as well as all input pages, menus and programs that can be opened
with icons can also be accessed using keyboard commands and repeated using <return>.
When you open a document, the
hyperMILL browser opens automatically. All CAM functionalities can be
accessed via the CAM entry in the menu bar.

Configure browser
The tabs can be arranged anywhere in the browser or undocked from the browser window. To do this, click
the tab with the left mouse button and drag the tab to the required place while holding down the mouse
button. Possible docking positions are indicated by a graphical feedback as blue, transparent areas. Dock
or undock the tab from the browser by double-clicking (left mouse button) the title bar in the browser.
Show or hide a tab. Right-click the tab and enable or disable the respective command on the shortcut
menu.

hyperMILL browser.
CAM → Setup View manager

Job definition dialogs
Dialog control configuration
Set the dialog control in the hyperMILL settings → Setup dialog, on the Application dialog page.
Dialogs
Modal: The input dialogs contain the general function icons. It is not possible to quickly switch the display
between different jobs.
Modeless: The input dialogs do not contain any general function icons. It is possible to quickly switch the
display between different jobs.
The dialog control functions can be accessed via the shortcut menu of the input dialog header. Input
dialogs can be fixed to any chosen position by clicking on a pin in the header. Jobs can be calculated
when a dialog is open
In this mode all settings are applied immediately and are always saved when the dialog is closed. It is not
possible to exit without saving changes.
Text: dialog tabs contain text that displays the contents. In the case of cycles with a high number of
definition parameters, the different tabs cannot be viewed side by side.
Icons: dialog tabs contain icons that display the contents. Even in the case of cycles with a high number of
definition parameters, all the tabs can be viewed side by side.
dialog control functions
The general dialog control functions can be accessed via icons (only in Modal) mode or via the shortcut
menu.
Shortcut menu: Position the mouse pointer in the left half of the input dialog header, then right-click. The
content depends on the input dialog and the selected mode for dialog control (modal/modeless).

Dialog positioning
In the Modeless dialog control mode, all input dialogs that are opened via the browser feature a pin
that allows the dialog to be fixed anywhere on the screen. Message windows always feature this pin,
regardless of which dialog control mode is set.
Dialog is not pinned: The current dialog window will close when you switch to another dialog or to the
browser.
Dialog is pinned: Pinning allows you to simultaneously display different dialogs for a job (for example,
job, tool and frame definition assigned to each other as well as message windows). When you select a
different job list entry, the display switches to the definitions for the currently selected list entry. This means
that you can quickly check all definitions for a job. The contents of the open message window refresh
immediately when you edit in other dialog windows.

Input field colors
Black input value: The value is correct.
Red input value: The job can be calculated with this value, however, collisions might occur. Read the warn-
ing in the message window. Change the respective values if necessary and check the job in simulation
after calculating the toolpath.
Input field values
Values can be entered as follows:
• Direct entry of required value into input field.
• Use of a predefined local cycle parameters.
• Definition of user variables.
• Definition using arithmetical expressions.
Local parameters and user variables can be combined in a single expression. You may also enter all
values directly into the input field using the keyboard.
Local cycle parameters
Depending on the cycle and input dialog, you can also use predefined local cycle parameters.
Click the icon to select a local parameter directly from the shortcut menu (J:). All the entries that you
make directly in the input field can be made without the J: prefix (as long as there are no user-defined
variables with the same name). No distinction is made between upper and lower case.

(R=0), lock the parameters for Path compensation so that the toolpath is always output
to the tool center point.
User variables
Click the icon (to the right of the input fields) to define a user variable and select the Create user
variables option.
The User Variable window opens. Right-click and then select New.... Enter the required data in the Code,
Value and Description fields. You can also enter predefined arithmetical expressions in the Value field.
Double-click the corresponding line of a user variable to change its definition. The most recently used
variables are displayed in the middle third of the shortcut menu (max.5 variables displayed). All data that
you enter directly into the input fields has to be entered in exactly the same way as defined in the variable.
Upper and lower case is not freely definable.

Excel. Supported formats:

hyperMILL: *.vst
• For Excel: Text (Tab delimited) (*.txt) and Formatted Text (Space delimited)
(*.prn).
Requirements for importing user variables via an Excel table:
1. The table must consist of three columns (name, diameter, comment).
2. In the selection dialog *.* must be set as a file type.
3. The file to be imported must be available in *.txt or *.prn format.

3. Basics of CAM editing
Overview: From the model to the NC program
The modular structure of
hyperMILL creates a flexible workflow from the model to the NC program.
Important elements of this workflow include:
1. CAM/CAD system
2. Specifying the basic settings
Define the measurement system and storage directories for
hyperMILL data. Configure the dialog
control, configure the tool and macro database and define further basic settings.
3. Define workpiece origin and frame(s)
With the origin reference system (NC system), establish a connection to the machine coordinate
system.
Using a frame, define the current machining side and machining direction.
Use origins to control the NC output and apply origins when defining transformations.
4. Define tool
Define a new tool or apply a tool from the tool database.
5. Prepare manufacturing geometry (contours, surfaces, stock model)
Both 2D contours and CAD models can be used for 2D machining.
3D, 5-axis and turning jobs are based on a CAD model.
A stock model can be defined for various machining operations.
6. Structure CAM project (define job list and jobs)
Define job and job list.
Use compound jobs to structure the workflow within a job list.
7. Collision check preparations
Specify a milling area or turning area to define the collision-checked part of the CAD model.
Define a collision-checked clamping area to firmly fix the workpiece during machining.
8. Calculate and analyze toolpaths
Calculate toolpaths either directly in the job definition or in the
hyperMILL browser.
Analyse toolpaths via the menu
hyperMILL → Analysis toolpath. For more information, see the
software documentation for the CAD system.
9. Simulate machining and generate NC program
Simulate machining using the internal simulation, the internal machine simulation, the
hyperVIEW
program, the VIRTUAL Machining Center or an external simulation program.
Output an NC program either via the Generate NC file shortcut menu in the
hyperMILL browser or
using
hyperVIEW.

Using the Project Assistant
Use the Project Assistant to create a milling project or MillTurn project in a predefined sequence of steps.
The following are defined in the individual steps:
• Model and machining technology
• NCS orientation
• Stock size and allowances

Function
Max. number of origins: Limits the maximum permissible number of origins.
Use global clearance plane: Select this option to use the global clearance plane of the frame instead of the
clearance plane from the job definition. The formula value for the global clearance plane will then be firmly
linked with the Clearance plane parameter for the job definition (greyed out).
To machine with a job-related clearance plane, adapt the Clearance plane job parameter by right-clicking
and then clicking Unlink on the shortcut menu.
Prefer featurelist frame: Activate to copy the frame assigned to a feature to the job.
Requirement: During feature mapping (hole), the Use feature list function is activated and the Frame
creation mode has been set to 2D.
If the Prefer featurelist frame function is not activated, the NCS is assigned to the job if its orientation is
identical to that for the frame orientation of the feature.
Use parameter: This function must be activated when local cycle parameters or user variables are to be
used as part of the job definition (also see Input field values).
Calculation
These settings apply to toolpath generation.
Display temporary graphics : Temporary toolpaths created during the calculation are shown on screen in
the interim and are then replaced by the final toolpaths.
Erase existing toolpaths: The next time a job is calculated, the existing toolpath is deleted. The newly
generated toolpath is output graphically on the screen.
Automatic geometry check: After a geometry that is to be machined has been modified, the outdated
geometry data is deleted from the cache before each calculation and the modified geometry is converted
again.
This function should always be enabled (it is active by default) in order to avoid faulty
calculations.
Notify changed geometry: A message is generated for the geometry to be machined before the job is
recalculated to notify the user that modified geometry data has been found and that the stored data will be
deleted.
Delete temporary files: Deletes the temporary files ( *.tmp) created during job list calculation. Do not
select this option if you are having problems with a component that requires the assistance of your OPEN
MIND dealer.
Preserve reports: Save your report file in the folder defined on the Application dialog page of the Setup
hyperMILL dialog (default paths).
Check toolpath status
Check geometry: When geometry changes are made, the system checks whether the toolpath is still
up-to-date.
A modified geometry is displayed in the
hyperMILL browser following a Check toolpath
status. As this function uses up a lot of processing time, it is disabled by default.

Performance
Use all CPU resources for cycle computing: The majority of cycles support multi-core processors and
perform calculations in parallel. If this option is selected, all of your computer's CPU resources will be
used for cycle computing. Please note that the simultaneous use of
hyperMILL for interactive work during
a calculation may slow down the system. If the option is not selected, a part of your computer's CPU
resources will be available during cycle computing for simultaneous
hyperMILL use, which means that
toolpath calculation may be slowed down as a result.
Backup
The Activate option allows
hyperMILL to create backup copies of the CAD model files used ( *.hmc /
*.e3). Backup files are created as:
[Original file name]_ [n].hmc.hyperMILL

hyperMILL, change the file extension to *.hmc / *.e3.
Number of backup copies per document: Specifies the number of backup copies per CAD model file. At
present, you can create up to 999 backup copies. Each time you save the model file, a backup copy
is created. Once the maximum number of backup copies is reached, the backup copy created first is
overwritten.
Save backup in user-defined folder: Backup files are saved in a user-defined directory. This directory is
either the directory displayed under Default paths → Backup files or (if the Project directories option has
been enabled on the Document dialog page) in the corresponding project directory.

NC system and frames
With the origin reference system (NC system), establish a connection to the machine coordinate system.
Using a frame, define the current machining side and machining direction.
Use origins to control the NC output and apply origins when defining transformations.
NC system
The NC system defines the position of the workpiece origin and the orientation of the machining axes
(XYZ).
The workpiece origin must match the reference point of the workpiece on the machine.
hyperMILL calculates all the toolpaths in the NC system. The NC system applies to an entire job list at one
time.
Define NC system
When a new (empty) joblist is opened, the NC system aligns with the world workplane. Before a joblist is
defined, the NC system must be adapted to the machining conditions. These changes can be made via the
joblist (Setup dialog page) or the frame definition.
Frame
A frame defines the current machining side and orientation. In multi-axis indexing, a frame has to be
defined for each machining side. The assignment of the frame to a job takes place in the job definition.

-- 43 of 1632 --

All frames must be defined before generating the toolpaths. Subsequent movement or
rotation will mean having to recalculate all tool paths affected by the change. If the NC
system is modified, then the entire job list has to be recalculated. If frames are modified,
the affected jobs must be recalculated.
Correct job definition and therefore machining can be achieved only if the frame is in the correct position
and orientation for the job, because:
All definitions for the vertical machining area are in relation to the frame (top, bottom), clearance distance,
XY plane, horizontal stepover.
The frame shares responsibility for collision checking during machining.
Surfaces that cannot be recognized from the tool axis perspective (1) are not machined.
In
hyperMILL, the first point of a toolpath can also lie below the level given by the height of the machining
side in the z+ direction. This generally means below the uppermost point in the model. The positioning
movements made by the machine axes up to this first point are not represented in the toolpath, but defined
in the postprocessor. An OPEN MIND postprocessor positions the rotational axes first, and only then
proceeds to the first point of the toolpath along the linear axes. This needs to be taken into particular
consideration during 5X programming, for example, when linking with the Clearance mode → Radial option
or when linking triaxial toolpaths with differently oriented frames.

Clamping position dialog page
The Clamping position dialog page is only available via the Define frame dialog in the job list (dialog page
Setup → NCS.
Use the clamping position to specify the zero point for the simulation. The table upper edge middle point of
the machine model serves as the reference.
The Z axis of the clamping position must always be defined parallel to the Z axis of the NCS. If rotation is
required, use the NCS transformation function in the machine configuration.
Examples:
1. The Clamping position option is not enabled. The model and clamp are placed in the middle of
the table in the machine model used in the simulation.
2. The Clamping position option is enabled, no movement is defined.
Origin: X = 0, Y = 0, Z = 0.
The joblist NC system is placed in the middle of the table in the machine model used in the
simulation.
3. The Clamping position option is enabled and a movement is defined.
Origin: X = -100, Y = -100, Z = -218.
The job list NC system is placed according to the defined movement against the table upper edge
middle reference point of the machine model used in the simulation.
If subsequent changes are made to the clamping position, update the jobs in the job
list using the Update clamping position function (job list's shortcut menu). It is not
necessary to recalculate the jobs.

Frame limit
None: The hole features may be in all directions.

Yellow: All jobs with a hole feature direction within the area marked in yellow will be merged into the
corresponding joblist.
Green: All jobs with a hole feature direction within the area marked in green will be merged into an
additionally created joblist.

Corrected output system dialog page
BEST FIT
More complex part shapes, alternative manufacturing processes (casting, 3D printing,
forged stock) and smaller allowances make manually aligning the part very time-con-
suming. The
hyperMILL Best Fit alignment eliminates the need for time-consuming
manual alignment measures. Positioning is automatic and based on the internal origin
shift captured using the 3D Point Probing cycle. Probing takes place both in the CAM
programming and on the machine, so that the position deviation between the virtual and
the real situation can be determined and corrected. The Best Fit real part position is
adjusted in the VIRTUAL Machining Center and is checked for collisions. An attempt is
made to comply with all machine limits with the help of the NC optimizer.
CORRECTED OUTPUT SYSTEM
In series production or workshop use, OPEN MIND generally recommends Best Fit
adjustment via the VIRTUAL Machining Center. For single parts, prototypes or large
toolpath files, the zero point can already be corrected in
hyperMILL. The shift is transfer-
red directly to the VIRTUAL Machining Center which means that the real position has
already been adjusted. After the collision check and release, the NC program can be
executed on the real position.
The Corrected output system dialog page is only displayed with a license for the VIRTU-
AL Machining Center. It is not available for origins. It is available for frames if the Best
Fit function has been activated on the Job list → Settings dialog page.

Example of use
Contour Milling on 3D Model- Transformations
To machine a contour on four different sides of a cube in a job, for example, you just have to program this
on one side. The other three sides of the cube are machined automatically by transformation. To do this in
the job definition, proceed as follows:
1. Create an origin for each side to be machined. Then create a frame for each origin using the New
frame from origin shortcut menu.
2. Make the required settings in each of the job dialogs. Make sure that the correct frame (defined
for the contour) is set in the Tool → Frame area. Then switch to the Transformation dialog page.
3. Define a General pattern where you specify each of the previously defined (origin-based) frames
as the target reference system. Switch to the Transformation dialog page of the job definition, set
the transformation to Active, disable the Keep original job option and select the Use job frame
option under Start reference.
In the calculation that follows, hyperMILL transforms the contour defined on the one side of the cube to
three other sides of the cube and therefore allows complete machining of all sides of the cube in a single
job.
Please note, that you need a special license to use this function. Please contact your OPEN MIND partner.

NCS and frame lie in one plane
Using
hyperMILL, it is possible to generate an NC output in these situations without switching workplanes
even when using indexing postprocessors.
All toolpath points (coordinates) refer to the active origin/NCS. In addition, the Z axes of the NCS and the
job frame must have the same direction.
If you would like to have this type of NC output, please contact your OPEN MIND partner, who will be glad
to assist you in enabling this new output.

Using
hyperMILL, it is possible to force jobs with transformations to switch to a different workplane for each
job created by a transformation if all these transformations are in the same plane as the job frame.
If the job frame and NCS are in the same plane and an NC output was already enabled for the NCS, then
this option is not available. Please contact your OPEN MIND partner to arrange this.

An external database and a document database are available for managing tools. Tools stored in the
external database are called external tools. Tools stored in the document database are called document

lar, angle tools or angle heads are not supported.

Meaning of the symbols
(1) The value in the cutting profile corresponds to the value in the technology data of the tool. The value
can be changed with a factor. To do so, select the field and enter the required factor.
(2) The value in the cutting profile is adjusted by a factor.
(3) The value in the cutting profile has been adjusted and is no longer linked to the technology data of the
tool. Place the mouse pointer over the changed value to display the value of the technology data.
(4) The value in the cutting profile has exceeded the limit defined in the technology data and was automati-
cally reset to the limit.
(5) Click the button to remove the link between the value in the cutting profile and the technology data
value. The cutting profile value can now be adjusted as required without changing the value in the
technology data and vice versa.
(6) Click the button to restore the link between the cutting profile and technology data. The value in the
cutting profile is then overwritten again by the value in the technology data.

hyperMILL browser, switch to the Tools tab, highlight the tool and choose Export to tool database
from the shortcut menu. If the ID of the tool already exists in the external database, a dialog box ( Con-

again in the external database. If the tool contains components that are already present in the external

exists. If no exact match exists, the differences will be displayed in a dialog box.
A password is requested when exporting to a password-protected database. The database remains pass-
word- protected after a successful export. For a re-export you need to re-enter the password.

Prepare manufacturing geometry
Both 2D contours and CAD models can be used for 2D machining.
3D, 5-axis and turning jobs are based on a CAD model.
A stock model can be defined for various machining operations.
2D machining
You can select the following contours:
• Lines, circles, polylines, splines, graphics loaded in *.omxformat (Contour Milling, Pocket Milling
and Helical Drilling).
• Points (drill positions)
Generate contours from toolpaths: Curves extracted from previously calculated toolpaths can be used both
as 2D contours and as help contours for 3D or 5-axis machining. For information on selecting contours,
see section Selecting elements in the CAD system.
3D and 5-axis machining
3D and 5-axis machining are based on a CAD model. This contains:
The CAD model
The basis for the creation of an NC program for 3D machining is the CAD model created in the CAD
program and consisting of surfaces and/or solids. It contains all areas to be machined, as well as adjacent
areas that are not to be machined in order to optimize the machining procedure and the collision check. 2D
or 3D lines that are used as limitation contours or leading curves for profiles during the job definition.
Surface gaps
Make sure that no gaps arise between adjacent surfaces or between adjacent surfaces and solids during
model creation. Large surface gaps can cause unwanted nose-diving of the cutter in the course of machin-
ing. Gaps with a size below the used cutter radius are not critical.
Overlapping surfaces
Overlapping surfaces can result in unwanted rest material areas. These areas cannot be removed by Auto-
matic rest material recognition, as they are not the result of too large cutter diameters but of intersecting
surfaces.
In the course of, and after creating machining cycles, the CAD model must neither be moved nor changed
in its position in space.
CAM
64

-- 64 of 1632 --

Negative allowances
The following restriction applies to all cycles: If the sum of the allowances is negative, the sum total must
be less than the Tool radius - Machining tolerance.
Example:
Tool radius = 5.00 mm
Machining tolerance = 0.01 mm
Allowance = -3.0mm
Additional allowance XY must be greater than -1.99 mm, e.g. 1.98, because
|-3.00 mm +(-1.98 mm)| < 5.00 mm -0.01 mm
In this context, the area-based allowance is also taken into account as an allowance in the Milling area →
definition. If several values are defined here, only the smallest value is taken into account.
Stock
A stock model in *.stl (Stereo Lithography) or *.vis (Visicut) format can be defined for various ma-
chining operations. Stock models in the format *.vis are recommended if you require greater accuracy
and want to use the stock models that are generated in further stock model calculations (= stock model
update).
If a stock model in *.stl format is used for a stock model update, it has to be a closed
solid.
By default, stock models with a file size of up to 200 MB are displayed in
hyperMILL. If
the stock file is larger, this is indicated in the browser by the following icon: . The size
limit can be adjusted to suit individual requirements in the dialog hyperMILL settings →
CAD document → STL file display.
Collision check
The updated stock model is checked for collisions. This guarantees that both tracked and calculated stock
models are always collision-checked.

shortcut menu in the lower area of the

for subsequent machining (stock model update).

Optimized stock model generation in 5X machining
The prerequisite for optimized stock model generation is that the Cutting length parameter is defined in the
tool definition of the underlying job. The following tool types are not subject to this requirement: Lollipop,
Barrel cutter, T-Slot cutter and Woodruff cutter.
The following applies to tapered and non-tapered tools: If no Cutting length is defined (value is 0), then
the Tip length parameter is used. The following applies for ball mills and bullnose end mills: If the Cutting
length is smaller than the Corner radius, then the Corner radius is used.
Mirror stock
Each stock mirror is based on an existing stock and the definition of a mirror. You can either mirror
individual stock models in the stock browser or all the stock models of a job list.
Mirror individual stock model
To mirror an individual stock model:
1. Select the stock model that you want to mirror in the stock browser and choose the Mirror stock
function from the shortcut menu.
2. Specify the mirror you require or define a new mirror in the Mirror stock dialog. For information on
defining a mirror, please see the Mirror section.
The mirrored stock model is displayed in the stock browser as follows: < Stock name[ mirrored]>.
Mirroring all stock in a joblist
When you mirror a job list you also have the option of mirroring the related stocks.
To mirror all stock models in a job list:
1. Double-click the job list entry and switch to the Mirror dialog page.
2. Set the mirror function to Active and enable the Copy option for Manufacturing parameters.
3. Answer the question Would you like stocks to be mirrored? with Yes.
Mirrored stocks are created for all stocks used in the job list. They are displayed in the stock browser as
follows: Stock name[mirrored]>.
Stock in *.vis format, Resulting stock, Cast offset stock and Compound stock cannot
be mirrored. Stock models resulting from mirrors (mirrored stock) are not associative. If
the original stock or the mirror plane changes, the stock models are not updated.
Combine multiple stock models
If you want to machine several components together that each have a separate stock model, you can
merge the stock models to form a Compound stock. A component can be machined and checked against
the compound stock at the same time.
To create a compound stock:

1. Right-click the stock browser and select New compound stock.
2. Then select the required stocks in the list of available stock models and confirm your selection.
Edit stock
The Edit stock function can be used to further process stock resulting from the preceding stock calculation.
1. Select the stock model that you want to process further and
2. select the Edit stock function from the shortcut menu.
Two functions are available in the Edit stock dialog.
The Split stock function splits the selected stock model into independent areas arising as the result of a
preceding machining job (see Calculate stock section). Each area is created as a new stock entry in the
stock browser (Stock[Split1].vis, Stock[Split2].vis, and so on).
The Clean stock function creates those stock areas connected with the selected milling area as a new
stock entry in the stock browser (Stock[Cleaned].vis).
Create stock chain
Use the Create stock chain function to create a resulting stock model for any job in a sequence of
machining steps, based on the stock model of the preceding job and the toolpath of the current job. This
function is available for joblists, any jobs in a joblist, an individual job or a compound job.
Requirements: A start stockmodel must be present. All toolpaths of the jobs for which a stockmodel is to
be created must have been calculated.
Procedure:
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, select the jobs for which you want to create a stock chain.
2. Select the Stock → Create stock chain function from the shortcut menu.
hyperMILL creates a stock object in the stock browser for each of the selected jobs.
To calculate the stock models, use the Stock → Calculate (update) function on the shortcut menu.
hyperMILL calculates the stock models for each of the generated stock objects. The stock models are
indicated by a corresponding icon in the stock browser.

Structure CAM project
Structure a CAM project in the

CAM Plan
The CAM plan includes functions that simplify the programming process. From analyzing the part, display-
ing and repairing possible surface defects to the automatic generation of features and geometries required
for programming. In addition, the CAM plan provides a platform for advanced technologies and more
interactivity during programming. The CAM plan is a dialog page in the
hyperMILL browser, divided into a
structure tree (in the upper part) and the Selections and Tasks areas (in the lower part).
CAM
73

-- 73 of 1632 --

Job list Uppermost administration level in the
hyperMILL job browser. If projects have a simple structure, the job
list (work schedule) is usually sufficient for including all the jobs required to machine a workpiece in the
correct sequence. Several job lists can be assigned to one CAD model. A job list can be transferred to
other CAD models that have a similar machining sequence.
Compound job
Organize your job lists with compound jobs and clearly structure extensive CAM projects. Use compound
jobs to structure transformations or assign individual transformations to several jobs. In contrast to job lists,
which only permit mirrors, compound jobs also allow linear patterns and circular patterns in addition to
mirrors.
Job Lowermost administration level in the
hyperMILL job browser. A
hyperMILL job is a typical machining step
within a joblist. The following machining strategies are available for defining jobs: Probing, Turning, Drilling,
2D Milling, 3D Milling, 5-axis Milling.
Linking job
Link jobs with each other in such a way that approach and retract movements for the entire machining
sequence and all linking movements between the individual jobs can be optimized and monitored for
collisions.
NC eventStructure your programming, independent of joblists and jobs, with control-specific functions and com-
mands that are forwarded directly to the postprocessor.
CAM Plan
The CAM plan includes functions that simplify the programming process. From analyzing the part, display-
ing and repairing possible surface defects to the automatic generation of features and geometries required
for programming. In addition, the CAM plan provides a platform for advanced technologies and more
interactivity during programming. The CAM plan is a dialog page in the
hyperMILL browser, divided into a
structure tree (in the upper part) and the Selections and Tasks areas (in the lower part).
After activating the CAM plan in the
hyperMILL settings (CAM menu Setup → Settings → hyperMILL
settings → CAM Plan → Activate CAM Plan), select a predefined project template. Depending on which
template was selected, the CAM plan contains different functions and tasks.
Use the / icons in the structure tree to control the visibility of elements.
To avoid possible issues during programming, all the tasks offered should be carried
out.
General (complementary): Control the visibility of all geometries not selected as a part using the /
icons.
Part: Select the surfaces of the part to be programmed without unnecessary additional surfaces or hole
capping. Then go through the tasks step by step to prepare the part completely.
Remove duplicate surfaces: Check the part for double surfaces and remove them if present.
CAM
74

-- 74 of 1632 --

Check surfaces: Check the selected surfaces for possible defects that could cause problems in the
subsequent programming process. If a damaged surface is found, the first step is to attempt to repair
the surface automatically. In the next step, a new layer is created, the corresponding surface is moved
there and removed from the selection made in Part. Ensure that this or any newly constructed surface is
included in the part selection again.
hyperMILL converter check: Check whether the selected part can be converted by the converter.
Check for gaps: Check whether there are gaps between the selected surfaces. If gaps are found, a layer
is automatically created upon which the gaps are displayed using curves and points. Decide whether the
gaps should be corrected or not. Skip this task by deactivating the corresponding option at Computable
task.
Orientate surfaces: Check whether the selected surfaces are correctly orientated. After starting the task,
the corresponding CAD function opens automatically and aligns the surfaces. Manually align any surfaces
that are not aligned correctly. The corresponding surfaces are displayed in a dark color.
Hole recognition / add capping: This task starts the Feature mapping based on the selection made for the
Part. Capping surfaces are automatically created for the recognized holes, a new layer is created and the
surfaces are moved there. Skip this task by deactivating the corresponding option at Computable task.
Create milling area(s): The milling areas required for programming are created automatically. Depending
on the selected project template one or two milling areas are created. If a template "with holes" has been
selected, two milling areas are created. One milling area that contains the part and the holes and one
milling area that contains no holes but the capping surfaces. If the "without holes" template has been
selected, only one milling area is created.
HPM Milling: Select all surfaces that are relevant as product surfaces for 3D finishing and create topology
information from them. The curves generated represent the exact topology information of the product
surfaces. They are saved internally and used for the point distribution of 3D finishing.

Job list
A job list is automatically created when you call up a machining cycle for a job definition.

Job list settings can be defined separately for each job list. You must make the settings before you
calculate the toolpaths.
To edit, double-click the joblist or select the Edit function from the shortcut menu.
Export/import job list
Save a joblist with all its parameters and settings in *.jst format and transfer to other CAD models.
Advantages: Job archiving is independent of the drawings, fast programming of frequently occurring
procedures, transfer of jobs to workpieces with the same drawing parts when machining sequence is the
same.
To export a job list:
1. Select job list and then select the Export function from the shortcut menu.
2. Specify the required export options as well as the name and path (storage location) of the file.
Include tools / Include geometry / Include frames: Tools, geometries (boundaries, profiles) and frames are
also exported along with the machining parameters.
Include milling area references / Include stock references / Include feature references: Milling areas, stock
models and features are also exported.
To import a job list:
1. Use the New → Load from file function on the browser's shortcut menu.
2. Select the *.jst file and enable the required import options.
The Export and Import functions are also available for the individual jobs in a job list.
Direct job transfer
Direct transfer of job lists or selected jobs to other CAD models using the Copy and Paste functions on the
shortcut menu. When pasting into a job list, select the ( Include tools / Include geometry) import options:
All tools assigned to the job or all defined geometries (boundaries, profiles) of the job are imported with the
machining parameters.

NC
The functions Origin ID (NCS) and NC safety are available with a license for the VIRTU-
AL Machining Center or the VIRTUAL Machining Optimizer. Please contact your OPEN
MIND partner.
Origin ID (NCS)
Use global definition: Enable to use the default settings of the VIRTUAL Machining postprocessor for
creating the NC file.
Origin ID (NCS): Activate to select the origin directly from the list for different projects or setups. Time-con-
suming reconfiguration in the VIRTUAL Machining Center is no longer necessary.
NC safety / Postprocessor safe positions
When the Postprocessor safe positions option is used, fixed positions in the machine coordinate system
are used to ensure NC safety.
The positions are stored in the postprocessor configuration and are approached, in particular, for safe
positioning (by moving linear and rotary axes). When approaching the positions, the NC file switches to
machine coordinates (for example M91 for Heidenhain, SUPA for Siemens).
NC safety / General safety
Use different safety functions (clearance distance/clearance plane) to enable collision-free machining on
the machine.
Prefer general safety: Activate for machining operations in which collision safety must be guaranteed
regardless of the model geometry and the tools used. The function combines the following strategies:
• (A): Machining with short tool. Linking movements take place at the level of the Security plane, see
General safety → Security plane.
• (B): Machining with very long tool. The 2D Curve is used to guide the tool, see NC safety - interac-
tive → 2D Curve. Linking movements take place at the Linking height, see NC safety - interactive →
Linking height.
If the Prefer general safety function is activated,
hyperMILL automatically decides between variants (A)
and (B), whereby (A) is generally used so long as the tool length is sufficiently short and the Z axis limits
are not violated. Otherwise, variant (B) is used.

NC safety / Optimized tunnel logic
The Optimized tunnel logic function is specially developed for machines with two rotary
axes in the table and the possibility of collision-safe positioning of the tool and spindle
by retreating into a tunnel with the Z axis. When approaching and retracting for NC jobs,
all axes except Z are positioned in a rapid traverse block, which significantly reduces
non-productive times.
Axial security distance: Distance to be maintained for the tool in the axial direction
If the Optimize clearance plane and Smooth linking functions are not activated, the defined axial security
distance is maintained to the highest point of the initial stock model of the job list, to the part and to the
fixture during linking movements between the jobs without a change of inclination.
When changing the inclination, a maximum retraction takes place in the direction of the tool axis up to the
tunnel position.
Fast travel movements from and to the
hyperMILL job clearance plane are automatically adjusted.
Optimize clearance plane: If the Optimize clearance plane function is activated, the defined axial security
distance is maintained to the highest point of the initial stock model of the job list, to the part and to the
fixture during linking movements between the jobs without a change of inclination.
When changing the inclination, the axial security distance to the initial stock model of the job list, to the part
and to the fixture is maintained.
Fast travel movements from and to the
hyperMILL job clearance plane are automatically adjusted.
Smooth linking: Optionally, the link rapids, including connections with alternating inclination, are made
using a natural movement that is adapted to the machine kinematics. The optimization of the
hyperMILL
job clearance planes is automatically activated during smooth linking.
If the Smooth linking function is activated, the axial security distance is maintained to the component and
to the fixture for all linking movements between the jobs.

Collision avoidance when changing solutions – Virtual Machine configuration
Initial situation: Collision avoidance for component, fixture, stock model, machine table against machine
housing/frame when changing solutions.
Collisions are prevented when changing solutions between two machining operations by activating the
Check machine body option and Rewind safe axis option in the Virtual Machine configuration. This is
achieved by an additional movement in the linear axis.
The axis in which the additional movement of the linear axis is to take place is to be selected as the
Rewind safe axis.
It is advisable to activate the functionality for machining oversized components on machines with at least
one linear axis and rotary axis in the machine table. This is also recommended for machines in which the
machine table can collide with the machine housing/frame when moving the rotary axis.
In order to carry out the optimization safely, it is necessary that the component is clamped on the real
machine identically to how it was collision-checked in the virtual machine.
Rewind safe axis not activated in the Virtual Machine configuration.
Rewind safe axis activated in the Virtual Machine configuration.

NC file names: Enable and select the method for naming the NC files (Single mode/Package mode).

page is disabled or for compound jobs that have no jobs for NC generation. Jobs for which the option
create NC file is disabled, are not included in the
hyperVIEW simulation.
Rule for filename generation: As standard, the file name of the NC file is composed of the following
elements: Jobname_Job ID.
Increment to job ID: This value is added to the job ID.
Package mode: All NC data for the selected joblist is written to a file. The name of the job list is used as
the file prefix.
Start of counter: Counters that the programme can output for NC file names. The NC file names created in
single mode are numbered consecutively.
Compound job as single job: Only available in single mode. If the function is enabled, all jobs in a
compound job will be written to a single NC file. The name of the compound job is used for the placeholder
in the NC file.
Vector fine interpolation: Enabled by default. The definition of a maximum permissible angle change
makes it possible for vector fine interpolation to control machine movements in the case of vector changes.
If you enable the function,
hyperMILL will insert intermediate points into the toolpath in order to avoid any
diverging interpolation of the machine from the calculated toolpath.

5X Rapid mode
Default: 5X rapid tool movements occur as defined in the cycle.
Optimized: Select this option to avoid a possible pole pass and high acceleration of the C axis for 5X
machining fast travel movements. This is made possible by simultaneous 5-axis rotary movements (conical
interpolation). On the whole, the movements of the machine are softer, faster and more predictable.

If the feedback display is activated, the tool, tool holder and tool head are shown by default:
• at the zero point of the WCS if the tool is defined in the browser.
• at the zero point of the selected frame if the tool is defined directly in the Job dialog.

General dialog page in the job definition input dialog.

can also be placed at any location.
Right-click the icon, choose Point and direction. The selected Base point determines the position. The

tool movements (G0) and infeed movements (G1) can be defined.

Tolerance cycle setting
Depending on the machining situation, use different tolerance values to generate the NC file. The values
influence the machining accuracy on the machine via the NC Generator and so enable an optimal combi-
nation of precision and dynamics adapted to the machining situation.
Roughing, Semi finishing or Finishing are already preset depending on the job and can be can be adapted
as required. Define the required tolerance values in the NC Generator → NC → General → Accuracy dialog.
Additional options
Relevant for two or more jobs with identical tool in direct machining sequence.
Force tool call: If the function is enabled for all jobs, the tool is called from all jobs at the beginning in the
postprocessor run. Safety positioning is carried out before and after each tool call. All relevant technology
commands are regenerated after each tool call.
If the function is not activated, the tool is called only at the beginning of the first job. Safety positioning is
carried out before and after the tool call. All relevant technology commands are regenerated after the tool
call.

NC Optimizer
When the Use NC Optimizer option is selected, the calculated NC program is divided between the axes
that exist in the machine. This way, collision situations and axis limitations are automatically taken into
account so that a checked toolpath is generated on the machine.
The NC Optimizer function is available with an appropriate license for the VIRTUAL
Machining Optimizer. Please contact your OPEN MIND partner.
OPEN MIND strongly recommends that you use the NC Optimizer for:
• 5-axis machining with rotary axes that do not rotate endlessly
OPEN MIND recommends that you use the NC Optimizer for:
• 5-axis simultaneous applications
• Machines that cannot move over the table center
• Machines with an asymmetrical traversing range of the primary rotary axes (for
example, from -7° to 180° or from -120° to 30°)
• Machines in the production environment (small-scale/large-scale production)
• Components that largely fill the available workspace and therefore restrict the
traversing range of the axes

As the tool moves away from the part in a local rewind movement and then approaches the part again after
the rewind movement in order to continue the machining, this movement is implemented with an overlap.
The overlap can be controlled with the following parameters:
Blending distance factor: Defines the value of the lateral pushing away from the component as a factor of
the machine tolerance.
Blending length factor: Defines the blending length as a factor of the tool diameter.

Relink
The original infeed movements within jobs are removed and connected again as specified by the NC
Optimizer. The optimized infeed movements are collision-free and are executed as linear movements on
the shortest possible path.
Collision avoidance during rewind - Virtual Machine configuration
Initial situation: Collision avoidance for component, fixture, stock model, machine table against machine
housing/frame during rewind movements.
By activating the options Check machine body and Rewind save axis in the Virtual Machine configuration,
collisions during rewind movements are avoided. This is done by an additional movement in the linear axis
within the rewind movement.
The axis in which the additional movement of the linear axis is to take place is to be selected as the
Rewind safe axis.
It is advisable to activate the functionality for machining oversized components on machines with at least
one linear axis and rotary axis in the machine table. This is also recommended for machines in which the
machine table can collide with the machine housing/frame when moving the rotary axis.
In order to carry out this optimization safely, it is necessary that the component is clamped on the real
machine identically to how it was collision-checked in the virtual machine.
Additional axes
: Click the icon to open the Additional axes definition dialog. Define a value for the preset position of the
fixed axis for machines with more than five axes. Depending on the machine kinematics, an angle value, a
linear value or both can be defined.
The Additional axes function depends on the kinematics defined in the machine model
and is available with an appropriate license for the VIRTUAL Machining Optimizer.
Please contact your OPEN MIND partner.
The following additional definition options are available in the dialog:
Additional axes definition
Fixed axes
The angle defined in the Virtual Machine configuration (Machine dialog page) for the respective axis is
used as the default angle.
Use preferred angle: Define the required angle. The NC Optimizer can change the defined angle to
achieve an inclination that is within the Machine limitation and at the same time collision-free. This is the
default setting when creating a new job.
optimization logic:
The defined angle is checked first. If this does not lead to a valid solution, the position of the previous job
is checked. If both positions do not lead to a valid solution, the NC Optimizer determines another valid
positioning of the rotary axis. This is iterated in increments between 180°, 90°, 45° and finally 1° steps.
Even if the NC Optimizer is deactivated, this logic is used to search for a kinematically
correct solution. This solution is not checked for collisions, but only for violation of the
axis limits.

-- 111 of 1632 --

Force: Define a value for the angle of the rotary axis. This is not optimized by the NC Optimizer and is only
checked when the NC Optimizer is active.
SERRATION
The fixed rotary axis is also optimized for machines with serration. Here the first solution
is chosen that is within the defined Hirth deviation tolerance. The Hirth deviation toler-
ance is defined in the Virtual Machine configuration (NC dialog page) under Common →
Formats. (Please note: The input field is hidden in the standard configuration).
Parallel axes
The position defined in the Virtual Machine configuration (Machine dialog page) for the respective axis is
used as the default value.
Use preferred position: Define a value for the position of the parallel axis. The NC Optimizer can change
the defined value to achieve a position that is within the Machine limitation and at the same time collision-
free. This is the default setting when creating a new job.
optimization logic:
Here, the defined value is checked first. If this does not lead to a valid solution, the position of the previous
job is checked. If both positions do not lead to a valid solution, the NC Optimizer determines another valid
positioning of the axis. An attempt is made to realize a minimum delta between the parallel axes.
Even if the NC Optimizer is deactivated, this logic is used to search for a kinematically
correct solution. This solution is not checked for collisions, but only for violation of the
axis limits.
Force: Define a value for the position of the parallel axis. This is not optimized and is only checked when
the NC Optimizer is active.

The positions or angles optimized by the NC Optimizer are displayed during the creation
of the NC file for the respective job and in the VIRTUAL Machining Center (postproces-
sor log). This also applies to optimizations for machines with serration.

Compound job
A compound jobs allows job lists to be structured clearly. You can combine any 2D, 3D or 5X jobs into a
compound job. For example, you can combine a machining section (roughing, finishing) into a compound
job.
To define a compound job:
1. Use the New → Compound job function on the browser’s shortcut menu or select the jobs to be
included in a compound job and use the Add to compound job function on the shortcut menu.
2. Specify a name and comment for the compound job.
You can also hold down the SHIFT key to move jobs to a compound job.
Linking job
A linking job contains other jobs that can be linked with each other in such a way that approach and retract
movements for the entire machining sequence and all linking movements between the individual jobs can
be optimized and monitored for collisions.
Advantages
• Shortened machining times.
• Option to perform complex machining tasks.
• Improved product flexibility.
Requirements
To combine multiple jobs into a linking job,
• for 2D/3D machining jobs, all sub-jobs must use the same tool,
• for turning jobs, all sub-jobs must use the same tool, the tool angles and tool orientation (Invert tool)
must be the same for all sub-jobs,
• for 3D/5X machining jobs, all sub-jobs must use the same tool.
For turning jobs, the following combinations of the Cutting side parameter are possible in the sub-jobs (see
Strategy dialog page):
Cutting side Outside machining Inside machining Plane Machining
Outside machining x - x
Inside machining - x x
Plane Machining x x x
CAM
113

-- 113 of 1632 --

Drill machining cannot be combined with a linking job.
Defining a linking job
Right-click and select the New → Linking job / New → Linking job turning function.
Add job to a linking job
Select the job(s) and then select the Add to linking job function on the shortcut menu or hold down the
SHIFT key to move the jobs to the previously created linking job.
The Linking job dialog
Linking jobs are defined on the following dialog pages: Tool, Parameters, Setup, Feature, Transformation,
General and NC.
Tool dialog page
All of the jobs combined into a linking job must contain the same tool. This also applies to 2D mode and 5X
mode.
Parameters dialog page
Linking mode
The following linking methods may be used:
2D: Linking of 2D, 3D, drill jobs and turning jobs that share the same frame orientation.
5X: Linking of 3D and 5-axis jobs. It is also possible to link the 2D cycles Pocket Milling and Rest
Machining in 5X mode.
Rapids
Specify the mode for the fast travel movements (rapids) of linked individual jobs.
Skip first and last: Skip the first infeed movement and last retract movement of the individual sub-jobs.
Keep all rapids: Keep all infeed and retract movements of sub-jobs within the linking job.
Conditions
Use min. distance G0: The movements between the jobs are executed as a direct link between pairs of
contour points in G1. Min.
G0 distance: Distance between two machining areas that can be traversed – without tool contact – close to
the surface with machining feedrate (G1).
Planar/ Radial: Specify how the toolpaths of the linked sub-jobs are linked. (1) Planar, (2) Radial.

Retract mode
The retract mode defines the Z level where the system executes horizontal infeed movements. The mode
set is valid for all machining directions (incl. approach, retract and return movement macros) and for the
profiles machined with them. Exception: Machining in zigzag mode without return macro.
Clearance distance (1): all retract and infeed movements are executed via the clearance distance. Starting
and end positions of an infeed movement in rapid are displaced in Z direction in order to guarantee a
collision-free linear infeed movement. The clearance distance is added to these positions.
Clearance plane (2): all retract and infeed movements are executed via the clearance plane.

NC eventUse NC events to clearly structure the program flow and influence programming by entering commands,
independent of job lists and jobs.
To create an NC event:
1. Use the New → NC event function on the browser's shortcut menu.
2. Define the Event type and enter the respective command under Event command.
CAM
117

-- 117 of 1632 --

NC events can be freely moved in the job browser. To do this, select the NC event with the left mouse
button and move it to the required position while holding down the mouse button. The content of the NC
Event always remains intact. Control-specific functions and commands are forwarded to the postprocessor
directly by the NC Event.
NC events cannot be simulated or checked for possible collisions. Postprocessing is
only possible in Package mode.
Free NC text is now also supported by VIRTUAL Machining. Only input in VNC format is
permitted. Otherwise, an error message is generated in the VIRTUAL Machining Center.
It is then no longer possible to release the NC program.
VIRTUAL Machining
In the case of NC events, the workplane, RTCP, spindle, and coolant are always reset before the NC
event. After the NC event, a new approach movement is generated. This includes switching on the spindle
and coolant. This is independent of whether the next job after the NC event has the same inclination as the
previous one. This is necessary to ensure safe and clear use of the NC event.
OPEN MIND RECOMMENDATION
OPEN MIND recommends using the NC-Text job option to insert simple M commands
(for example, activation of the chip conveyor) or comments into the NC program. We al-
so recommend using the correct VNC variables for commands (including M commands)
that result in a movement or changed behavior (for example, activation of RTCP) of the
CNC machine.
Associative job copy
Copy of a job in which all parameters correspond to the parameters of the original job. A job copy is
associatively linked with the original job. If a parameter is changed in the original job, then this parameter
will also change in the associative job copy. Parameters cannot be edited. Exception: transformations and
contours.
To create an associative job copy:
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, select the job in the job list, right-click and
2. choose the Associative job copy function on the shortcut menu.
To unlink the copied job and original job:
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, select the copied job, right-click and
2. choose the Unlink associative copy function on the shortcut menu.
All changes to the original job are summarized on the Overview dialog page.
The associative job copy corresponds to the Copy option when using a mirror within a job definition
(Transformation dialog page). If you define a mirror on job list level and have enabled the Copy option, a
mirrored associative copy of the original job is created from all jobs in the job list with the parameters and
settings of the original job.
To deactivate the associative link between the original job and the associative job copy for individual
parameters, right-click the relevant parameter and select Unlink.

Changes to this parameter in the original job no longer affect the associative job copy. Conversely, the
parameter can now be edited directly in the job copy without affecting the original job. The associativity
between both jobs is restored using the Link function.
If you recalculate a job for which an associative job copy exists, you can also recalculate the job copy.

Job Optimization
Optimization of manually created jobs as well as macro jobs with the aim of reducing the
number of tool changes and shortening machine running times.
Optimization of manually created jobs
To optimize manually created jobs, use the Optimization (only compound jobs) function on the job list’s
shortcut menu.
Compound jobs
Group manually created jobs of a job list into compound jobs.
Grouping is also available for macro jobs.
The No optimization option is enabled by default for manually created jobs. The job steps in the job list are
grouped into compound jobs either by tool or by machining step. Only directly consecutive jobs for which
the tool or the job type remains the same are combined. There is no change in the job sequence.
Example – Group by tool:
No compound jobs: No compound jobs are created.
Group by tool: Jobs with the same tool are combined in a compound job. The name of the generated
compound job is composed as follows: [Tool number / Tool diameter / Tool name].
Group by process step: Job steps of the same job type (same job name) are combined in a compound job.
The name of the generated compound job is composed as follows: [Cycle name].
Optimization of macro jobs
To optimize macro jobs, use the Optimization (only compound jobs) function on the job list’s shortcut
menu.
Optimization
Optimize macro jobs. Manually created jobs are not optimized.
CAM
120

-- 120 of 1632 --

No optimization: No jobs are optimized. The sequence of all job steps remains the same.
Optimization with job grouping: Macro jobs are sorted taking into account the tool sequence within macros.
Jobs with different features but the same tool and the same job parameters are combined into one job
step.
Optimization without job grouping: Macro jobs are sorted taking into account the tool sequence within
macros. Identical job steps with the same tool are not combined into one job step. The job steps are sorted
in the order of the tool calls in macros.
Manually created jobs, which are located between macro jobs, remain at their positions in the job list.
Tool Sorting
Optimize macro jobs. Manually created jobs are not optimized. Requirement: The option Optimization →
Optimization with job grouping or Optimization → Optimization without job grouping is enabled.
No sorting: No change in the sequence of tool calls.
With ascending and descending sorting, the logical order of the tools within the macro
has top priority, which means that sorting may not always be maintained correctly or the
same tool may be changed twice.
Sort by ascending diameter: Taking into account the macro order, the tools used are sorted in ascending
order by diameter. Example: In a component with holes D6, D8, D9 and M10, the holes D6 and D8 are
drilled first, then the core hole for M10 with D8.5 and finally the hole D9. The order within a macro is not
changed.
Sort by descending diameter: Taking into account the order within a macro, the tools used are sorted in
descending order by diameter.
Example: In a component with holes D6, D8, D9 and M10, first the hole for D9 is created, then the core
hole M10 with D8.5 and finally the holes D8 and D6. The order within a macro is not changed.
Multi axis indexing
Prerequisites for multi axis indexing:
• A machine with C axis and/or swiveling milling head (5X machining).
• A drawing in the form of a 3D model.
Programming always takes place in the G17 workplane:
• Infeed in (negative) Z direction; Z axis is perpendicular to the machining side
• Machining in the XY direction.
Hence in multi-axis machining, you first have to define the coordinate system and the frame for each
machining side. See the information in section NC system and frames (page 43).

The job sequence is basically arbitrary. If a tool change optimization is required, the definition should be
made one page at a time (shorter calculation time).
To do this, open the machining cycle, set the required frame in the Setup input dialog and define the job's
machining parameters.
At any given time, only the current frame is visible in the CAD drawing. Only those contours that lie on the
frame's XY plane can be selected.

Tool change optimization
Before generating the toolpaths, it is possible to optimize tool changes by sorting individual jobs according
to different criteria.
CAM
122

-- 122 of 1632 --

Macro job lists for holes must be expanded into individual jobs prior to tool change optimization. Use the
Explode function on the shortcut menu for this.
It is possible to sort by different criteria. Use the function you require from the joblist’s shortcut menu.
Sort by tool: Starting with the first tool in the expanded joblist (drilling cycles expanded into individual
drillings), the jobs are sorted by tool number in ascending order, regardless of the frame in the job. The job
sequence can also be sorted again manually.
Sort by frame: The jobs are sorted by frame number. The job and tool sequence already defined for each
frame is retained.
Global editing
Edit job definition parameters for multiple jobs at the same time.
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, select the Jobs tab, select all jobs, for which common parameters
should be determined.
2. To edit, click the icon or right-click and select Edit.
3. The Global editing input window opens. Here, you can specify definitions in the following areas for
several jobs.
Edit a parameter by double-clicking the corresponding line. If you move the mouse over a parameter in the
column on the left, the jobs that use this parameter are shown as a tooltip.

Transformations
A transformation is a relative movement within a reference coordinate system. The starting point is a start
reference (start coordinate system) and the end point is a target reference (target coordinate system). The
movement can comprise a linear and/or rotating movement.
Y
Z
Z Z
X
Y
Y
X
X
In
hyperMILL, transformation refers to the duplication and positioning of toolpaths for the production of
identical and/or similar components.
hyperMILL supports mirroring, linear patterns, circular patterns and
general patterns.
Advantages
• Significantly shorter programming times for identical and/or similar geometries
• Associativity of the transformation when changes are made to the geometry
• Flexibility as a result of partial deactivation of the direct connection between the base element and
the transformed element
• No limitations for 2D, 3D and 5X machining
Transformations add a transformation rule to the toolpath calculated.
hyperMILL displays the resulting
jobs / job copies in the form of graphical feedback. When mirroring toolpaths using the Mirror mode →
Mirror path function of the Transformation dialog page, only the calculated toolpath is mirrored, not the
model or stock.
The NC is output as if a new frame was used for the resulting job. As a result, positioning movements can
sometimes occur on 5-axis machines when using rotation axes.
It is possible to use NC control functions (e.g., zero point moves, subprograms, etc.).
However, they require a special adjustment to the postprocessor. Please contact your
OPEN MIND partner.
CAM
129

-- 129 of 1632 --

Examples
1. Circular pattern in the plane with 3D postprocessor (no index postprocessor)
The postprocessor maps the frame system of all copies on the NCS and creates link rapids on
the clearance plane of the jobs.
2. Circular pattern in the plane with 5-axis postprocessor
Depending on the settings, the postprocessor outputs a different table/head orientation for each
position, if required. Additional movements occur between all copies, which correspond to a safe
positioning logic of the machine.
Linking movements created by the postprocessor are not collision-checked
against the 3D model. You therefore need to ensure that the clearance plane is
above all collision-relevant elements.
3. Using the frame ID for postprocessors
If your postprocessor requires you to define a frame ID or a frame comment, your postprocessor
is incompatible with toolpaths that were created using the
hyperMILL Transformation function.
For this reason, please only use toolpaths without transformations for these postprocessors.
4. Structuring the NC output
For recurring toolpaths that were created using transformations, a simplified NC output is not
generally provided (for example, as a subprogram or part of the program that repeats).
If you wish to have a suitable simplified NC output, contact your OPEN MIND dealer. Please also
bear in mind that a fee may be required for postprocessor enhancements.
For toolpaths generated by a transformation, only one safety check with a tolerance of 0.05 mm
will be carried out. Collisions with a sufficiently small overlap may not be recognized under certain
circumstances. Please check the geometric conditions and parameters of the transformation
carefully before machining. This constraint does not hold for the mirror.
Define and apply transformations
Define transformations and apply them in a job.
Define
To define a transformation, switch to the Frames tab in the
hyperMILL browser and select the desired
transformation from the shortcut menu in the Transformation area or create a new transformation.
Apply it to a job
In order to apply a transformation in a job, change to the Transformation dialog page and select the Active
checkbox.
Now select the type of transformation under Selection and then click the icon to select a transformation
or click the icon to create a new transformation.
For toolpaths generated by a transformation, no precise safety check will be carried out.
Collisions with a sufficiently small overlap may not be recognized under certain circum-
stances. Please check the geometric conditions and parameters of the transformation
carefully before machining.

Linear pattern
You can use a linear pattern in a job, compound job or linking job.
Define
1. Define the Transformation name and a Comment in the Transformations dialog.
2. Use X direction / Y direction to define the direction of the pattern.
Structure: If the Fixed distance option is selected, the Number of elements defined and the Dis-
tance specified between each element are taken into account when creating the transformation. If
the Fit elements option is selected, the Number of elements defined is fitted to the Length of the
entire pattern.
Apply it to a job
To apply a linear pattern to the job:
1. Navigate to the Transformation dialog page, enable the Active checkbox and select the required
linear pattern under Selection.
2. Under Start reference, specify the start coordinate system to be used as a basis for the relative
movement of the transformation. Utilize the Use job frame option to use the active job frame.
Alternatively, select a frame or origin.
Target reference: The target coordinate system to be used as a basis for the relative movement
of the transformation. Use the Use start reference option to utilize the start reference system.

Mirror
This special type of transformation mirrors the base geometry. A prerequisite for this is the symmetry of the
part used.
HyperMILL calculates new toolpaths on the basis of the mirrored geometry.
The Mirror mode → Mirror path option in the job definition, Transformation dialog page is
used to prevent the geometry from being mirrored.
Advantages: Improved performance, easy to use.
Limitations: Climb milling becomes Conventional milling and vice versa, no collision
check is performed, not available for compound job or job list, but only for an individual
job.
You can use a mirror in a job, compound job or job list.
Advantages
• Full associativity between the base geometry and the mirrored element (job, compound job or job
list)
• No limitations for 2D, 3D and 5X machining
• Flexibility as a result of partial deactivation of the direct link between the base element and the
mirrored element
• Retention of technology parameters (such as auto climb, automatic macros or optimized linking
movements) in the mirror.
• Patterns can be combined.
The mirroring of turning jobs is not possible due to a risk of collision. This also applies to
the Turning drilling mode in drilling cycles.
Climb milling/Conventional milling
When mirroring curve machinings in the 2D Contour Milling, 3D Free Path Milling and 5X Contouring
cycles, a distinction is drawn between whether machining takes place to the side of the contour (options:
Left/ Right) or on the contour (option: On contour) .
(1) When machining takes place on the contour, the curve is mirrored, including the start point, to guaran-
tee geometrically symmetric material removal.
(2) When machining takes place at the side of the contour, the direction of the contour in the mirroring is
inverted to also guarantee equal climb to the contour in the mirrored machining.

How to apply a mirror:

2. Enable the Copy option to create a mirror of the original (job, compound job or job list). In the
hyperMILL browser, a mirrored copy of the original element is created and associatively linked
with the original. All parameters are greyed out in the mirrored jobs and cannot be edited directly.
As a result of the direct link (associativity) between the original job and the mirrored copy, all
changes to the original job are also taken into account in the copy during the recalculation.
In mirrored machining jobs, you can remove the link between all parameters to the origi-
nal job and adjust them individually! Right-click the respective location in the greyed-out
dialog and select Unlink. The parameter can now be edited directly in the job copy. The
associativity between both jobs is restored using the Link function.

Transformation Pattern Recognition
Use the Transformation Pattern Recognition function to recognize equal subareas of the CAD model and
transform toolpaths, which have already been generated for a subarea, to the recognized equal subareas
of the CAD model. To use the function, proceed as follows:
1. Open the dialog via the context menu of the Feature browser Feature lists → Transformation
Pattern Recognition.
2. In the dialog, select the frame under Frame and the surfaces of the previously edited geometry
under Selection → Surfaces. The Sorting → Shortest distance function searches for the same
geometries at the shortest distance from the selected geometry, taking the current frame view into
account. If the Grouping function is also activated, the same geometries found are grouped within
the selected frame and the groups are sorted according to the shortest distance.

3. As a result of the calculation, a new transformation is created in the Frames browser under Trans-
formations. It contains a correct frame for each geometry found. The frames are automatically
used for machining when the transformation is used.
4. For further processing, activate the Transformation function in the job definition and select the
newly created transformation under Selection → General pattern.
Mirrors and stock models
Stock models which are to be reflected, must be in *. format. To mirror a job list that uses a stock model:
1. On the Mirror dialog page in the joblist, select the mirror plane and enable the Copy option to
create a (mirrored) copy of the joblist that you have already defined.
2. On the Models dialog page in the mirrored job list, define the stock model that you want to use for
the mirror. The resulting stock model of the original job list can also be used for this purpose.
3. Assign this stock model to the first job contained in the job list and enable the Generate resulting
stock option.
4. Check the job status of the jobs contained in the job list and calculate the mirrored job list.
Resulting stock
Resulting stock is also mirrored during mirroring ( Job list → Mirror) if the Manufacturing parameters →
Copy function is activated.
Mirror stock chain
A stock chain is also mirrored during mirroring ( Job list → Mirror) if the Manufacturing parameters → Copy
function is activated.
