Collision check preparations
Specify a milling area or turning area to define the collision-checked part of the CAD model.
Define a collision-checked clamping area to fix the workpiece during machining.
General information
The Milling area or Turning area defines the area of the CAD model to be machined that is checked for
collisions at the same time. The Fixture area is also checked for collisions; this includes those areas of the
CAD model that are used to fix the part during machining.
hyperMILL automatically generates a polyhedron model (3DF format) at a suitably high surface resolution
(accuracy) for the Milling area, Turning area or Clamping area. For this purpose, the CAD model is
subdivided into separate machining areas as required by the collision-checking function.
All subareas of the model not inside the milling area, turning area or clamping area are not collision-
checked. Inside the milling area/turning area, you can exclude areas from machining (with the help of stop
surfaces, for example).
The machining area within the milling area is defined
• by defining a boundary (possible for all 3D and 5X cycles) or
• by defining milling surfaces (possible for the following cycles: 3D / 5X Profile Finishing, 3D / 5X Z
Level Finishing, 3D Z Level Shape Finishing and 3D / 5X Rest Machining).
Machining safety
To machine safely with
hyperMILL, please observe the following instructions.
Traversing movements on the clearance plane are not collision-checked.
This applies to all machining processes and cycle calculations as well as to simulation in
simulations that are not NC code-based. Therefore the clearance plane must be placed
at a sufficient distance above the surface of the component.
OPEN MIND recommends the use of an NC code-based simulation such as the VIRTU-
AL Machining Center or an external simulation program to ensure the greatest possible
degree of safety and collision protection.
Define milling area
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, double-click to open the job list.
2. On the Part data dialog page, select the Defined option and select a milling area.
3. Define a new milling area or modify a milling area.
Alternatively, open the dialog via the job definition on the Setup dialog page or using the New milling area
shortcut menu in the
hyperMILL browser on the Models dialog page.
The Milling area dialog
The dialog consists of the Definition and Milling area dialog pages.
On the Definition dialog page, define the elements that belong to the milling area. On the Milling area
dialog page, define the name and storage location for the milling area.
File: Click the Path button to select a 3DF or STL file.

Collision checking with the
hyperMILL Converter
A collision check can either be performed by defining milling areas in the
hyperMILL browser or using the
hyperMILL Converter (polyhedron model). Model areas located on disabled layers are not converted.
You have to create at least one 3DF file (polyhedron model) for each CAD model. Areas with a different
accuracy and different stock allowances can be entered in a 3DF file.
Several 3DF files are required for CAD models that exceed the travel range of the machine and therefore
need to be moved and reclamped during machining.
Recommendation: Always convert as many surfaces and solids as possible in one process. The conver-
sion of individual areas with a higher resolution should always include adjacent surfaces.
All 3DF files belonging to a model become invalid if the model changes position in the
coordinate system, is turned or scaled.
Start the converter via the CAM → Converter menu.
The
hyperMILL Converter dialog
The
hyperMILL Converter dialog consists of the Setup and Options dialog pages.
Setup dialog page
3DF file: Select the storage location for the 3DF file. Set the default storage location in the hyperMILL
settings dialog. The model name with the *.3df file extension is used as the file name.
Resolution
Mathematical resolution: Specify the resolution of edge curve circle segments in G1 lengths using the
maximum chordal height. Set the surface resolution to be somewhat finer than the dimensional accuracy
required in production.
Recommendation: roughing 0.5 to 0.1 mm, finishing 0.05 to 0.01 mm, HSC machining 0.005 to 0.001 mm.
Max. facet length: Controls the maximum facet length within the 3DF model. Can be defined for each
group in group definitions.
CAM
143

-- 143 of 1632 --

If a sufficiently precise definition cannot be achieved using the Mathematical resolution function (for
example, with surfaces that are only slightly curved), a limit can be set.
Selection options
All solids, All surfaces, All: Select one of these options if no user-specific selection for conversion is to be
used and the selected areas are all to be converted with the same mathematical resolution.
User-defined
Surfaces: Select solids or surfaces to be converted. The same mathematical resolution applies to all
selected surfaces/solids.
Groups
Group definition: Select this option if you want to convert areas with different mathematical resolutions
and/or different stock allowances, in order, for example, to define different collision and protected areas.
A coarse resolution is sufficient for roughing areas. A finer resolution should be defined for different fine
machining processes.
The group definition is relevant for: Profile Finishing, Equidistant Finishing, Iso Machining, Free Path
Milling.
Groups dialog page
Groups
A 3DF file can contain up to five groups of surfaces and/or solids with different mathematical resolutions
and different stock allowances. A surface can only be allocated to one Surface Group.
Current selection
Group name: Name of the surface(s).
Surfaces: Select the solids or surfaces to be converted.
Mathematical resolution: Surface resolution of the model.
Allowance: Remaining material on the workpiece. If more than five groups are required to machine a
model, create the respective number of 3DF files with different names. You assign the 3DF files in the job
definition.
Max. facet length: Maximum facet length of the surfaces within a group.
Options dialog page
Mode of conversion

New 3DF file: The selected objects will be converted at the set mathematical resolution and a new 3DF file
will be created.
Add to existing 3DF file: The selected objects will be converted at the set mathematical resolution and
added to the existing 3DF file. In this way, several areas with different mathematical resolutions can be
combined into one 3DF file and later modifications to the model can be included.
Does not apply to group definitions.
Save existing 3DF file
Yes: When adding surfaces, the existing 3DF file that the current conversion process is going to expand
can be backed up by saving it under a different name.
Save as: Select the path and file name for saving the existing 3DF file.
No: An existing 3DF file is saved under an existing path and file name with the addition of the new
surfaces/solids to be converted.

Calculate and analyze toolpaths
Prerequisites, information and options for calculating toolpaths.
Delete, read, update and analyze toolpaths.
Requirements
1. Correct job sequence: The sequence of jobs in the job list matches the machining order.
2. Correct job definition: Before calculating a toolpath check jobs that have an error or warning
notification. Use the Messages function on the shortcut menu for this. If these are not manually
checked, all messages will be displayed prior to the toolpath calculation.
3. For 3D and 5-axis machining, a milling area must be present in order to calculate a toolpath.
Jobs whose machining ended with an error should only be post processed after an extensive check.
General settings
The system of units that has been set is valid for the toolpath calculation. Changes to the measurement
system are not permitted after the jobs, tools and frames have been defined. Relevant settings for calculat-
ing toolpaths are specified in the
hyperMILL Settings dialog, on the Calculation tab.
Job list-specific settings
The following are defined on a job-specific basis:
• Name and path of toolpaths
• NCS (program zero)
• Original stock (if necessary) and model
• Postprocessor-specific settings
The NCS must be identical for all jobs within a job list. If the NCS is moved, previously
calculated jobs become invalid.
Job-specific settings
The frame is set on a job-specific basis.
The display colors and sizes for the toolpath and collision output can also be set on a job-specific basis.
Calculate toolpaths
Either directly in the job definition (for an individual job) or in the
hyperMILL browser (for an individual job,
multiple jobs or all the jobs in a job list).
In the job definition
Calculate: The main purpose of this method of creating a toolpath is to enable a quick check of the
work-through of an individual job.
In the
hyperMILL browser
Select the required jobs or job list and then select the Calculate function from the shortcut menu.
When calculating/updating one or more linking jobs, the system displays a message asking whether
you want to recalculate all sub-jobs. If you choose No, only the linking job, and not its sub-jobs, are
recalculated.
CAM
146

-- 146 of 1632 --

Prior to the calculation, the messages stored for the jobs or joblists to be calculated are displayed.
Ignore: Ignore the messages and calculate the job.
Ignore all: Ignore all messages and calculate all jobs.
Cancel: Cancel the calculation.
Edit: Open the dialog (Job/Joblist) and edit the settings.
During the calculation, the message window displays information on the status of the calculation. The
calculation can be controlled as follows:
Cancel the toolpath calculation.
Stop the toolpath calculation.
Continue the toolpath calculation.
For some machining cycles, temporary toolpaths are displayed initially that correspond to the calculation
sequence. Once the calculation has finished, the calculated toolpaths will be displayed if you have selec-
ted the Display toolpaths option in the
hyperMILL settings dialog.
If the system identifies collisions while calculating the toolpaths, they are also displayed graphically.
Information on the calculation process is displayed in the window that appears at the same time. In the
hyper MILL settings dialog, enable the required option under Message mode on the Application dialog
page. In addition, various messages can be viewed in the report file. The report file (*.rep) is stored by
default in the Global Working Space.
If the name of a job list or a job comment is changed after the toolpaths have been
calculated, it is not necessary to subsequently recalculate the toolpaths of the job list.
hyperMILL automatically adapts the toolpaths accordingly.

Delete the toolpaths of one or several jobs via Toolpaths → Delete on the shortcut menu.

Read toolpaths and display in the CAD system.

menu.
2. Reading of any toolpaths (for example, for analysis purposes) via the CAM → Read toolpath
menu. Open the dialog from the shortcut menu of a job list or job.

clipped areas.

Update calculated toolpaths
Changes to the feedrate, spindle RPM or comment do not require a recalculation of the job for the
following cycles.
- all 3D cycles except Form Pocket
- all 5X cavity cycles except Z-level roughing and cutting edge
- all 5X surface cycles
- 5X Blade Top Milling
- 5X MB Point Milling
To change the spindle RPM or feedrate of the tool, choose one of the following options:
1. Change the value for this job only directly on the Tool tab of the job definition. To do so, select the
Unlink command from the Spindle RPM / Feedrate shortcut menu in the Cutting profile section.
Enter the value directly into the dialog.
2. Change the value for the tool in the Technology tab of the tool definition. Click the icon to open
the Edit tool dialog and enter the required changes on the Technology tab.
Then update the toolpath file in the
hyperMILL browser using the Update shortcut menu.
Information on calculated toolpaths
Information is available for the following via a quickinfo (tooltip): frame, job ID, job name, comment, job
type, linked job, tool ID and tool name.
Configure the information displayed on menu File → Options → Tooltip content konfigurieren. To do this,
move the elements from the Available TAGs area to the Tooltip content area.
The Toolpath Edit cycle
Use the Toolpath Edit cycle to delete certain sections in calculated toolpaths using a boundary and link the
remaining parts of the toolpath together or split a toolpath on the basis of the tool life in order to exchange
the tool or the inserts.
A collision check is available for the following tool types: ball mill, end mill, bullnose end mill. A warning
message appears if machining is carried out with a different tool. The job to be edited and the cycle
Toolpath Edit represent a jointly managed unit. Changes in the original job are reproducible with the same
settings in the Toolpath Edit cycle.
Start the Edit toolpath cycle via the shortcut menu of the job to be edited (New → Edit toolpath).

Parameters dialog page
Mode
Edit job: Delete certain sections in calculated toolpaths using a boundary and link the remaining parts of
the toolpath together. All linking paths and approach and retract macros are checked for collisions.
The Edit job function is available for the following cycles:
• 3D Milling / 3D Advanced Milling: All cycles except for 3D Arbitrary Stock Roughing and 3D Form
Pocket.
• 5X Cavity Milling: All cycles except for 3D Z Level Roughing and 3D Cutting Edge Machining.
Split job: Split a toolpath on the basis of the tool life in order to exchange the tool or the inserts. The
toolpath is split either based on time or based on length.
The Split job function is available for the following cycles:
• 3D Milling: 3D Arbitrary Stock Roughing, 3D Optimized Roughing, 3D Profile Finishing, 3D Z Level
Finishing, 3D Z Level Shape Finishing, 3D Iso Machining, 3D Plane Machining.
• 3D Advanced Milling: 3D Complete Finishing, 3D Equidistant Finishing, 3D Automatic Rest Machin-
ing, 3D Rework Machining.
• 5X Cavity Milling: 5X Optimized Rest Roughing, 5X Z Level Finishing, 5X Profile Finishing, 5X
Equidistant Finishing, 5X Rest Machining, 5X Rework Machining, 5X Z level Roughing.
Conditions
Use min. dist. G0: Unnecessary rapid link movements are avoided. If they fall below the specified value,
toolpaths at the defined boundary are linked with the machining feedrate. This enhances process safety
and reduces machine running time.
Connect smooth: This option smoothly connects toolpaths that run close to one another.
(1) Function not enabled, (2) Function enabled.
For information on the retract mode and clearance, see sections Retract mode (page 797) and Clear-
ance (page 440).

Simulate machining
Machining can be simulated as follows.
1. Using the internal simulation. See the information in section Internal simulation (page 155).
2. With the Simulation Center.
3. Using the
hyperVIEW program. See the information in section Simulation in
hyperVIEW (page
156).
4. With the VIRTUAL Machining Center. See the information in the VIRTUAL Machining Center
documentation.
5. Using an external simulation program (for example, VERICUT). See the information in section
External simulation (page 187).
OPEN MIND recommends the use of an NC code-based simulation such as the VIRTU-
AL Machining Center or an external simulation program to ensure the greatest possible
degree of safety and collision protection.
To run an NC code-based simulation, an appropriate VIRTUAL Machining Center li-
cense is required. Please contact your OPEN MIND partner.
The internal simulation, the SIMULATION Center, and the simulation with
hyperVIEW
are not based on an NC file.

Machining safety
To machine safely with
hyperMILL, please observe the following instructions.
Traversing movements on the clearance plane are not collision-checked.
This applies to all machining processes and cycle calculations as well as to simulation in
simulations that are not NC code-based. Therefore the clearance plane must be placed
at a sufficient distance above the surface of the component.
Machining planner
Start the VIRTUAL Machining Center in Machining planner mode and equip a turret for turning jobs with
graphical support.
Internal simulation
The internal simulation is based on the calculated toolpaths. It is not an NC code-based
simulation.
To start the internal simulation, select the required job list or required job and select the Internal simulation
option from the shortcut menu.
Job status: This indicates the job that is currently being simulated.
Frame: Shows the frame of the simulated job.
Tool/Origin: Shows the tool and origin of the simulated job.
Speed: Set the simulation speed using 50 steps.
Tool: Configure the tool display.
Display the tool holder (enabled by default).
Display a freely defined tool geometry (enabled by default).
Generate an image of the tool at the current position. To delete the image, use the
shortcut menu.
Start the toolpath viewer. The toolpath viewer displays the complete toolpath in G0/G1
steps. Each entry corresponds to one toolpath step. Z levels and macro movements are
displayed separately. This means that you can locate and analyze the individual tool
movements very accurately. To address a position of the tool directly, double-click the
respective row.

SIMULATION Center
Introduction
Use the new SIMULATION Center simulation solution to check machining operations quickly and effective-
ly for possible collisions. After the toolpath calculation, start the simulation as follows: Right-click and then
select Simulation Center on the shortcut menu of the job or job list.
The simulation takes into account the machine defined in the Machine properties → General → Postproces-
sor dialog and is based on the calculation of the toolpaths. This is not an NC code-based simulation.
Linking movements between individual jobs are not simulated.
The VIRTUAL Machining Center software with simulation and analysis options for the NC code after the
postprocessor run is the right solution to choose if a virtual representation of the actual processes is to be
safely evaluated, controlled and optimized.
To start the SIMULATION Center it is no longer necessary to select a machine (postprocessor) in the
job list. If no machine (postprocessor) or a postprocessor without a machine model is selected, the
SIMULATION Center can also be started without a model selected in the job list.
This software documentation provides information on how to use the SIMULATION Center software.

The application is adapted to the use of wide screen formats and for working with multiple screens. You
can also place variable areas outside of the program window, that is, you can move them to another
screen. When you exit a document the last window positions are saved.

Progress indicator: Displays the progress for computing-intensive processes, 6 	and information is provi-
ded on the current action within the process (if possible).

Operating modes
Use the main navigation toolbar to switch between the various operating modes: Project administration,
Program run (simulation), Machine configuration, VIRTUAL Machining Center configuration and Analysis.
Project administration operating mode
For extensive programs, load one of several available main programs. If the project con-
tains only one main program, this is loaded automatically.

control). View the axis limits of the machine.

tool reference point and coordinate systems of the machine used.

points and conditions for breakpoints, display breakpoints as a list and display breakpoint
coordinates.

The speed control refers to a path unit. Minimum = 0.01 mm, Maximum = 100 mm. If necessary, interpo-
lation is carried out between the individual blocks to provide a tool movement that is as uniform and
consistent as possible. If the increment is not smooth enough, blocks may also be omitted. The increment
has no influence on the collision check and material removal simulation.
Double-click one of the two speed controllers to switch the program run to whole blocks, independent of
the speed, (the speed controllers are then greyed out). This always applies both to G0 and G1 movements
as well as to moving forwards and backwards one step at a time. Double-click one of the two speed
controllers again to restore the original behavior.

Collision check options
Use the following options to control the collision check.
The tolerance values/limit values for the still permissible contact of the tool with the
component/stock must be in reasonable proportion to the size of the tool used. OPEN
MIND recommends defining these values no larger than half the tool diameter.
Check tool against model: Checks the tool against the model.
Check holder/shaft/core against model: Holder, shank and tool core are checked against the model.
Always check G0: The rapid traverse check is activated by default. If the Check tool against model function
is deactivated, the check for all fast travel movements can also be optionally switched off. This can make it
easier to release an NC file in certain situations (for example, when machining non-modelled areas).
Check stock: Checks tool and holder against the stock.
Remove detached stock: Only available if Check stock is enabled. If this function is activated, a check is
performed during the collision check and the simulation to see whether there is a stock area that has no
contact with the defined milling area (model). If this is the case, the stock is automatically removed during
the simulation and the collision check.
Consider core diameter for milling tools: The tool tip is checked for collisions with the stock, taking the core
diameter into account.
Limits for component contact
Use G0 tip limit / G1 tip limit to set the limit value for the still permitted contact of the tool tip with the model
in G0 and G1 movements. If a larger value is detected during the test, a message is generated.
Part allowance
Use part allowance: Activate if a part allowance should be defined for the collision check. The part
allowance is then defined either using the settings in the job (if the Use job settings option has been
activated) or it can be entered directly under Allowance. The tool shape is offset in all directions by the
entered value. If -0.01 is entered, a ball mill D10 becomes a ball mill D9.98 during the collision check.
Use job settings: Enabled by default. The values defined in the job for allowance, allowance XY and
allowance Z are used for the collision check.
CAM
170

-- 170 of 1632 --

A check is also performed to see whether a negative allowance or the Chamfer height
parameter is defined for theChamfer Milling on 3D Model cycle. As a component viola-
tion is desired here, no collision message is output in these cases.
If the Use job settings option has not been activated, the value for the Allowance can be entered directly.
The value that is entered is offset on the shank diameter. If -0.01 is entered, the diameter of the shank is
reduced by 0.02 (shank radius -0.01).
Only tip: The allowance is only applied to the tool tip (to be activated if, for example, only a small area at
the bottom of a cavity is to be machined with a negative allowance).
Whole tool: The stock allowance is applied to the entire tool (including thickened shank and holder) (to
be activated if, for example, a complete steep area is to be machined from top to bottom with a negative
allowance).
Stock contact
allow thin shank contact: Activate to use a tool where the shank and cutting edge have been defined
with the same diameter. The tool shank may touch the stock. No collision message is output. Use with
imprecisely defined tool geometry.
derive from stock model resolution: Activate to use a tool where the shank and cutting edge have been
defined with the same diameter. Situations in which there is a distance of 0 between the stock and shank
are not regarded as a collision. The tolerance required for the collision check is automatically derived from
the stock tolerance if the function is activated.
If the function is not activated, the value for the tolerance can be entered directly. The value that is entered
is offset on the shank diameter. If -0.01 is entered, the diameter of the shank is reduced by 0.02 (shank
radius -0.01).
Part contact
allow thin shank contact: Activate to use a tool where the shank and cutting edge have been defined with
the same diameter. The tool shank may touch the component. No collision message is output. Use with
imprecisely defined tool geometry.
derive from job settings: Activate to use a tool where the shank and cutting edge have been defined with
the same diameter. Situations in which there is a distance of 0 between the component and shank are
not regarded as a collision. The tolerance required for the collision check is automatically derived from the
calculation tolerance in the
hyperMILL job if the function is activated.
If the function is not activated, the value for the tolerance can be entered directly. The value that is entered
is offset on the shank diameter. If -0.01 is entered, the diameter of the shank is reduced by 0.02 (shank
radius -0.01).
Tool safety distance to fixture
Safety distance to be maintained between the tool and the fixture (exception: touch probe).
Use hyperMILL settings: Use the settings from
hyperMILL.
Further collision check options
Resolution: Set the accuracy for the collision check.
Stop on first collision: During the collision check, the program stops at the first collision found.
Save As Default: The settings for the collision check are saved across machines and simulations (for the
VIRTUAL Machining Center, the SIMULATION Center and the toolpath preview). Saving is user-specific. It
is still possible to temporarily change settings by confirming with OK.

Please contact your OPEN MIND support team if you would like to save company-wide
standards.

Show line numbers for VNC data: Displays the line numbers in the VNC program file/NC file. Both
numbers correlate, however, they are not identical with the line numbers of the NC program that is output.
Simulation
Minimum feedrate for rapid movements: G1 movements with a higher feedrate (than the defined value)
are handled as rapid tool movements. Here, the feedrate is replaced by the default feedrate for G0
movements. The toolpath is displayed in red in the program run and the display also corresponds to G0
movements.
Number of replay steps: Specify the number of steps that the machine travels in order to approach a
toolpath point again that was defined using the Pick new position function.
Simulation tolerance: Accuracy of the simulation for the collision check.
Simulate machine cycles as a single operation: Machine cycles such as Simple Drilling or Circular Pocket
can be simulated separately as a single operation.
Appearance
Toolpaths
Show at simulation start: Activates the loading of the toolpaths at the start of the VIRTUAL Machining
Center / SIMULATION Center, in order to show them directly. Activating this option will cause a longer
starting time for the VIRTUAL Machining Center / SIMULATION Center. The setting of this option is
automatically used as default.
The toolpaths can be shown after the start of the VIRTUAL Machining Center / SIMULATION Center at
any time by using the Show toolpaths button on the Simulation dialog page. Showing the toolpaths for the
first time results in a loading process.
The status of the toolpath display is also taken into account during a program change
(if, for example, several programs are loaded). If the option is activated, the toolpaths
for the selected program are displayed. If the option is deactivated, the toolpaths for the
selected program are not displayed.

External simulation
hyperMILL currently supports the following external simulation programs:
• VERICUT
• COLLISION SAFEGUARD
• NCSIMUL SOLUTIONS
The following section contains information on activating and configuring external simu-
lation programs in
hyperMILL. For information on how the simulation programs work,
please consult the product documentation supplied by the respective manufacturer.
If you use an external simulation program, you must activate it first. Afterwards, you can specify various
settings for its use.
Please note that a license is necessary to use the program. Please contact your OPEN MIND partner for
details.
Activate VERICUT
1. First open the hyperMILL CONFIGURATION Center program and select Connect applications.
2. Select the VERICUT entry under Key, then go to Program, browse to the correct folder in your
VERICUT installation and select vericut.bat.
3. Confirm by selecting OK.
4. On the Postprocessor tab in the job list, select the Machine option.
5. Click the icon to open the Machine administration dialog.
6. Define a machine whose NC output you want to check using VERICUT.
7. Activate the required simulation in the General → External simulation section.
8. Click the icon to open the configuration dialog.
Configure VERICUT / COLLISION SAFEGUARD
Machine
Select a machine model (file format: *.mch/ *.xmhc).
Controller
Select a controller (file format: *.ctl/ *.xctl).
Project
Select a project file. This is a template file in which the VERICUT start configuration is defined (including
window view, tolerances, collision checking, etc.). To change the configuration, open the project file in
VERICUT and then save your changes.
Options
Default correction list: This value will be used if it has not already been defined in hyperMILL (job definition,
Tool tab). Numerical values (integers), variables (tool numbers) and calculation options (such as T:No+10)
may be used.
Tool reference point ID: Definition of a unique tool name (with formula support). Prerequisite for a correct
tool change.
Attach to: Specify whether the components are to be placed automatically ( Automatic option). The
VERICUT interface will then automatically search for the intended clamping position.
CAM
187

-- 187 of 1632 --

Position: Specify the position manually. The name of the VERICUT element at which the workpieces are
placed must be defined.
Model: Close STL specifies whether a closed solid should be created for the STL files of the model.
Option Close fixture STL creates a closed solid for the STL files of the clamping part.
Closing the files can prevent display problems in VERICUT.
Program zero: Specify whether the VERICUT interface Automatically moves the program zero point or
whether the setting is imported from the Project template.
This concludes the settings required to use the VERICUT interface.
Activate NCSIMUL
1. Open the hyperMILL CONFIGURATION Center program and select Connect applications.
2. Select the entry under Key, then go to Program, browse to the correct folder in your installation
and select ConnectorFromNXF.exe.
3. Confirm by selecting OK.
4. On the Post processor tab in the job list, select the machine option.
5. Click the icon to open the Machine administration dialog.
6. Define a machine whose NC output you want to check using .
7. Activate as a simulation in the General → External simulation section.
8. Click the icon to open the configuration dialog.
Configure

Configuration dialog).

software.
Clamping position manually: Activate to select a frame from the list to define the clamping position.
Output project: Path to create the *.nxf file and the *.stl file.
Generate project data: The files are created without starting NCSIMUL.
Run NCSIMUL: The files are created and NCSimul is started.

To show or hide all groups, right-click in the list display and select All on/All off. To show or hide all
selected groups, right-click in the list display and select All selected on/All selected off.

this group are colored red in the CAD model.

element).

Contour offset
To limit machining areas optimally, change the size of contours. If the contour has not been created yet,
you can also select surface edges and offset them at the same time.
Start via the CAM → Utilities → Contour offset menu.
Option
Tolerance: Enter the required tolerance value. This value defines:
• The maximum distances between individual elements that can be closed when joining points or
lines to curves or mesh elements.
• The minimum distances between surface edges for them to be recognized as separate contours.
Color: Color of the newly created contour.
Layer: Layer on which the newly created contour is stored.
Selection
Contours: Select contours that you want to edit. For information on selecting contours, see section
Selecting elements in the CAD system.
Allowance
Value: Distance of the new contour from the original contour.
Increment: The value defined here is added to (or subtracted from) the specified allowance value.
Coordinate system: The direction in which the newly generated contour is moved.
Click the icon to select a frame or specify a new frame.
Project on workplane: Projects the contour generated with the Contour offset function onto the current
workplane.
Apply: Creates a new contour with the data you previously entered.
Cancel: Exits the input dialog box.
Contour autolink
Link adjacent contours that do not meet exactly. The system trims minor overlaps and closes small gaps
within the tolerance specified. The resulting contours can be used for machining.
Start via the CAM → Utilities → Contour Autolink menu.

CAD Utilities
Prepare CAD models for machining with
hyperMILL.
hyperMILL for Autodesk® Inventor®
The following CAD utilities are available:
Show surfaces with errors
hyperMILL runs a plausibility check on the selected surfaces before each milling area recognition. If one
or more surfaces with errors are recognized, you can use this function to save the found surfaces with
errors to a layer. You can repair the surfaces (for example, reconstruct) or remove them from the milling
area if they are not relevant to CAM editing.
Hide surfaces with errors
You can use this function to hide all surfaces that could not be converted correctly when generating the
polyhedron.
Clear information about surfaces with errors
You can use this function to delete information about surfaces that could not be converted correctly
when generating the polyhedron.
hyperMILL for SOLIDWORKS
The following CAD utilities are available:
Incorrect converted faces
hyperMILL runs a plausibility check on the selected surfaces before each milling area recognition. If one
or more surfaces with errors are recognized, you can use this function to save the found surfaces with
errors to a layer.
You can repair the surfaces (for example, reconstruct) or remove them from the milling area if they are not
relevant to CAM editing.

CAD window.

Show all: Shows all incorrectly converted faces in the current CAD window.

CAD window.

list of incorrect faces.

machining, you can exclude them from the selection. You must then convert the surfaces again, so that the
polyhedron is generated correctly.

4. Feature and macro technology
The advantages of feature technology
Feature technology processes geometry information present in the CAD model for CAM programming in
a way that significantly reduces programming effort. In addition to the assigned geometry, features also
contain information relevant to manufacturing, such as tolerance values or fits.
The automatic derivation of manufacturing geometries makes it possible to transfer data directly from a
feature to the job definition (Feature Job Connector) for use across jobs and job lists.
Furthermore, Customized Process Features make it possible to define company standards for similar
geometries, thus increasing programming automation even further. In this process, work processes are
defined and stored as technology macros, which can be applied to similar machining tasks.
Feature technology provides you with enormous potential to increase efficiency and save time in manufac-
turing.
User interface
The user interface of the feature module comprises the following:
• The feature browser (Feature tab in the
hyperMILL browser) with representation of the feature lists
and features.
• The Feature editor (Feature dialog) for defining feature parameters and
• The Feature job connector (Feature dialog page of the job definition) for selecting and using
features in a job.

The Feature tab in the
hyperMILL browser is known as the feature browser. The feature browser compri-
ses the following:
• The top area with feature lists and shortcut menu functions (1)
• The bottom area with feature and shortcut menu functions (2)
• A freely definable filter (3)
• A toolbar with filter functions and functions to control the visibility of features (4).

Generic Hole
Generic holes are universally applicable, from Simple Holes through to complex stepped holes. Generic
holes are structured according to manufacturing elements and related properties.
Generic Holes were developed to replace in the medium term the Simple Hole, Sink Hole and Free defined
Hole features.
Generic Holes offer significant advantages when using macro machining. In particular,
when setting up a macro database with macro rules, OPEN MIND recommends exclu-
sive use of Generic Holes.
Macro databases created using previous hole features do not support the new Generic Holes. The previ-
ous hole features are still supported as an option under Feature Mapping.
Geometric data from the Generic Pocket feature can be used for the 2D, 3D and drilling cycles in the job
definition.
A generic hole can contain grooves (A), sinks (B) and back sinks (C). A distinction is made between the
following basic sink types: Counterbore (1), countersink (2), drill (3), form sink (4), tapered sink (5), torus
(6) and undercut (7).

Compound Feature
Geometric data from the Compound Feature can be used for 2D, 3D, 5X and drilling cycles in the job
definition. The following parameters can be defined
Frame: Yes if uniform frame required. If this option is selected, only sub features with the same frame
system within the Compound Feature are used. No, if uniform frame is not required.
Frame origin: Enter coordinate values or determine the orientation vector from CAD system.
Frame orientation: Enter coordinate values or determine the orientation vector from CAD system.
Sub features: Select previously defined features. Existing features can be added to a Compound Feature
directly in the feature browser. To do so, select the feature and use the Compound Feature function in the
shortcut menu.
Sub features of a Compound Feature can be selected directly in the feature browser and freely moved or
reordered (drag-and-drop operations). A Compound Feature consists of referenced sub features. Changes
to one or more sub features are automatically passed to the Compound Feature.
Functions on the shortcut menu
Point optimization:
hyperMILL optimizes the paths to be travelled between the holes of the Compound
Feature. To do so, select the feature and then select the Point optimization function from the shortcut
menu. The machining sequence is indicated by arrows. The first step is indicated by a blue arrow.
When one of the hole features within the Compound Feature already consists of several holes, these need
to be broken up first for the points to be optimized efficiently. To do so, select the feature and then select
the Explode function from the shortcut menu. The optimize the points as described above.
Reverse sequence: Use this function to reverse the machining sequence for the holes in a Compound
Feature.
Sort Holes: Sort the list of intersecting holes of a Compound Feature in the feature browser. Use Diameter
or Depth to define the sort criterion. Use Ascending or Descending to determine the sort sequence Holes
that have the same diameter or the same depth are combined into a frame (feature list). If necessary,
adjust the Tolerance for the grouping.
Import hole / Export hole: Import or export all parameters defined with a hole in *.hmf format. This applies
to the Simple Hole, Sink Hole or Free defined Hole features.
Reference frame: A reference frame can be selected when exporting holes. By doing so, all holes will be
exported with their relative frame coordinates. If this option is not activated, the WCS coordinates are used
when exporting the holes. If the model position has changed, the holes will be correctly imported, if the
same Reference frame is selected.
Use feature lists: When importing the holes, you can enable the Use feature list option to preserve the
allocation of the Features to the Feature lists.

and impellers and blisks to be easily and flexibly reused with different machining strategies. Filter defini-
tions simplify automated machining and macro programming.

Requirements
To use a CPF for machining models from a family of parts that are designed in a similar way, the following
conditions should be fulfilled:
1. The models have common geometric characteristics.
2. The machining sequence is specified in the job list.
3. Geometric elements of the CPF are linked with job parameters.
Example pocket machining
Using common geometric characteristics: Profiles (1), Bottom plane (2) and Side surfaces (3), other
pockets of a part family, such as hexagonal or octagonal, flat or deep, small or large pockets, can also be
described.

Machining step Job/Cycle

mized – planes only)
3. Finishing the side walls 3D Profile Finishing

Define structure
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, switch to the Feature tab.
2. Right-click and select New → Customized Process Feature → Machining object. The Customized
Process Feature dialog opens.
3. Name the CPF according to the machining planned.
4. Specify the CPF elements to be used in the Select area.
5. Select 1 for Orientation number.
6. Click the icon to display further options. Leave the default settings Frame for Usage in job and
W (‘write’) for Mode.
7. Select 2 for Surface group number, click the icon and use the predefined settings.
Rename parameters
You can rename the parameters (for example: Orientation 1 > Frame pocket). To do this, enter the name
of your choice in the right-hand part of the line.
In addition, you can assign a graphic to each parameter that clearly shows which geometric elements
make up the parameter. This simplifies the manual selection of geometric elements in the CAD model.
Icons in the Customized process feature dialog:
Insert graphic from a file
Paste graphic from the clipboard
Delete graphic.
Define filter
By defining a filter, you specify how elements are recognized in the CAD model. Manual assignment is
then no longer necessary. This increases the degree of automation when using the CPF.
To define a filter
1. Click the icon to open the Filter definition dialog, select the Active checkbox and enable the
required filter option: Use color filter, Use tag filter or Use layer filter.
2. Then click the and icons to Add / select color filter or Add / select tag filter and define the
color or tag class. If required, click the icon to select the surfaces that are to be used as the
basis for the filter definition.
3. If a layer filter or a layer container filter is to be used, select the Layer filter or Layer container filter
checkbox. Then click the and icons to Add / select layer filter orAdd/Select layer container
filter and define the layer/layer container.
4. To do this, in the Layer / Layer container line, click the icon / to select a layer or a layer
container that will be used for the filter definition. Click the icon to select the surfaces that are
to be used as the basis for the filter definition. By selecting sample elements, you define which
CAM
236

-- 236 of 1632 --

geometric elements will be used when using the CPF later on. In the case of surfaces on [Layer
2], the CPF searches in the job for surfaces that are on [Layer 2].
5. To delete one or all filters, click the color, Layer or Tag class line and use the Delete / Delete all
function on the shortcut menu.
6. Click the icon to include the elements found in the CAD model on the basis of the filter
definition in the selection.
Prepare CAD model
For the automatic reading of the geometry elements to work correctly using filters, the CAD models must
be created according to the filter definition.
1. Select 1 for Profile group number.
2. Click the icon and select Boundary for Usage in Job and W for Mode.
3. Enable the Milling area and Stock options and name.
4. Now confirm the CPF definition.
The CPF structure is now completely defined. The newly created CPF appears as an entry in the list under
Customized Process Feature.
Use CPF
The aim of using the CPF is to automate extensive machining processes. Before the CPF can be used, the
data from a CAD model must be assigned. This link between the CAD model and the CPF supplies a job
with the required information when using the CPF.
Link CPF to CAD data
To link CAD data of a model to the CPF, proceed as follows:
1. Right-click the feature browser and open the CPF dialog.
2. Select New → Customized Process Feature → [CPF name]. A corresponding entry is created in
the lower part of the feature browser [CPF name] and all previously defined geometry elements
are displayed in the CPF dialog.
3. For Orientation 1, select the required Frame for machining.
4. Select the hub and side surfaces of the pocket for Surfaces 1 and 2.
5. Select the limit of the hub surface for Profiles 1.
6. Finally, define the Milling area and Stock.
If all parameters of the CPF are clearly named and the corresponding data from the CAD model assigned,
the CPF can be used in the job definition. The job and CPF are linked in the Feature Job Connector.
Use CPF in the job definition
Usage of a defined CPF using the example of pocket machining (roughing).
Requirements:
• All the jobs required for machining are created in the job list in the correct sequence.
• All job parameters, which are not to be taken from the CPF, are correctly defined.
To use a CPF in the job definition, proceed as follows:
1. In the job definition, switch to the Feature dialog page and select the corresponding CPF.
2. The cycle recognizes that the profile (boundary) as well as frame, milling area and stock can be
used from the CPF for roughing and automatically sets these to active. At the same time, the
CAM
237

-- 237 of 1632 --

corresponding parameters are "greyed out" in the job definition and cannot therefore be machined
manually.
3. Deactivate CPF parameters that are not used in the job definition. To do this, double-click the en-
try in the lower area of the Feature job connector. The status changes from Active to Deactivated.
4. The job definition is free of errors and warnings and the job can be calculated.
Boundary
Stop surfaces
Use stop surfaces to define the area of the CAD model on which no machining takes place. Always use
stop surfaces whenever you need to ensure that the tool does not touch the stop surfaces.
Offset: the offset of the stop surfaces extends the area excluded from machining by the specified value.
Valid in X, Y and Z direction.
Reuse CPF in new CAD model
To reuse the CPF and the machining sequence with modified CAD data, proceed as follows:
1. Use the menu File → Merge... to insert the new CAD model, which includes allgeometric elements
used in the CPF.
2. Select the CPF in the feature browser, right-click and select Update filter definition(s). All ele-
ments of the CPF for which filters are defined are updated. This also applies to filters that were
not directly defined in the CPF (such as filters for the milling area).
By updating the filter, the data is read from the model and transferred to the jobs via the CPF.
The data in the CPF has been correctly defined and can be calculated.

Offset to bottom: Features based on through holes are created with the bottom offset specified here.

Frame creation mode
2D: A feature list is created for each drilling direction and a frame is assigned to each feature list.
5X: All recognized features are combined into one feature list, but a frame is not assigned to this list.
Mixed: If several holes have the same orientation, a feature list is created for this orientation and a frame is
assigned to the feature list. All other holes are combined into one feature list, but a frame is not assigned
to this list.
Split by diameter: In the case of multi-step holes, the diameter of the individual steps is taken into account
when arranging the features in the feature list (B). The machining direction (4) is included.
If, from the direction of machining, the diameter of a subsequent step is greater than the diameter of the
preceding step, the hole is divided into two or more Simple (3) and Sink Holes (2).
If the split by diameter function is disabled (A), this multi-step hole is included in the feature list as a freely
defined hole (1).

Use color table
When importing feature information from a CAD model,
hyperMILL also recognizes feature properties such
as thread, ISO fits or feature classes if these are defined in a color table.
hyperMILL evaluates the assignment of color information to feature properties when generating features
and incorporates the corresponding parameter directly in the feature. At the same time, this parameter is
also included in the feature name and is thus available for selection when creating and using macros.
To read information from a color table, activate the option Use color table in the Feature Mapping (Hole) di-
alog and use the Edit color table function (via the menu CAM → Setup → Settings → Database → Color
table) to specify colors for threads, ISO-fits and pockets using sample elements.
The information is stored in a *.xml file, which is located in the following folder by default.
C:\Users\Public\Documents\OPEN MIND\ColorTable\default[version].xml
In order for
hyperMILL to be able to correctly recognise the Thread and Fits feature properties, they must
be defined as follows:
Example:
<Color_Table>
<Color_Machining_Definition R="128" G="64" B="64"
FitDesignation="H7" ThreadDesignation="Mx"
FeatureClass="Special FC"
UseThreadNominalDiameter="1"/>
<Color_Machining_Definition R="128" G="0" B="128"
FitDesignation="H12"ThreadDesignation="M;G"
UseThreadNominalDiameter="0" />
</Color_Table>
The R (Red), G (Green) and B (Blue) identifiers can be assigned color values between 0 and 255.
The FitDesignation element can assume fit designations (example H7) and the ThreadDesignation ele-
ment can assume the values M = Metric Coarse Pitch, Mx = Metric Fine Pitch, W = Whitworth and G = Gas
Uni.
Several thread types are separated by ; with the order of the list determining the order of the search.
The FeatureClass element can accept designations of defined feature classes.
UseThreadNominalDiameter can assume the values 0 and 1. 0 = Reference value is the core diameter of
the thread, 1 = Reference value is the nominal diameter of the thread.

Feature Recognition
Interactive recognition of feature information from a CAD model. The following modules are available in
hyperMILL:
• Single Hole Recognition
• Plane Recognition
• Pocket Recognition
• Boundary Recognition
To recognize feature information from a CAD model:
1. In the
hyperMILL browser, switch to the Feature tab.
2. Right-click the upper area of the browser and select the required function from the shortcut menu.
Single Hole Recognition
Geometric information is gathered from the holes in a model by defining a sample hole and searching for
comparison holes, whose parameters are compared with the base hole.
The Single Hole Recognition dialog comprises the following dialog pages: Sample hole, Search and Setup.
Sample hole dialog page
The parameters of a sample hole form the basis for recognising a hole.
Strategy
Automatic recognition: Only select a surface of the base hole. All other surfaces are automatically recog-
nized.
Manual Definition: Select all surfaces of the base hole.
Reference feature: The parameters of a reference feature are used as the basis for creating Generic Holes
based on points/circles on surfaces. On the Search dialog page, use the Points and surfaces option and
select the surfaces/points that are to be used to create the hole features. The orientation of the newly
created hole features follows the surface normals in the area of the selected points.
Move to featurelist: Select an existing feature list to which the features will be assigned. With the New
option, a new feature list can be created.
Selection
Select surfaces of the hole.
Sample search: Start recognition of the sample hole.
Reverse direction: Reverse the direction of the sample hole.
Use the Reference feature strategy to select a feature from the list as reference features.
Parameters
List of recognized parameters of the base hole.
CAM
246

-- 246 of 1632 --

Further parameters can be defined if necessary.
Name: Define a name for the hole. The name is automatically copied to the feature list.
Thread: Yes, if you want to use a Thread.
Thread: Standard: Select a thread form from the Standard Options offered for the thread form Metric
Coarse Pitch, Metric Fine Pitch or Whitworth. To define an individual thread form,
1. Select User, define the designation and
2. specify the values for Diameter, Pitch, Type and Length.
Search dialog page
Here you can determine which hole surfaces should be compared with the base hole. As the result of this
comparison, holes are found which have the same parameters as the base hole.
Group selection
User: Select the required holes, whose parameters are to be compared with those of the base hole.
You can also search for holes using the Window selection function in the CAD program.
This is particularly useful with very complex models, for which Feature Recognition is
only partly relevant.
Complete model: All holes in the model with the same parameters as the base hole are automatically
recognized.
Start: Start the automatic recognition of the holes. All recognized holes are shown under Result in a list
display. The numbers mean:
Example: 3 (2)
(3) Number of directions
(2) Number of holes in this direction
Recognized holes are transferred to a feature list as a Generic Hole or Compound Feature.
Holes with the same parameters (Direction, Depth) are combined into a feature. Please note that the
defined base hole is also always included as a component of a feature.
Filter
Use a filter to limit the hoes to be recognized.
Same color: Only holes of the same color as the base hole are recognized.
Same layer: Only holes on the same layer as the base hole are recognized.
Same orientation: Only holes with the same orientation as the base hole are recognized.
Frame limit: Define a frame limit (angle) for the recognition process.
Frame: Define the frame to be used for the frame limit.

Pocket Recognition
The model used should be a (static) solid. Closed solids offer the strongest guarantee that all bottom
surfaces (surface normals) will be recognized correctly. In open solids, surface gaps may mean that some
topological information is missing and consequently yield incorrect results. In individual cases it may be
necessary to check the surface normals manually.
Pockets with bottoms, through pockets, open and closed pockets and T-Slots are recognized. Recognition
is performed through the use of manual or automatic surface selections.
The Pocket feature recognition dialog comprises the dialog pages Sample pocket, Search and Setup.
Sample pocket dialog page
Define the pocket type to be recognized. Select the surfaces of a sample pocket. Define search options
and filter criteria. Recognized bottom surfaces and pockets are presented in a list.
Option
Pocket type: Define a pocket type for recognition purposes. Distinguish between the following:
Pocket with bottom: Pockets with a bottom are recognized.
T-Slot: T-Slots are recognized.
Pockets with bottom and T-slots: Pockets with bottom and T-slot are recognized.
Through pocket: Through pockets are recognized.
Tolerance: The required tolerance of the curve resolution for the selected feature.
Name: Define a name for the pockets. This is used in the
hyperMILL feature browser; it also contains the
smallest radius in the pocket. This name is used when performing a tool search in the macro database.
Example:
If a pocket has this name, it can be machined using tools with a radius of 3 mm or less.

specify the sample pockets:
Combine pockets: Enable if individual pockets of a model are to be automatically combined into a more
complex pocket.
When used in a job, combined pockets are processed more efficiently than individual pockets
It is possible to combine the following: pockets with bottoms (1), through pockets (2) and open (2) and
closed (3) pockets. The pockets must have a common edge (4) and the same frame in order to be
combined.
Pockets connected to one another through an open pocket (5) are not considered for
automatic combination.

Search dialog page
Search for comparison pockets based on the defined sample pocket(s). Limit the search for comparison
pockets to a part of the model (option: User) or search the entire model (option: Complete model).
Recognized pockets are presented in a list.
Setup dialog page
Limit the search using filter criteria. Define comparison parameters for the search. Define conditions for
accessibility of pockets and the creation of feature lists.
Pocket filters
Tool diameter: Limit the pocket size using the tool diameter. Only pockets matching the following criteria
will be recognized: the upper diameter should not fit in the pocket, while the lower diameter should still fit.
Circular pocket limit: This option can be used to prevent holes from being recognized as circular pockets
by defining a diameter limitation. Only pockets that fall within the defined limitation are recognized.
Chamfer height / Fillet radius: Height of the chamfer or radius of the fillet between the bottom surface and
the pocket wall.
Chamfer angle: Lower / upper limit for the chamfer angle between the bottom surface and the pocket wall.
Allowed wall types: Specify which wall type is to be recognized. The Perpendicular option corresponds to
the Z axis of the frame that is defined on the Pocket example dialog page.
Combine pockets: If the Suppress original pockets option is enabled, the original pockets will be deleted
after combining.
Pocket comparison parameter
These two parameters relate to the comparison between the sample pocket and the pockets that are to be
recognized (see Comparison dialog page).
Scale limit: The minimum / maximum scale limit defines the recognition of pockets in the model on the
basis of characteristic geometric parameters.
Comparison tolerance: The degree of accuracy with which the characteristic geometric parameters (see
Scale limit) of one or more sample pocket(s) are compared with the pockets to be recognized.
Pocket Recognition can be restricted to certain pockets through the Pocket filter using geometric features.
All pocket filters are in effect when the sample pocket is defined. If they are activated, the options under
Accessibility check are effective when searching for comparison pockets.
Accessibility
Since not all pockets are directly accessible and can be processed, conditions for the accessibility of a
pocket are defined here.
Accessibility check: the accessibility is checked in the direction of the surface normals of the respective
bottom surfaces, and in the opposite direction (1).
Approach length: defines the minimum distance between a potential bottom plane and another surface that
may prevent access to the bottom plane (2).

255

1 	2
Polyhedron offset: Accessibility of the bottom plane (pocket bottom) is determined on the basis of this
contour offset over an extrusion surface. This should always be larger than the value for polyhedron
tolerance (3).
3
Polyhedron tolerance: accuracy of the polyhedron representation for the accessibility check (faceting of the
model).
All recognized pockets are transferred as Generic Pocket feature (close/open) to a feature list. Pockets
with the same Z direction are combined into one list (frame). The colors of the feature lists that you create
are defined in the
hyperMILL settings (see dialog page Document → Colors).
Feature list generation
Use feature list: if this option is enabled, the pockets are saved as features in the existing feature lists.
Feature assignment is in reference to the frames assigned to feature lists. Feature lists that do not contain
frames are ignored.
Use color table: When reading feature information, pocket bottoms with a specific color value (RGB value)
are automatically recognized and the respective features are assigned to a corresponding feature class.
For this purpose, both the color value and the name of the feature class are defined in an XML file. The
name and location of the XML file can be selected freely.
Example:
CAM
256

-- 256 of 1632 --

<Color_Table>
<Color_Machining_Definition
R="214" G="214" B="214" IsPocketBottom="1" FeatureClass="Special
Pocket"/>
</Color_Table>
To read this information, activate the Use color table option, select the corresponding file (format: *.xml)
and confirm your entries. The Pocket feature created contains the designation of the feature class in the
feature name.
Example:
Generische Tasche <Geschlossen R10 Spezial-Feature>.
The feature class is displayed in the feature editor (section: General).
Use all colors: Even pocket bottoms whose colors are not contained in the XML file will be recognized. The
recognized pockets are, however, not assigned to a feature class.
If the function is disabled, only pocket bottoms that correspond to a color in the XML file will be recognized.
XML files can also be used in the Feature Mapping area to read in feature information.

User: Plane Recognition is performed based on the defined surfaces. Select the surfaces to be used for
the recognition.
Automatic: Plane Recognition is performed automatically based on the entire CAD model.
Filter
Several filter functions are available.
Use frame: When this option is enabled, only planes that have the same orientation as the selected frame
are recognized.
Top / Bottom: Specifies the range (Z direction) that is relevant to the Plane Recognition.
Ignore circular planes: Enable this option when circular planes (of holes) are to be excluded from recogni-
tion.
Start: Start the recognition process.
Result
Recognized planes are shown in a list display. Use the Reverse function on the shortcut menu for the
recognized planes to reverse the direction of the surface normals (machining direction) of the recognized
planes. Use Reverse all to reverse all the surface normals. Select Delete to delete the feature for a
recognized plane.
Top / Bottom: Define the height of the top and bottom for recognized planes. The values are transferred as
parameters to the Feature dialog.
Apply: Create a feature from recognized planes. All recognized planes are transferred as features to a
feature list.

Transformation Pattern Recognition
Use the Transformation Pattern Recognition function to recognize equal subareas of the CAD model and
transform toolpaths, which have already been generated for a subarea, to the recognized equal subareas
of the CAD model. To use the function, proceed as follows:
1. Select Transformation Pattern Recognition from the shortcut menu in the feature browser (feature
lists) and open the dialog.
2. In the dialog, select the frame under Frame and the surfaces of the previously edited geometry
under Selection → Surfaces. The Sorting → Shortest distance function searches for the same
geometries at the shortest distance from the selected geometry, taking the current frame view into
account. If the Grouping function is also activated, the same geometries found are grouped within
the selected frame and the groups are sorted according to the shortest distance.
3. As a result of the calculation, a new transformation is created in the Frames browser under Trans-
formations. It contains a correct frame for each geometry found. The frames are automatically
used for machining when the transformation is used.
4. For further processing, activate the Transformation function in the job definition and select the
newly created transformation under Selection → General pattern.
CAM

Use feature
A feature defined in
hyperMILL is shown as an entry in the
hyperMILL browser and is directly available
during job definition. Two basic options are available to use a feature during job definition: from feature to
job or from job to feature.
From feature to job
To use a feature during job definition:
1. Start the
hyperMILL browser and switch to the Feature tab.
2. Select the required feature and right-click.
3. Choose the New job with feature function on the shortcut menu. A list appears with the cycles in
which you can use the selected feature.
4. Select the cycle you require and go to the Feature dialog page.
5. The feature currently connected with the job and the status of the geometric data are displayed in
the Feature Job Connector.
To edit a feature:
1. Select the feature, right-click and select Edit.
2. Make the required changes in the Feature editor and close the editor.
To select a feature:
1. Click the icon to open the Select feature dialog.
2. Drag the feature into the right window and confirm with OK.
In 2D cycles, only those features with the same frame as the one already being used in
the job can be added.
To change the geometry status of a feature, select the geometry to be changed in the right window, click
the right mouse button and select Active or Inactive.
If there are several geometries in the Feature Job Connector, but only one of these is to be active, select
the geometry to be changed in the right window, click the right mouse button and select Active only.
From job to feature
To use a feature during job definition:
1. Start the
hyperMILL browser, go to the Jobs tab and select the required cycle.
2. Specify the required settings and go to the Feature dialog page.
3. Click the icon to open the Select feature dialog.
4. Drag the feature into the right window and confirm with OK.
To define a new feature for a job,
1. right-click the left window of the Feature job connector and
2. select New → [Feature Name].
CAM
261

3. Select the required feature from the list.
Reverse orientation of the feature
If you use a feature in the job definition, the correct feature orientation is important. You can reverse the
feature orientation directly in the feature browser for through holes and through pockets. To do so, select
the feature and then select the Reverse hole or Reverse pocket function from the shortcut menu.
If the feature orientation is not identical to the frame orientation of the feature list, the feature is marked
with an exclamation mark and a message is output.
Disconnect: Deactivate the link between the job and the feature. The contour which has been derived from
the feature is retained as a CAD element, and can be used for job definition.
Create new frame with feature
To create a new frame with the selected feature, select the feature in the left window of the Feature job
connector, right-click and select New frame on feature. The new frame appears in the
hyperMILL browser
(Model tab).

Define the sink diameter and sink depth. The original feature name remains.

Replace by thread: Only available for the Sink Hole feature, adds a thread to a Sink Hole. Here, the sink

Fit hole to stock model (1): Adjust a hole feature to an existing or modified stockmodel geometry. Select
the hole features to be adjusted in the
hyperMILL feature browser and select the Fit hole to stock model
function from the shortcut menu (right-click). Spots will also be taken into account.
1
Selection

ungroup combined features if this is necessary in order to adjust the stock model geometry (for more
information, see the Tolerance option).
Manual: Manually define how to adjust the hole features to the stock model geometry. A negative stock
allowance is not possible at present. The changes associated with the Manual option only concern the top
side of the hole (origin).

If the tolerance value is higher than the difference of the distances between the smallest and largest

grouped to form new features.

Macro technology
Macros link machining strategies and tools for machining characteristic geometries (= features) and there-
by considerably reduce programming expenditure during production.
Advantages and uses
• Automation and recycling of workflows: Workflows can be automated and recycled using macros.
This significantly reduces programming time, particularly when it comes to producing 2.5D parts.
• Efficient macro management: Your macros reside in a macro database. This provides a production
knowledge base that is efficiently and easily managed.
• Updating workflows: You can modify your existing macros at any point to match user-specific new
production requirements as they arise.
• Higher degree of automation thanks to ‘intelligent’ macros: Using ‘intelligent’ macros, operations
that were previously assigned to a feature manually can be automatically linked. Rules and condi-
tions are defined to allow
hyperMILL to automatically decide which machining will be applied. This
method can therefore reduce the number of macros needed to machine a complete model.
Create macro
A macro includes features and job information. It is created based on a job or a feature.
Creating job-based macros
To generate a macro based on a job:
1. Open the
hyperMILL browser and select the Jobs tab.
2. Select the job that you want to associate with the macro and select Macros → New macro from
job.
The New macro window opens.
Create feature-based macro
To create a macro based on a feature:
1. Open the
hyperMILL browser and select the Feature tab.
2. Highlight the feature whose information you wish to use.
3. Right-click and select New macro from feature.
The New macro dialog opens.
The New macro dialog
Macro
Name: The name of the source feature. This is part of the macro name. The name is written to the macro
database when the macro is saved. The name is also used for automatic macro searches. The names of
feature-based macros contain the prefix F; the names of job-based macros contain the prefix J.
Comment: You can also enter a comment for easier identification of the macro.
Macro group: Each macro has to be assigned to a macro group. Macro groups allow you to combine
macros that are typical for a particular machining situation, for example.

The Apply macro dialog
Specify which macros should be applied in the Apply macro dialog. Use filters to restrict or increase the

Tools in the macro database
The Tool data column in the list view indicates how the used tool was created. A distinction is made
between the following:
Macro: The tool was defined directly in the macro (or job) without a search of the tool database.
DB: the tool used for the job is taken from the tool database (numbered NC tool).
DB+Auto: Only applies to 2D drilling jobs. Like DB + automatic tool search, the Tool length is taken into
account. All of the tools suggested are collision-free.
DB+Auto+: Only applies to 2D drilling jobs. Like DB + automatic tool search, the Tool length and Tool
diameter are taken into account. All of the tools suggested are collision-free.
Automatic macro search
During an automatic macro search,
hyperMILL searches the database for macros that match the selected
feature and then applies these.
Macro optimization
Jobs that can be machined using the same tool are processed in sequence (tool change optimization).
Intelligent macros
Macros link machining strategies and tools with geometric information. Intelligent macros also include rules
that evaluate geometric information and define when a machining strategy is executed. Intelligent macros
are available for all types of features.
Initial situation: The workpiece to be machined contains many holes of various depths, diameters and sink
types. A typical procedure in production may then be as follows:
1. Using Feature Mapping, the drilling geometries are recognized automatically and saved as a
feature.
2. The assignment of the machining methods of these features (jobs) and the saving as a macro are
initially done manually.
3. The rules are now defined in the next step. They determine which part of a macro is to be
executed under specific conditions.
Define rule
To define a rule for an intelligent macro:
1. Open the macro database and select the macro for which you wish to define a rule.
2. Right-click and select Free feature parameter.
3. Specify the parameters you want to free. When you do this, the link between feature parameters
and macros is severed so that you can then use the parameters for the purpose of rule definition.
4. Now open the job to which you wish to assign a rule by double-clicking the job entry in the lower
area of the macro database (macro jobs).
5. On the Rule dialog tab, click the Job active entry and then click the icon .
CAM
273

-- 273 of 1632 --

6. Set the conditions for enabling a machining mode (of a job) based on simple IF-THEN rules.
A part of the macro name is then displayed in square brackets (example: F:D8[Through]). This indicates
that parameters have been freed.
Feature parameters and formulas can be used to define macro rules.
With the aid of formulas, tool parameters (such as T:Rad, T:Len, T:GageLen, T:Ti-
pAng) and user variables (such as F:H, F:R, F:LD) are available for rule definition.
Once you have confirmed your entries, the job will be marked in the macro database with [R] = Rule.
Example: [R] Simple Drilling.
If all geometries in the model and strategies necessary for machining have been specified as part of the
rules and if the corresponding macros have been saved in the macro database, they will be available for
cross-model application.
Upon application of the macros,
hyperMILL automatically provides for each geometry the correct machin-
ing sequence and thus enables the automatic machining of the models to be machined.

5. Probing
Available machining cycles
3D Point Probing: Measure the coordinates of any 3D points to measure the accuracy of a machining job.
Workpiece alignment along edge: Compensation of a workpiece misalignment with a probing tool along an
edge. The compensation angle is calculated automatically by
hyperMILL, which means there is no need to
manually align the fixture.
Workpiece alignment with holes: Compensation of a workpiece misalignment with a probing tool using two
holes. The compensation angle is calculated automatically by
hyperMILL, which means there is no need to
manually align the fixture.
Rectangular Probing: Measure the size and location of rectangular bosses and pockets to measure the
accuracy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and the origin can be set.
Slot-Rib Probing: Probing of the size and position of slots and ribs with the option to adjust a reference tool
and set the origin.
Circular Probing: Measure the size and location of cylinders and holes to measure the accuracy of a
machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and the origin can be set.
Axis dependent Probing: Measure the location of points depending on the X, Y and Z axis of the machining
frame to measure the accuracy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and the
origin can be set.
3D Point Probing
Probing of point(s) on any surface/model. The motion of the probe is perpendicular to the touch point.
The results are the coordinate of the probe in X, Y and Z when it triggers. Evaluation of the deviation is
performed via protocol.

Optimization
Drilling point optimization allows any drilling patterns to be optimized in accordance with various criteria
(not available for the Turning strategy), so that the stresses and heat that are generated during drilling are
distributed as evenly as possible over the entire surface.
hyperMILL generates a graphical feedback of the drilling points that have been selected
for machining. Since a large number of drilling points requires a correspondingly pow-
erful computer to calculate and display this graphical preview, the preview display is
limited to 1000 drilling points by default.
Sorting strategy
Off: Drill holes are machined in the order in which they were selected.
Shortest distance: Machining is carried out starting with the (drilling) point closest to the origin of the
specified coordinate system (frame), followed by the next closest in each case. Select the Use start
reference option to use a start point as the reference for the beginning of the optimization.
Circular: The drill holes to be machined are divided into concentric circle segments starting from a center
point.
X or Y parallel: The drill holes to be machined are divided into segments that are referenced on the X or Y
axis of the selected machining coordinate system (frame).
Contour parallel: The drill holes are machined along the outline of the outer contour of the drilling point
pattern.
More information about the various parameters is provided in the next few chapters.
Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is aligned
with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature
definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
CAM
277

-- 277 of 1632 --

Circular sorting strategy
Start
Use start reference: Define any point as the start point. This start point can be inside or outside of the
drilling point pattern. In this case, machining starts from the defined start reference and moves to the
neighboring point in accordance with the Machining direction and Orientation.
Z optimization
Z optimization: Use the Max. Z depth parameter to specify the conditions for optimized machining of drill
holes at different Z levels. If the distance between two levels is greater than this value, all of the drill holes
on one level are fully machined first before moving to the next level. XY optimization takes place on every
level, while taking account of the relevant starting points.
This method reduces the number of empty paths.
(1) without Z optimization, (2) with Z optimization.
1 	2
Orientation
The parameters for controlling orientation relate to the machining of the segments.
Clockwise: The segments are machined in clockwise order.
Counterclockwise: The segments are machined in counterclockwise order.
Zigzag: The orientation (clockwise/counterclockwise) is reversed after each segment of the circle.
Machining
Inside-Out: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the inside outwards.
Outside-In: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the outside inwards.
Parameters
Radial width (1): Width of a circle segment, measured from the center of the machining area.
Center point: In order to obtain a correct toolpath calculation, it is essential to define a center point. The
center point to be defined represents the center point of all circle segments that define the machining area.
In the following, the surface between two concentric circles will be referred to as a circle segment. The
term circle segment is not used in
hyperMILL. It is only used in this documentation to describe the drilling
optimization functionality.

Orientation
Zigzag: The machining direction of the segments changes after each segment.
Oneway: The segments are always machined in the same direction.
Shortest distance: Machining continues from the last drilling point of a segment to the closest drilling point

Revert X: The machining direction oriented on the X axis of the frame coordinate system is reversed.
Revert Y: The machining direction oriented on the Y axis of the frame coordinate system is reversed.

Segment width (A): Width of a segment extending in the X or Y direction. Corresponds to the maximum
distance between points in the X or Y direction within a segment.

Create log file: Creates a measuring log.
