Check tool
The tool check ensures that all of the components defined for the tool are protected from a possible
collision with the CAD model on the basis of existing material. The tool check is only available if you have
defined a tool and also a model to be checked.
Check on: You must always enable this option if you want the tool to be checked for collisions. If the tool
check is not enabled, the tool used is shown in red in the graphic preview. When this check is enabled,
the defined clearance is used to check all of the components defined for the tool. We recommend that you
define the clearance so that it gets continuously larger, starting with the thick shank in the direction of the
spindle.
Tool check setup: the tool check settings are specified in this dialog box. For further information, see
section Tool check setup (page 722)

tion for the generation of toolpath is carried out.
Stop before execution: A stop marker in the toolpath causes the tool to stop.
In addition to activating this function, go to the Machine properties → Program halt dialog and enter the
command to stop the tool (by means of M function or command chain). Open the Machine properties
dialog via Job list → Postprocessor → Machine → Machine administration → Edit.

Define the stock.
Check tool
The tool check ensures that all of the components defined for the tool are protected from a possible
collision with the CAD model on the basis of existing material. The tool check is only available if you have
defined a tool and also a model to be checked.
Check on: You must always enable this option if you want the tool to be checked for collisions. If the tool
check is not enabled, the tool used is shown in red in the graphic preview. When this check is enabled,
the defined clearance is used to check all of the components defined for the tool. We recommend that you
define the clearance so that it gets continuously larger, starting with the thick shank in the direction of the
spindle.

Compensation of a workpiece misalignment with a probing tool using two holes. The compensation angle

hyperMILL based on the tool geometry, which means there is no need to
manually align the setup.

After the correction, the clamping situation is no longer consistent with the calculated

hyperMILL. There is a risk of collision! Please check the aligned component

OPEN MIND recommends that you proceed as follows for the workpiece alignment:

dependent Probing cycles.

Contour selection
The following elements can be selected as a contour: rectangle, rectangle with corner radius, point, arc

the X and Y direction.

of the ball of the probing tool. It is specified either relative to the contour (option: Relative to contour) or as

Additional surfaces: Temporary safety surfaces to avoid unnecessary rapid travel movements. Surfa-

Check tool
The tool check ensures that all of the components defined for the tool are protected from a possible
collision with the CAD model on the basis of existing material. The tool check is only available if you have
defined a tool and also a model to be checked.
Check on: You must always enable this option if you want the tool to be checked for collisions. If the tool
check is not enabled, the tool used is shown in red in the graphic preview. When this check is enabled,
the defined clearance is used to check all of the components defined for the tool. We recommend that you
define the clearance so that it gets continuously larger, starting with the thick shank in the direction of the
spindle.
Tool check setup: the tool check settings are specified in this dialog box. For further information, see
section Tool check setup (page 722)

Stop before execution: A stop marker in the toolpath causes the tool to stop.

dialog via Job list → Postprocessor → Machine → Machine administration → Edit.

6. Turning
Turning is a production process for manufacturing rotationally symmetrical internal and external surfaces
by removing material from turning stock of any shape. The external shape of a workpiece is created by
using the Outside option, and the internal shape by using the Inside option.
The
millTURN module allows for the combination of milling and turning tasks in a job list.
Stockmodel for subsequent machining tasks: As with milling jobs, a stockmodel can also be generated for
subsequent turning operations (resulting stock).
NC files: The NC files created with the
millTURN module can be used for both milling and turning tasks.
Available machining cycles
Roughing: Roughing of turning stock of any shape in axial or radial machining direction.
Contour parallel Turning: Roughing of turning stock of any shape parallel to contour.
Finishing: Contour parallel finishing of workpieces of any shape based on a preceding roughing operation.
Rollfeed Turning: Machining of workpieces by rolling the tool insert on the component contour, ensuring a
very high surface quality.
3X simultaneous Roughing: Roughing of workpieces with a simultaneous swivel axis.
3X simultaneous Finishing: Finishing of workpieces with a simultaneous swivel axis.
Groove Turning: Axial roughing of workpieces with grooves or shoulders.
Groove Plunging: Radial roughing of workpieces with grooves and shoulders.
Groove Finishing: Radial finishing of turning workpieces with grooves or shoulders.
Face Groove Turning: Radial roughing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoulders. The tools
used normally have three cutting edges.
Face Groove Plunging: Axial roughing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoulders. The tools
used normally have three cutting edges.
Face Groove Finishing: Finishing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoulders.
Parting: Radial machining to separate the component from the bar stock, optionally with chamfer. Parting
off can be done on the front or at the back of the workpiece.
Thread Cutting: Creation of single or multiple start, cylindrical or conical, external and internal threads with
constant pitch. Infeed can be performed either with constant chip section or with constant X value.
Roughing
Roughing of turning stock of any shape in axial or radial machining direction.
Tool Free angle: Defines the minimum angle to be maintained between the tool insert and the calculated
toolpath (1). Defining a free angle automatically calculates the tool plunge angle. (2) Turning contour, (3)
turning model.

Radial / axial infeed to the next machining plane.
Constant (1): Constant infeed depth over the entire machining area.
Ascending (2): Based on a starting infeed (a) the infeed value is increased by one value per cut. The

minimal cutting depth (b), the ramp angle is calculated automatically in relation to the contour.

High Performance
High Performance Roughing
Use if material that is difficult to cut is to be machined or a reliable chip break cannot be achieved with
conventional strategies.
MAXX Machining for turning jobs is characterized by:
• High degree of process reliability and material removal plus a high level of quality at the same time.
• Constant, low load on the tool and machine during the entire machining.
• Support for round inserts.
• Feedrate for fast positioning movements.
High Performance Mode: To use the function, select the High Performance Mode checkbox.

Strategy
Linear: (1), (2) Material is removed parallel to the turning axis in accordance with the specified Infeed
direction (see Strategy dialog page).
Ramping: (3), (4) Ramp-shaped material removal. Here, a ramp-shaped first cut is always made on a
plane and the remaining material is cleared on the same plane in a second cut parallel to the turning axis.
Zigzag: (2), (4) Machining with alternating cutting mode.

Feedrate reposition: Feedrate for the repositioning between the infeed planes.

Tool life control
Activate the function if the material to be machined requires the time the tool is engaged to be controlled.
Use the Distance option and the Max. Distance parameter to define the maximum permissible length of the
toolpath for which the tool is engaged. Select the Time option in order to define the maximum permissible
time for which the tool should be engaged using the Max. time parameter. Number of paths limits the
time the tool is engaged with the Max. number of paths parameter. When the defined condition has been
achieved, the machining ends and the tool retracts to the clearance plane.
Chip thickness control
The Chip thickness control function ensures that the chip thickness remains as constant as possible during
machining, thus guaranteeing reliable chip breaking during lead in and retraction and at shallow cutting
depths.
Use the two parameters Min. feedrate and Max. feedrate to define the range for adjusting the feedrate.
The target chip thickness is calculated from the feedrate of the tool (see cutting profile of the tool).
1) Chip thickness control is activated, (2) Chip thickness control is not activated.

Turning stock
Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turning frame and
the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.
Open the Stock model dialog. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning stock.
Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock.
Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent turning jobs based on the current
turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent milling jobs based on the current
turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.
The From existing mill stock option should only be used if the following conditions are
fulfilled:
1. Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
2. The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of different
resolutions during stock tracking.
Generate milling stock from turning stock: Any turning stock that is represented by an entry in the
hy-
perMILL model browser can be used to create a milling stock model.
Highlight the corresponding turning stock model in the browser and select the Create milling stock function
from the shortcut menu. Specify the required resolution and click OK to confirm. The created milling stock
model appears as an entry in the
hyperMILL model browser.
Frame: The Z axis of the machining frame must be the same as the rotary axis of the tool. Both the
turning area (turning model) and the turning stock must lie in the X-Z plane.

Define the Color and Layer of the turning contour. Select Use model colors to adopt the current colors from

Surfaces
Resolution: Define the resolution (fineness) of the turning area.
Select surfaces or a solid.
hyperMILL automatically creates a turning contour that defines the turning
area. An entry is created in the
hyperMILL browser and a Contour feature is created in the feature
browser.
Turning stock
Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turning frame and
the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.
Open the Stock model dialog. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning stock.
Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock.
Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent turning jobs based on the current
turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent milling jobs based on the current
turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.
The From existing mill stock option should only be used if the following conditions are
fulfilled:
1. Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
2. The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of different
resolutions during stock tracking.
Generate milling stock from turning stock: Any turning stock that is represented by an entry in the
hy-
perMILL model browser can be used to create a milling stock model.
Highlight the corresponding turning stock model in the browser and select the Create milling stock function
from the shortcut menu. Specify the required resolution and click OK to confirm. The created milling stock
model appears as an entry in the
hyperMILL model browser.
Frame: The Z axis of the machining frame must be the same as the rotary axis of the tool. Both the
turning area (turning model) and the turning stock must lie in the X-Z plane.

Smooth overlap
Various tools and orientations are often required to manufacture complex components.
The Smooth overlap function achieves smooth transitions without any visible machining
marks between individual machining areas (jobs). The tool follows the selected contour
beyond the boundary in a gentle lifting movement.
Please note: The selected contour must be part of the turning area.
Use smooth overlap: Activate to enable smooth lifting of the tool in the contour extension. Use Contour
length to define the length of the lifting movement and Distance to define the maximum retract value of the
tool for the extension of the selected contour.

High Performance
High Performance Roughing
Use if material that is difficult to cut is to be machined or a reliable chip break cannot be achieved with
conventional strategies.
MAXX Machining for turning jobs is characterized by:
• High degree of process reliability and material removal plus a high level of quality at the same time.
• Constant, low load on the tool and machine during the entire machining.
• Support for round inserts.
• Feedrate for fast positioning movements.
High Performance Mode: To use the function, select the High Performance Mode checkbox.

Linear: (1), (2) Material is removed parallel to the turning axis in accordance with the specified Infeed
direction (see Strategy dialog page).
Ramping: (3), (4) Ramp-shaped material removal. Here, a ramp-shaped first cut is always made on a
plane and the remaining material is cleared on the same plane in a second cut parallel to the turning axis.
Zigzag: (2), (4) Machining with alternating cutting mode.

Fillet radius: Additional toolpath filleting in the corners. Default: corner radius * 0.1.
Feedrate
Feedrate reposition: Feedrate for the repositioning between the infeed planes.
Unit: mm or inch/revolution of the workpiece.
Tool life control
Activate the function if the material to be machined requires the time the tool is engaged to be controlled.
Use the Distance option and the Max. Distance parameter to define the maximum permissible length of the
toolpath for which the tool is engaged. Select the Time option in order to define the maximum permissible
time for which the tool should be engaged using the Max. time parameter. Number of paths limits the
time the tool is engaged with the Max. number of paths parameter. When the defined condition has been
achieved, the machining ends and the tool retracts to the clearance plane.

Tangential (2): Define tangential length.
Circular (3): Define radius and arc angle.
Ramp (4): Define ramp length and ramp angle.

Setup
Models and stock models for turning cycles are always shown in a 2D view for the sake
of clarity.
Turning model
A turning model is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour that is located in the X-Z plane of the
turning frame.
CAM
372

-- 372 of 1632 --

Collision check: If this option is selected, the holder of the tool used is permanently checked for potential
collisions against the current stock model (tracked stock model) and the current turning model.
Open the Turning area dialog. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning area.
Generate a turning area by selecting a closed contour.
Open the Create turning area from model dialog to create a turning area from surfaces or solids. Define
the frame, color and layer of the turning contour.
Frame for turning axis
Select a frame for the turning axis from the list.
Define the Color and Layer of the turning contour. Select Use model colors to adopt the current colors from
the model.
Surfaces
Resolution: Define the resolution (fineness) of the turning area.
Select surfaces or a solid.
hyperMILL automatically creates a turning contour that defines the turning
area. An entry is created in the
hyperMILL browser and a Contour feature is created in the feature
browser.
Turning stock
Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turning frame and
the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.
Open the Stock model dialog. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning stock.
Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock.
Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent turning jobs based on the current
turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent milling jobs based on the current
turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.
The From existing mill stock option should only be used if the following conditions are
fulfilled:
1. Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
2. The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of different
resolutions during stock tracking.
Generate milling stock from turning stock: Any turning stock that is represented by an entry in the
hy-
perMILL model browser can be used to create a milling stock model.
Highlight the corresponding turning stock model in the browser and select the Create milling stock function
from the shortcut menu. Specify the required resolution and click OK to confirm. The created milling stock
model appears as an entry in the
hyperMILL model browser.
Frame: The Z axis of the machining frame must be the same as the rotary axis of the tool. Both the
turning area (turning model) and the turning stock must lie in the X-Z plane.

Options
Radial / axial limit: Limits the machining area of the tool used in the radial or axial direction.
Radial compensation
Pre-plunge: During finishing, the tool is plunged at the transition of the defined contour from the axial to
the radial direction. Removing material here prevents the tool from engaging with two sides of the insert
at the same time in the following machining step. The Pre-plunge option also supports smaller retraction
movements.
Radial compensation value (1): Radial deviation from the model contour in final finishing. The radial
compensation value is necessary due to the deflection of the tool, which is affected by the following
factors: feedrate (f), cutting depth (ap), geometry of the tool, cutting speed (Vc), and workpiece material.

length of the used tool can also be machined.

Options
Radial / axial limit: Limits the machining area of the tool used in the radial or axial direction.
Enable path compensation: When this option is activated, path compensation is handled by the controller,
that is, the cutting radius is calculated by the controller (G41 and G42). If this option is not enabled, the
cutting radius is calculated beforehand in
hyperMILL.
Change reference side: The reference side of the recessing tool changes (left/right) during machining.
Only available if path compensation is enabled.
Machining mode
Limit machining to selected areas.
Flat and steep areas are separated from each other by a slope angle. 0° corresponds to parallel to the
turning axis and 90° is perpendicular to the turning axis.
Off: Steep and flat areas of the defined contour are machined (1).
Steep areas: Only the steep areas of the defined contour are machined (2).
Flat areas: Only the flat areas of the defined contour are machined (3).
1 2 3
Radial compensation
Pre-plunge: During finishing, the tool is plunged at the transition of the defined contour from the axial to
the radial direction. Removing material here prevents the tool from engaging with two sides of the insert
at the same time in the following machining step. The Pre-plunge option also supports smaller retraction
movements.

Downward: Material is removed with downward movements only.
Side allowance (1): Allowance in Z direction.
Overlap (2): A path overlap to avoid collision with perpendicular walls (residual stock). The value should
always be slightly larger than the radius of the tool.

Turning model
A turning model is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour that is located in the X-Z plane of the
turning frame.
Collision check: If this option is selected, the holder of the tool used is permanently checked for potential
collisions against the current stock model (tracked stock model) and the current turning model.
Open the Turning area dialog. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning area.
Generate a turning area by selecting a closed contour.
Open the Create turning area from model dialog to create a turning area from surfaces or solids. Define
the frame, color and layer of the turning contour.
Frame for turning axis
Select a frame for the turning axis from the list.
Define the Color and Layer of the turning contour. Select Use model colors to adopt the current colors from
the model.
Surfaces
Resolution: Define the resolution (fineness) of the turning area.
Select surfaces or a solid.
hyperMILL automatically creates a turning contour that defines the turning
area. An entry is created in the
hyperMILL browser and a Contour feature is created in the feature
browser.
Turning stock
Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turning frame and
the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.
Open the Stock model dialog. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning stock.
Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock.
Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent turning jobs based on the current
turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent milling jobs based on the current
turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.
The From existing mill stock option should only be used if the following conditions are
fulfilled:
1. Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
2. The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of different
resolutions during stock tracking.
Generate milling stock from turning stock: Any turning stock that is represented by an entry in the
hy-
perMILL model browser can be used to create a milling stock model.
Highlight the corresponding turning stock model in the browser and select the Create milling stock function
from the shortcut menu. Specify the required resolution and click OK to confirm. The created milling stock
model appears as an entry in the
hyperMILL model browser.

The machining strategy is determined by the parting tool definition. If the parting insert position on the tool
is left, Front face is automatically enabled as a strategy (1); if the position is right, Back face is activated as
a strategy (2). If the parting insert position on the tool is neutral, the strategy can be chosen freely (3). In
this case, the parameter front angle of the insert is not available.

Type
Defines how the tool should proceed after parting off.
Parting off and rapid (1): A retraction movement is performed at feedrate in Z direction to clearance
distance, then rapid retract to the clearance radius.
Parting off and rapid (2): a retraction movement is performed at feedrate in Z direction to clearance
distance, then rapid retract at feedrate up to the clearance radius.

feedrate.
Retract clearance distance (2): Parting off is performed in multiple passes, each with the defined Plunge

Retract to clearance radius (3): parting off is done in multiple passes, each with the defined plunge depth

Turning stock
Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turning frame and
the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.
Open the Stock model dialog. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning stock.
Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock.
Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent turning jobs based on the current
turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stock model for subsequent milling jobs based on the current
turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.
The From existing mill stock option should only be used if the following conditions are
fulfilled:
1. Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
2. The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of different
resolutions during stock tracking.
Generate milling stock from turning stock: Any turning stock that is represented by an entry in the
hy-
perMILL model browser can be used to create a milling stock model.
Highlight the corresponding turning stock model in the browser and select the Create milling stock function
from the shortcut menu. Specify the required resolution and click OK to confirm. The created milling stock
model appears as an entry in the
hyperMILL model browser.
Frame: The Z axis of the machining frame must be the same as the rotary axis of the tool. Both the

7. Drilling
Available machining cycles
Centering (page 454): Centering with various parameters.
Simple Drilling (page 466): Machining of Simple Holes in one infeed.
Drilling with Chip Beak (page 478): Machining of Simple Holes in several drilling strokes.
Drilling with Pecking (page 491): Machining of Simple Holes with retract to clearance distance between
each drilling stroke.
Optimized deep Hole Drilling (page 508): Machining of holes with feedrate optimization for cross holes or
breakthroughs.
Reaming (page 535): Reboring to improve the quality of the surface when chip thickness is reduced.
Tapping (page 547): Drilling of threads with various parameters.
Boring (page 560): Drilling with a boring bar for large drilling diameters. Input parameters similar to Simple
Hole.
Helical Drilling (page 588): Machining of circular pockets with helical stepdown and horizontal grooving on
the pocket floor. Roughing, grooving on pocket floor, finishing and chamfering can be carried out in one
job.
Thread Milling (page 601): Using a helical stepdown, this cycle produces single and multiple inside and
outside threads with a definable chamfer. A hole must have been predrilled for internal threads.
Circular Pocket (page 620): Machining of circular pockets parallel to the contour, with specifiable machin-
ing direction using climb milling or conventional milling.
Gun Drilling (page 632): Drilling of very deep holes with a long tool with small diameter. This requires a
previously drilled hole of the same diameter as the hole to be created by Gun Drilling.
5X Helical Drilling (MAXX Machining) (page 632): This cycle produces circular holes through helical
toolpaths. The tool is executed in a 5-axis manner with a given lead and tilt angle.
Tool The following applies to all drilling cycles that support the parameter Tip angle compensation:
When using stepped tools with multiple reference points (for example, reference point 1 = 0 and reference
point 2 = 25), this option should not be enabled.
Contours
Define the drilling strategy, contour selection for the holes and the vertical machining area (top and depth)
of the holes.
Drilling mode
2D Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is always aligned with the Z axis of the defined frame system.
When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be collision
checked using the Milling area.
2D multi index drilling: the direction of any number of drillings can be aligned with the different frames/
planes. For infeed movements in XY direction, a relative clearance (automatically calculated for each
frame) can be defined. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
5X Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is aligned with the normals of the selected surfaces or with the
selected lines. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be
collision checked using the milling area.
CAM

-- 441 of 1632 --

The following applies to multi-axis indexing:
1. In Drilling mode: The frame specifies the machining direction. The linking movements between
the frames are controlled by the postprocessor.
2. In 5X Drilling mode: Several sides can be machined in one job. The linking movements between
the machining sides are checked for collisions and are executed as 5X simultaneous movements.
A machine is required that supports this type of movement.
Turning: With this option, turning jobs can be carried out with a rotating spindle and fixed tool. The
machining direction is defined by the Z axis of the frame. The drill position is always located in the center
point of the workpiece being turned.
Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is aligned
with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature
definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
Drilling in 5X Drilling mode in combination with tool reference points is no longer sup-
ported. If you want to machine with reference points, OPEN MIND recommends using
the2D multi index drilling mode.

Drill positions are selected either directly on the Contours input page or by allocating a previously defined
feature on the Feature input page.

CAD system.

Contour selection – 2D Drilling
Lines: The selected contour defines the top and depth of the drill hole. The machining area (top/depth) can
be changed on the dialog page by entering values. Positive values will enlarge the drill hole and negative
values will reduce the size of the drill hole. The direction of the drill hole is determined by the Z-axis of the
defined frame.
Points: The following methods are available for defining the top and depth: Absolute (job frame), Top of
contour, Bottom of contour, Relative to the top (depth only).
Absolute (jobframe) (A): The definitions for Top (1) and Depth (2) are absolute values relative to the zero
point of the defined frame (3). They are independent of the actual position of the selected geometries.
Top / Depth (B): The dimension entered relates to the top edge and/or bottom edge of the selected contour
(4).
Relative to top (C): The dimension entered for the depth relates to the defined top of the drill hole (5).

Optimization
Drilling point optimization allows any drilling patterns to be optimized in accordance with various criteria
(not available for the Turning strategy), so that the stresses and heat that are generated during drilling are
distributed as evenly as possible over the entire surface.
hyperMILL generates a graphical feedback of the drilling points that have been selected
for machining. Since a large number of drilling points requires a correspondingly pow-
erful computer to calculate and display this graphical preview, the preview display is
limited to 1000 drilling points by default.
5X Drilling
Two different optimization methods are available for 5-axis drilling.
5X
Frame view: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are calculated from the frame view, while
taking account of the selected drilling strategy. All of the drilling strategies that can be applied during 2D
drilling are available.
5X grouping: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are combined into groups and calculated
according to the shortest distance method. The grouping depends on the tool axis (B axis/C axis) that may
be moved first.
The machining paths from one frame to the next can be checked for collisions (optional) if the correspond-
ing parameter (Setup dialog box) is enabled.
Start
Use start reference: Select a start point, if you want optimization to begin at a defined starting point.
Parameters
Move B axis first / Move C axis first: Control the grouping of drill holes and thus specify the machining
sequence. The drilling points are always processed in a vertical direction first (Z direction of the NCS).
Afterwards, the method for 5X movement is used.
Sorting strategy
Off: Drill holes are machined in the order in which they were selected.
Shortest distance: Machining is carried out starting with the (drilling) point closest to the origin of the
specified coordinate system (frame), followed by the next closest in each case. Select the Use start
reference option to use a start point as the reference for the beginning of the optimization.
Circular: The drill holes to be machined are divided into concentric circle segments starting from a center
point.
X or Y parallel: The drill holes to be machined are divided into segments that are referenced on the X or Y
axis of the selected machining coordinate system (frame).
Contour parallel: The drill holes are machined along the outline of the outer contour of the drilling point
pattern.
More information about the various parameters is provided in the next few chapters.
Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is aligned
with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature
definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
CAM
444

Circular sorting strategy
Start
Use start reference: Define any point as the start point. This start point can be inside or outside of the
drilling point pattern. In this case, machining starts from the defined start reference and moves to the
neighboring point in accordance with the Machining direction and Orientation.
Z optimization
Z optimization: Use the Max. Z depth parameter to specify the conditions for optimized machining of drill
holes at different Z levels. If the distance between two levels is greater than this value, all of the drill holes
on one level are fully machined first before moving to the next level. XY optimization takes place on every
level, while taking account of the relevant starting points.
This method reduces the number of empty paths.
(1) without Z optimization, (2) with Z optimization.

Orientation
The parameters for controlling orientation relate to the machining of the segments.
Clockwise: The segments are machined in clockwise order.
Counterclockwise: The segments are machined in counterclockwise order.
Zigzag: The orientation (clockwise/counterclockwise) is reversed after each segment of the circle.
Machining
Inside-Out: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the inside outwards.
Outside-In: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the outside inwards.
Parameters
Radial width (1): Width of a circle segment, measured from the center of the machining area.
Center point: In order to obtain a correct toolpath calculation, it is essential to define a center point. The
center point to be defined represents the center point of all circle segments that define the machining area.
In the following, the surface between two concentric circles will be referred to as a circle segment. The
term circle segment is not used in
hyperMILL. It is only used in this documentation to describe the drilling
optimization functionality.

Define the machining areas (in addition to definitions on the Contours dialog page), the infeed and

Machining area
Bottom offset: The drill depth is reduced by the specified amount.
Absolute top / Absolute bottom: The defined absolute values are considered in each case. This facilitates
simple machining if the drill hole(s) must be made before the material removal (of the stock model).
Tip angle compensation: Extends the toolpath by the length of the tip so that drill holes can be machined
completely.
Break through length: Extends the toolpath in the axial direction. In the case of a through hole, approach
must continue by this value to ensure that no burring occurs and the thread is completely formed.
The Break through length option is used without taking the bottom type (Flat or
Through) into account. Collisions with the model may occur if the option is used for
blind holes. The Break through length option cannot be used in combination with blind
or through holes if the Check hole function is enabled.

Hole security
These parameters apply for all drilling cycles. They refer to the drill holes of the component.
Clearance distance: (1) Axial distance of the tool to the top of the drill hole during the approach. The
approach takes place as a rapid movement up to the Clearance distance. The tool moves at the feedrate
between the clearance distance and top of the drill hole.

Drilling mode
2D Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is always aligned with the Z axis of the defined frame system.
When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be collision
checked using the Milling area.
2D multi index drilling: the direction of any number of drillings can be aligned with the different frames/
planes. For infeed movements in XY direction, a relative clearance (automatically calculated for each
frame) can be defined. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
5X Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is aligned with the normals of the selected surfaces or with the
selected lines. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be
collision checked using the milling area.
The following applies to multi-axis indexing:
1. In Drilling mode: The frame specifies the machining direction. The linking movements between
the frames are controlled by the postprocessor.
2. In 5X Drilling mode: Several sides can be machined in one job. The linking movements between
the machining sides are checked for collisions and are executed as 5X simultaneous movements.
A machine is required that supports this type of movement.
Turning: With this option, turning jobs can be carried out with a rotating spindle and fixed tool. The
machining direction is defined by the Z axis of the frame. The drill position is always located in the center
point of the workpiece being turned.
Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is aligned
with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature
definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
Drilling in 5X Drilling mode in combination with tool reference points is no longer sup-
ported. If you want to machine with reference points, OPEN MIND recommends using
the2D multi index drilling mode.
Contour selection – general information
Drill positions are selected either directly on the Contours input page or by allocating a previously defined
feature on the Feature input page.
For information on linking features and the machining cycle, see section From job to feature (page 261).
The following CAD geometries are recognized as drill holes:
points,
lines, but no line points (for example, end points), no grid points.
For information on the general procedure for selecting contours, see section Selecting elements in the
CAD system.
You can select all the drill holes for a drilling job that are produced with the same tools and have the same
collision parameters (clearance distance, clearance plane).
Contour selection – 2D Drilling
Lines: The selected contour defines the top and depth of the drill hole. The machining area (top/depth) can
be changed on the dialog page by entering values. Positive values will enlarge the drill hole and negative
values will reduce the size of the drill hole. The direction of the drill hole is determined by the Z-axis of the
defined frame.

contour, Bottom of contour, Relative to the top (depth only).
Absolute (jobframe) (A): The definitions for Top (1) and Depth (2) are absolute values relative to the zero
point of the defined frame (3). They are independent of the actual position of the selected geometries.
Top / Depth (B): The dimension entered relates to the top edge and/or bottom edge of the selected contour
(4).
Relative to top (C): The dimension entered for the depth relates to the defined top of the drill hole (5).

Diameter: Define the required diameter of the drill hole.
Additional distance: Clearance distance for an individual drill hole (as opposed to the clearance distance

Points and surfaces: Set the drill position with the selected points and surfaces and set the direction of the

Lines: The selected contour (line) automatically defines the Top and Depth of the drill hole.
Points and surfaces: Set the drill position with the selected points and surfaces and set the direction using
the frame (Tool dialog page). Enter depth and diameter in the respective field.
Contour selection – Turning
Outer line: The start and end of machining in the Z direction and the machining diameter are specified
(depending on the applied cycle) by defining a contour (outer line).
Base point: The start of machining in the Z direction is specified with the definition of a base point. If
the base point does not lie on the turning axis, it is projected onto the turning axis in the X direction
automatically.
Contour attributes
To define contour attributes (top, bottom), select the machining contour in the contour list. By making
multiple selections in this contour list, you can quickly define the same top and bottom values for several
contours.

Up, (3) Delete, (4) Down, (5) To the bottom.
Optimization
Drilling point optimization allows any drilling patterns to be optimized in accordance with various criteria
(not available for the Turning strategy), so that the stresses and heat that are generated during drilling are
distributed as evenly as possible over the entire surface.
hyperMILL generates a graphical feedback of the drilling points that have been selected
for machining. Since a large number of drilling points requires a correspondingly pow-
erful computer to calculate and display this graphical preview, the preview display is
limited to 1000 drilling points by default.
5X Drilling
Two different optimization methods are available for 5-axis drilling.
5X
Frame view: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are calculated from the frame view, while
taking account of the selected drilling strategy. All of the drilling strategies that can be applied during 2D
drilling are available.
5X grouping: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are combined into groups and calculated
according to the shortest distance method. The grouping depends on the tool axis (B axis/C axis) that may
be moved first.
The machining paths from one frame to the next can be checked for collisions (optional) if the correspond-
ing parameter (Setup dialog box) is enabled.
Start
Use start reference: Select a start point, if you want optimization to begin at a defined starting point.
Parameters
Move B axis first / Move C axis first: Control the grouping of drill holes and thus specify the machining
sequence. The drilling points are always processed in a vertical direction first (Z direction of the NCS).
Afterwards, the method for 5X movement is used.
Sorting strategy
Off: Drill holes are machined in the order in which they were selected.
Shortest distance: Machining is carried out starting with the (drilling) point closest to the origin of the
specified coordinate system (frame), followed by the next closest in each case. Select the Use start
reference option to use a start point as the reference for the beginning of the optimization.
Circular: The drill holes to be machined are divided into concentric circle segments starting from a center
point.
X or Y parallel: The drill holes to be machined are divided into segments that are referenced on the X or Y
axis of the selected machining coordinate system (frame).
Contour parallel: The drill holes are machined along the outline of the outer contour of the drilling point
pattern.
More information about the various parameters is provided in the next few chapters.
CAM
457

-- 457 of 1632 --

Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is aligned
with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature
definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
Circular sorting strategy
Start
Use start reference: Define any point as the start point. This start point can be inside or outside of the
drilling point pattern. In this case, machining starts from the defined start reference and moves to the
neighboring point in accordance with the Machining direction and Orientation.
Z optimization
The Z height of the selected drill holes is taken into account during optimization. Define the value for the
Max. Z depth.
Orientation
The parameters for controlling orientation relate to the machining of the segments.
Clockwise: The segments are machined in clockwise order.
Counterclockwise: The segments are machined in counterclockwise order.
Zigzag: The orientation (clockwise/counterclockwise) is reversed after each segment of the circle.
Machining
Inside-Out: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the inside outwards.
Outside-In: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the outside inwards.
Parameters
Radial width (1): Width of a circle segment, measured from the center of the machining area.
Center point: In order to obtain a correct toolpath calculation, it is essential to define a center point. The
center point to be defined represents the center point of all circle segments that define the machining area.
In the following, the surface between two concentric circles will be referred to as a circle segment. The
term circle segment is not used in
hyperMILL. It is only used in this documentation to describe the drilling
optimization functionality.
Example:
In the example (see illustration), all the drilling points that lie within the radial distance in a circle segment
are machined. In this context, machining continues with the neighboring drilling point. Once all the drilling
points in a circle segment have been processed, the machine moves to the next circle segment.
The machining sequence in the example is: circle segment A, circle segment B, circle segment C. Machin-
ing is clockwise from the outside in.

Orientation
Zigzag: The machining direction of the segments changes after each segment.
Oneway: The segments are always machined in the same direction.
Shortest distance: Machining continues from the last drilling point of a segment to the closest drilling point
in the next segment.
Machining
Revert X: The machining direction oriented on the X axis of the frame coordinate system is reversed.
Revert Y: The machining direction oriented on the Y axis of the frame coordinate system is reversed.
Parameters
Segment width (A): Width of a segment extending in the X or Y direction. Corresponds to the maximum
distance between points in the X or Y direction within a segment.

5X Drilling
Two different optimization methods are available for 5-axis drilling.
5X
Frame view: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are calculated from the frame view, while
taking account of the selected drilling strategy. All of the drilling strategies that can be applied during 2D
drilling are available.
CAM
461

-- 461 of 1632 --

5X grouping: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are combined into groups and calculated
according to the shortest distance method. The grouping depends on the tool axis (B axis/C axis) that may
be moved first.
The machining paths from one frame to the next can be checked for collisions (optional) if the correspond-
ing parameter (Setup dialog box) is enabled.
Start
Use start reference: Select a start point, if you want optimization to begin at a defined starting point.
Parameters
Move B axis first / Move C axis first: Control the grouping of drill holes and thus specify the machining
sequence. The drilling points are always processed in a vertical direction first (Z direction of the NCS).
Afterwards, the method for 5X movement is used.
Z optimization
Z optimization: Use the Max. Z depth parameter to specify the conditions for optimized machining of drill
holes at different Z levels. If the distance between two levels is greater than this value, all of the drill holes
on one level are fully machined first before moving to the next level. XY optimization takes place on every
level, while taking account of the relevant starting points.
This method reduces the number of empty paths.

Machining depth
The drilling depth can be defined in several different ways:
Related to depth: Drilling stops when the specified depth is reached.
Related to diameter: Drilling stops when the specified diameter (< tool diameter!) is reached.
Related to hole diameter: Drilling stops when the specified drill hole diameter is reached.
The drill hole diameter parameter is made up of the Diameter parameter (Contours dialog page) and the
chamfer width.
Top offset mode
Relative offset: Use the Top offset parameter to set the value for the relative offset for centering.
Absolute top: Use the Absolute top parameter or select points on the model to specify the value to start
centering.
With Offset top only, you can limit the offset to the top (start of G1 movement) (1). The Offset centering
complete option defines the offset for the top and depth of the centering (G1 movement) (2).

Model
Definition of the collision checked part of the CAD model. For further information, see section Collision
check preparations (page 139).
Additional surfaces: Temporary safety surfaces to avoid unnecessary rapid travel movements.
For information on the holder/spindle clearance, see section Check tool (page 285).
Check tool
The tool check ensures that all of the components defined for the tool are protected from a possible
collision with the CAD model on the basis of existing material. The tool check is only available if you have
defined a tool and also a model to be checked.
Check on: You must always enable this option if you want the tool to be checked for collisions. If the tool
check is not enabled, the tool used is shown in red in the graphic preview. When this check is enabled,
the defined clearance is used to check all of the components defined for the tool. We recommend that you
define the clearance so that it gets continuously larger, starting with the thick shank in the direction of the
spindle.
Tool check setup: the tool check settings are specified in this dialog box. For further information, see
section Tool check setup (page 722)
Available for the cycles Thread Milling and Tapping:
Check tool tip off: During the tool check for collisions with the CAD model, the tool tip is not considered.
Check tool diameter: The tool diameter is checked for collisions with the CAD model during the tool check.
Use for drill holes with a thread diameter.
Check core diameter: The diameter of the tool core is used during the tool check for collisions with the
CAD model. Use for drill holes with a drilling diameter.
For unresolvable collision
Unresolvable collisions may occur if:
CAM
464

-- 464 of 1632 --

• It is not possible to avoid a collision in 5X machining as a result of a change to the tool orientation.
• In 3D machining, it is not possible to resolve a collision involving the tool extension, holder and/or
spindle by extending the tool (see calculating the tool length) or a collision will occur with the thick
shank.
If a collision cannot be avoided by changing the tool orientation (5X) or tool length calculation, various
options are available for the machining strategies:
Stop: The toolpath calculation stops when a collision occurs (applies for all machining strategies).
NC parameters
Stop before execution: A stop marker in the toolpath causes the tool to stop.
In addition to activating this function, go to the Machine properties → Program halt dialog and enter the
command to stop the tool (by means of M function or command chain). Open the Machine properties
dialog via Job list → Postprocessor → Machine → Machine administration → Edit.
x For the new PP technology (VIRTUAL Machining), open the Virtual Machine configuration
dialog under Machine properties → General → Virtual Machine directory by clicking the icon
and configure the stop of the tool in the NC → General → Output area with the available
options.
Max. angle increment: Vector density for rapid movements at the clearance distance.
Accuracy : Defines the quality of the model (mesh) against which the check takes place.
Check hole: Checks the tool for collisions with the model geometry during the drill movement.
Check tolerance : Defines the permissible violation of the model geometry; the value must be specified as
the radius. Example: with a value of 1, a Ø10 tool can drill a Ø8 hole.
Linking movement
Define the parameters for the linking movements between the drill holes. Only available for the 5X Drilling
drilling mode.
Distance angle limit: Angle difference for various tool inclinations between two separate machining areas
(for example: drilling groups) of a model.
If the defined value (default = 91°) is exceeded or it is equal to the defined value, the linking movement
between the two machining areas takes place at the height of the clearance plane, even if Clearance
distance is defined as the retract mode (Parameters dialog page) (1).
If the angle value falls below the defined value, the linking movement takes place at the height of the
clearance distance (dialog page: Parameters) (2). If there is no angle change, the tool moves rapidly to
clearance distance. If there is no angle change, the tool moves rapidly to clearance distance.
Clearance straighten angle: If the angle between the Z axis of the current machining frame and Z axis of
the tool is greater than the defined straighten angle (default = 45°), the tool turns to the defined value for
the straighten angle, after it has reached the clearance plane.
If the angle between the Z axis of the current machining frame and Z axis of the tool is smaller than or
equal to the defined Straighten angle, the tool moves to the clearance plane without changing the tool
inclination (3).

The clearance straighten angle provides collision avoidance, in particular for machines with conical inter-
polation that allow a 180° vector change
The straighten angle must be defined so that the tip of the tool describes the deepest
point of the entire collision body, including spindle and head. The Z axis of the frame
must be parallel to the NCS Z axis!
Clearance feedrate: Linking movements between two machining areas in the clearance distance are
executed at this feedrate.
Condition for retraction to clearance plane:
Clearance plane is defined as retract mode or value for Clearance straighten angle is exceeded (as
described above).

Z optimization: Use the Max. Z depth parameter to specify the conditions for optimized machining of drill
holes at different Z levels. If the distance between two levels is greater than this value, all of the drill holes
on one level are fully machined first before moving to the next level. XY optimization takes place on every
level, while taking account of the relevant starting points.
This method reduces the number of empty paths.
(1) without Z optimization, (2) with Z optimization.
1 	2
Orientation
The parameters for controlling orientation relate to the machining of the segments.
Clockwise: The segments are machined in clockwise order.
Counterclockwise: The segments are machined in counterclockwise order.
Zigzag: The orientation (clockwise/counterclockwise) is reversed after each segment of the circle.
Machining
Inside-Out: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the inside outwards.
Outside-In: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the outside inwards.
Parameters
Radial width (1): Width of a circle segment, measured from the center of the machining area.
Center point: In order to obtain a correct toolpath calculation, it is essential to define a center point. The
center point to be defined represents the center point of all circle segments that define the machining area.
In the following, the surface between two concentric circles will be referred to as a circle segment. The
term circle segment is not used in
hyperMILL. It is only used in this documentation to describe the drilling
optimization functionality.
CAM

are machined. In this context, machining continues with the neighboring drilling point. Once all the drilling
points in a circle segment have been processed, the machine moves to the next circle segment.
The machining sequence in the example is: circle segment A, circle segment B, circle segment C. Machin-
ing is clockwise from the outside in.

5X Drilling
Two different optimization methods are available for 5-axis drilling.
5X
Frame view: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are calculated from the frame view, while
taking account of the selected drilling strategy. All of the drilling strategies that can be applied during 2D
drilling are available.
5X grouping: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are combined into groups and calculated
according to the shortest distance method. The grouping depends on the tool axis (B axis/C axis) that may
be moved first.
The machining paths from one frame to the next can be checked for collisions (optional) if the correspond-
ing parameter (Setup dialog box) is enabled.
Start
Use start reference: Select a start point, if you want optimization to begin at a defined starting point.
Parameters
Move B axis first / Move C axis first: Control the grouping of drill holes and thus specify the machining
sequence. The drilling points are always processed in a vertical direction first (Z direction of the NCS).
Afterwards, the method for 5X movement is used.
CAM
474

Z optimization: Use the Max. Z depth parameter to specify the conditions for optimized machining of drill
holes at different Z levels. If the distance between two levels is greater than this value, all of the drill holes
on one level are fully machined first before moving to the next level. XY optimization takes place on every
level, while taking account of the relevant starting points.
This method reduces the number of empty paths.
(1) without Z optimization, (2) with Z optimization.

Model
Definition of the collision checked part of the CAD model. For further information, see section Collision

Additional surfaces: Temporary safety surfaces to avoid unnecessary rapid travel movements.
For information on the holder/spindle clearance, see section Check tool (page 285).
Check tool
The tool check ensures that all of the components defined for the tool are protected from a possible
collision with the CAD model on the basis of existing material. The tool check is only available if you have
defined a tool and also a model to be checked.
Check on: You must always enable this option if you want the tool to be checked for collisions. If the tool
check is not enabled, the tool used is shown in red in the graphic preview. When this check is enabled,
the defined clearance is used to check all of the components defined for the tool. We recommend that you
define the clearance so that it gets continuously larger, starting with the thick shank in the direction of the
spindle.
Tool check setup: the tool check settings are specified in this dialog box. For further information, see
section Tool check setup (page 722)
Available for the cycles Thread Milling and Tapping:
Check tool tip off: During the tool check for collisions with the CAD model, the tool tip is not considered.
Check tool diameter: The tool diameter is checked for collisions with the CAD model during the tool check.
Use for drill holes with a thread diameter.
Check core diameter: The diameter of the tool core is used during the tool check for collisions with the
CAD model. Use for drill holes with a drilling diameter.
For unresolvable collision
Unresolvable collisions may occur if:
CAM
476

-- 476 of 1632 --

• It is not possible to avoid a collision in 5X machining as a result of a change to the tool orientation.
• In 3D machining, it is not possible to resolve a collision involving the tool extension, holder and/or
spindle by extending the tool (see calculating the tool length) or a collision will occur with the thick
shank.
If a collision cannot be avoided by changing the tool orientation (5X) or tool length calculation, various
options are available for the machining strategies:
Stop: The toolpath calculation stops when a collision occurs (applies for all machining strategies).
NC parameters
Stop before execution: A stop marker in the toolpath causes the tool to stop.
In addition to activating this function, go to the Machine properties → Program halt dialog and enter the
command to stop the tool (by means of M function or command chain). Open the Machine properties
dialog via Job list → Postprocessor → Machine → Machine administration → Edit.
x For the new PP technology (VIRTUAL Machining), open the Virtual Machine configuration
dialog under Machine properties → General → Virtual Machine directory by clicking the icon
and configure the stop of the tool in the NC → General → Output area with the available
options.
Max. angle increment: Vector density for rapid movements at the clearance distance.
Accuracy : Defines the quality of the model (mesh) against which the check takes place.
Check hole: Checks the tool for collisions with the model geometry during the drill movement.
Check tolerance : Defines the permissible violation of the model geometry; the value must be specified as
the radius. Example: with a value of 1, a Ø10 tool can drill a Ø8 hole.
Linking movement
Define the parameters for the linking movements between the drill holes. Only available for the 5X Drilling
drilling mode.
Distance angle limit: Angle difference for various tool inclinations between two separate machining areas
(for example: drilling groups) of a model.
If the defined value (default = 91°) is exceeded or it is equal to the defined value, the linking movement
between the two machining areas takes place at the height of the clearance plane, even if Clearance
distance is defined as the retract mode (Parameters dialog page) (1).
If the angle value falls below the defined value, the linking movement takes place at the height of the
clearance distance (dialog page: Parameters) (2). If there is no angle change, the tool moves rapidly to
clearance distance. If there is no angle change, the tool moves rapidly to clearance distance.
Clearance straighten angle: If the angle between the Z axis of the current machining frame and Z axis of
the tool is greater than the defined straighten angle (default = 45°), the tool turns to the defined value for
the straighten angle, after it has reached the clearance plane.
If the angle between the Z axis of the current machining frame and Z axis of the tool is smaller than or
equal to the defined Straighten angle, the tool moves to the clearance plane without changing the tool
inclination (3).

The clearance straighten angle provides collision avoidance, in particular for machines with conical inter-
polation that allow a 180° vector change
The straighten angle must be defined so that the tip of the tool describes the deepest
point of the entire collision body, including spindle and head. The Z axis of the frame
must be parallel to the NCS Z axis!
Clearance feedrate: Linking movements between two machining areas in the clearance distance are
executed at this feedrate.
Condition for retraction to clearance plane:
Clearance plane is defined as retract mode or value for Clearance straighten angle is exceeded (as
described above).

deep Hole Drilling cycle.

Contours
Define the drilling strategy, contour selection for the holes and the vertical machining area (top and depth)
of the holes.
Drilling mode
2D Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is always aligned with the Z axis of the defined frame system.
When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be collision
checked using the Milling area.
2D multi index drilling: the direction of any number of drillings can be aligned with the different frames/
planes. For infeed movements in XY direction, a relative clearance (automatically calculated for each
frame) can be defined. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
5X Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is aligned with the normals of the selected surfaces or with the
selected lines. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be
collision checked using the milling area.
The following applies to multi-axis indexing:
1. In Drilling mode: The frame specifies the machining direction. The linking movements between
the frames are controlled by the postprocessor.
2. In 5X Drilling mode: Several sides can be machined in one job. The linking movements between
the machining sides are checked for collisions and are executed as 5X simultaneous movements.
A machine is required that supports this type of movement.
Turning: With this option, turning jobs can be carried out with a rotating spindle and fixed tool. The
machining direction is defined by the Z axis of the frame. The drill position is always located in the center
point of the workpiece being turned.
Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is aligned
with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature
definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
Drilling in 5X Drilling mode in combination with tool reference points is no longer sup-
ported. If you want to machine with reference points, OPEN MIND recommends using
the2D multi index drilling mode.

Contour selection – general information
Drill positions are selected either directly on the Contours input page or by allocating a previously defined
feature on the Feature input page.
For information on linking features and the machining cycle, see section From job to feature (page 261).
The following CAD geometries are recognized as drill holes:
points,
lines, but no line points (for example, end points), no grid points.
For information on the general procedure for selecting contours, see section Selecting elements in the
CAD system.
You can select all the drill holes for a drilling job that are produced with the same tools and have the same
collision parameters (clearance distance, clearance plane).
Contour selection – 2D Drilling
Lines: The selected contour defines the top and depth of the drill hole. The machining area (top/depth) can
be changed on the dialog page by entering values. Positive values will enlarge the drill hole and negative
values will reduce the size of the drill hole. The direction of the drill hole is determined by the Z-axis of the
defined frame.
Points: The following methods are available for defining the top and depth: Absolute (job frame), Top of
contour, Bottom of contour, Relative to the top (depth only).
Absolute (jobframe) (A): The definitions for Top (1) and Depth (2) are absolute values relative to the zero
point of the defined frame (3). They are independent of the actual position of the selected geometries.
Top / Depth (B): The dimension entered relates to the top edge and/or bottom edge of the selected contour
(4).
Relative to top (C): The dimension entered for the depth relates to the defined top of the drill hole (5).

Additional distance: Clearance distance for an individual drill hole (as opposed to the clearance distance
parameter on the Parameters dialog page) when collision check is disabled.
Points and surfaces: Set the drill position with the selected points and surfaces and set the direction of the
drill hole using the frame. Enter depth and diameter in the respective field.
Contour selection – 2D multi index drilling
Lines: The selected contour (line) automatically defines the Top and Depth of the drill hole.
Points and surfaces: Set the drill position with the selected points and surfaces and set the direction using
the frame (Tool dialog page). Enter depth and diameter in the respective field.
Contour selection – Turning
Outer line: The start and end of machining in the Z direction and the machining diameter are specified
(depending on the applied cycle) by defining a contour (outer line).
Base point: The start of machining in the Z direction is specified with the definition of a base point. If
the base point does not lie on the turning axis, it is projected onto the turning axis in the X direction
automatically.
Contour attributes
To define contour attributes (top, bottom), select the machining contour in the contour list. By making
multiple selections in this contour list, you can quickly define the same top and bottom values for several
contours.
Use the following buttons to change the order of selected contours or delete a contour. (1) To the top, (2)
Up, (3) Delete, (4) Down, (5) To the bottom.
Optimization
Drilling point optimization allows any drilling patterns to be optimized in accordance with various criteria
(not available for the Turning strategy), so that the stresses and heat that are generated during drilling are
distributed as evenly as possible over the entire surface.
hyperMILL generates a graphical feedback of the drilling points that have been selected
for machining. Since a large number of drilling points requires a correspondingly pow-
erful computer to calculate and display this graphical preview, the preview display is
limited to 1000 drilling points by default.
5X Drilling
Two different optimization methods are available for 5-axis drilling.
5X
Frame view: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are calculated from the frame view, while
taking account of the selected drilling strategy. All of the drilling strategies that can be applied during 2D
drilling are available.
5X grouping: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are combined into groups and calculated
according to the shortest distance method. The grouping depends on the tool axis (B axis/C axis) that may
be moved first.
The machining paths from one frame to the next can be checked for collisions (optional) if the correspond-
ing parameter (Setup dialog box) is enabled.

Start
Use start reference: Select a start point, if you want optimization to begin at a defined starting point.
Parameters
Move B axis first / Move C axis first: Control the grouping of drill holes and thus specify the machining
sequence. The drilling points are always processed in a vertical direction first (Z direction of the NCS).
Afterwards, the method for 5X movement is used.
Sorting strategy
Off: Drill holes are machined in the order in which they were selected.
Shortest distance: Machining is carried out starting with the (drilling) point closest to the origin of the
specified coordinate system (frame), followed by the next closest in each case. Select the Use start
reference option to use a start point as the reference for the beginning of the optimization.
Circular: The drill holes to be machined are divided into concentric circle segments starting from a center
point.
X or Y parallel: The drill holes to be machined are divided into segments that are referenced on the X or Y
axis of the selected machining coordinate system (frame).
Contour parallel: The drill holes are machined along the outline of the outer contour of the drilling point
pattern.
More information about the various parameters is provided in the next few chapters.
Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is aligned
with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature
definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
Circular sorting strategy

drilling point pattern. In this case, machining starts from the defined start reference and moves to the
neighboring point in accordance with the Machining direction and Orientation.

Z optimization: Use the Max. Z depth parameter to specify the conditions for optimized machining of drill
holes at different Z levels. If the distance between two levels is greater than this value, all of the drill holes
on one level are fully machined first before moving to the next level. XY optimization takes place on every
level, while taking account of the relevant starting points.
This method reduces the number of empty paths.

Contours
Define the drilling strategy, contour selection for the holes and the vertical machining area (top and depth)
of the holes.
Drilling mode
2D Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is always aligned with the Z axis of the defined frame system.
When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be collision
checked using the Milling area.
2D multi index drilling: the direction of any number of drillings can be aligned with the different frames/
planes. For infeed movements in XY direction, a relative clearance (automatically calculated for each
frame) can be defined. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
5X Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is aligned with the normals of the selected surfaces or with the
selected lines. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be
collision checked using the milling area.
The following applies to multi-axis indexing:
1. In Drilling mode: The frame specifies the machining direction. The linking movements between
the frames are controlled by the postprocessor.
2. In 5X Drilling mode: Several sides can be machined in one job. The linking movements between
the machining sides are checked for collisions and are executed as 5X simultaneous movements.
A machine is required that supports this type of movement.
Turning: With this option, turning jobs can be carried out with a rotating spindle and fixed tool. The
machining direction is defined by the Z axis of the frame. The drill position is always located in the center
point of the workpiece being turned.
Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is aligned
with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature
definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.
Drilling in 5X Drilling mode in combination with tool reference points is no longer sup-
ported. If you want to machine with reference points, OPEN MIND recommends using
the2D multi index drilling mode.

Contour selection – general information
Drill positions are selected either directly on the Contours input page or by allocating a previously defined
feature on the Feature input page.
For information on linking features and the machining cycle, see section From job to feature (page 261).
The following CAD geometries are recognized as drill holes:
points,
lines, but no line points (for example, end points), no grid points.
For information on the general procedure for selecting contours, see section Selecting elements in the
CAD system.
You can select all the drill holes for a drilling job that are produced with the same tools and have the same
collision parameters (clearance distance, clearance plane).
Contour selection – 2D Drilling
Lines: The selected contour defines the top and depth of the drill hole. The machining area (top/depth) can
be changed on the dialog page by entering values. Positive values will enlarge the drill hole and negative
values will reduce the size of the drill hole. The direction of the drill hole is determined by the Z-axis of the
defined frame.
Points: The following methods are available for defining the top and depth: Absolute (job frame), Top of
contour, Bottom of contour, Relative to the top (depth only).
Absolute (jobframe) (A): The definitions for Top (1) and Depth (2) are absolute values relative to the zero
point of the defined frame (3). They are independent of the actual position of the selected geometries.
Top / Depth (B): The dimension entered relates to the top edge and/or bottom edge of the selected contour
(4).
Relative to top (C): The dimension entered for the depth relates to the defined top of the drill hole (5).

Points and surfaces: Set the drill position with the selected points and surfaces and set the direction of the
