Interfaces
Interfaces to the following tool management systems are supported in the OPEN MIND tool database:
• TDM Systems
• WinTool
• Zoller
• NCSIMUL | Tool
TDM Systems integration
Manage the exchange of data with the TDM Systems tool management system using the TDM Systems
integration.
Set up the TDM Systems database from the following dialog: hyperMILL → Setup → hyperMILL → settings
→ Database → Settings Wizard.
Import tools from the TDM Systems database
1. Open the TDM Systems database
via the entry CAM → Utilities → Import TDM Systems tools or
via the job definition, job browser or tool browser.
2. Click a tool icon to first select the required tool type and then the tools to be imported.
If the TDM Systems database was opened from the job dialog, then only the tool type already
selected in the job dialog is selectable.
Tools which were imported using the TDM Tool Manager can be used in macro pro-
gramming. A prerequisite is that the tools are saved in the database as an NC tool with
a unique ID. In the Apply macro dialog, NC tools used in macro jobs which come from
the tool database and have a unique ID are marked as DB.
Export tools to the TDM Systems database
1. Open the TDM Systems database via the menu hyperMILL → Tools → TDM Systems tools.
2. Define the name of the tool list to be exported using List ID.
Either all local tools defined in the ( *.hmc) model file are exported or all tools in a job
list. To only export the tools in a job list, select the respective job list beforehand.
WinTool integration
The WinTool integration enables data exchange with the WinTool tool management system and is availa-
ble via the CAM → Utilities menu.
It is possible to access complete tools and tool lists directly from
hyperMILL. The tools exported from
WinTool are not written to the OPENMIND tool database, but directly to the
hyperMILL document. This
way, a redundant tool management system is avoided.
To enable the WinTool integration, right-click the CAD program’s toolbar and select WinTool hyperMILL
Interface.
CAM
1558

-- 1558 of 1632 --

Import tools from the WinTool database
During the exchange of data between WinTool and
hyperMILL, the existing tool IDs are checked. When
importing tools from WinTool,
hyperMILL assigns NC numbers automatically. The next NC number is the
highest existing number + 1.
Export tools to the WinTool database
Using the WT-MakeList function, all tools used in a hyperMILL document are adopted in a list and
exported to WinTool. The list consists of a set of IDs and NC numbers for each tool used.
For more information on the functions of WinTool integration, see your WinTool documentation.
Zoller integration
The Zoller integration enables data exchange with the Zoller tool management system and is available via
the CAM → Utilities menu.
Import tools from the Zoller database
Open the Zoller database dialog to choose the tools that are to be imported to
hyperMILL. The imported
tools are automatically entered in the tool list of the current document.
Export tools to the Zoller database
All tools used in the document are exported to the Zoller database. If the document contains multiple
job lists, a usage list is created for each job list of the document
Import and export are available only if the Zoller TMS has been started.
NCSIMUL | Tool
The NCSIMUL | Tool integration enables data exchange with the NCSIMUL | Tool tool management
system and is available via the CAM → Utilities menu.
Import tools from the NCSIMUL | Tool database.
Open the NCSIMUL | Tool database dialog to choose the tools that are to be imported to
hyperMILL.

hyperVIEW
hyperVIEW’s basic functions include:
• Display of the toolpaths and control of the tool's movements.
• Machine simulation based on toolpaths.
• The generation of NC files.
• The generation of reports.
• Print functions.
This documentation provides you with:
• A brief overview of the basic functions in the following section.
• Information on the screen layout in section User interface (page 1562).
• A brief summary of the most important workflows in section Important workflows (page 1563).
• Detailed descriptions of the individual functions on the menu in section Menu functions (page 1567).
• Descriptions of the
hyperVIEW browser functions in section Functions in the hyperVIEW brows-
er (page 1573).
• Information on the toolbars in section Toolbars (page 1595).
User interface
The user interface consists of the following elements:
(1) Menu bar, (2) Toolbars, (3) Browser, (4) Graphics area, (5) Status bar.
CAM
1562

-- 1562 of 1632 --

Important workflows
Important workflows are outlined below.
Set up machine
For much of the work carried out, you need to specify a machine to use for simulations. Therefore, when
you start
hyperVIEW for the first time, you will be prompted to set up a machine.
Proceed as follows to set up a machine:
1. Open the Machine administration dialog.
2. Alternatively, open the Machine administration dialog via the job list in
hyperMILL ( Postprocessor
→ Machine).
3. Specify the machine's name and postprocessor in the Common category of the Machine proper-
ties dialog.
The postprocessor's parameters need to be suitably configured before it is used for the
first time. Please contact your OPEN MIND dealer to get information regarding this.
Proceed as follows to modify a postprocessor's configuration:
1. Open the Postprocessor configuration dialog and, if necessary, change the name, type and
value of individual parameters.
2. Make sure to document all changes made in the configuration dialog!
Model mode: Specify whether a machine model is to be used for the simulation or whether only the part
and tool are to be displayed. If a machine is used, define the format of the machine model file.
Model from MMF file / VMM file: Select if a machine is to be displayed in
hyperVIEW.
Select the machine model file. The settings for Model from VMM file correspond to the settings for the
Fixed part option.
Model from postprocessor: Select if the postprocessor ( *.oma) contains a machine model. Only licensed
tool machine models can be used. For more information on this, please contact your OPEN MIND partner.
Please note that these machine models are not assured to match any particular ma-
chine in your machine shop. Functions like collision control and workspace monitor may
vary from our typical model to your actual machine. OPEN MIND or your OPEN MIND
partner can adjust the machine to your particular requirements. This service, which does
not form part of the standard delivery, is charged separately.
Fixed part / Fixed tool: Select if there is no machine model or if the machine model is irrelevant to the
simulation. Only the part and the tool are displayed in the simulation; one of the two needs to be fixed.
Generate NC program
Proceed as follows to write an NC file:
1. Define machine.
CAM
1563

2. Create an NC job (right-click > Create NC job).
hyperVIEW creates an entry in the browser
consisting of the following elements: machine, several parts (stock, model, result) and toolpaths.
3. Insert a toolpath (select the Toolpath entry in the browser, right-click and select > Insert toolpath).
4. Start the postprocessor run (select the NC job entry, right-click and select > Write NC-File).
The postprocessor run terminates with an error message if no license is found.
OPEN MIND has enhanced the postprocessor run to include an analysis of the postpro-
cessor. The following message appears if a security-related issue is detected:
Important note on your postprocessor. OPEN MIND detected a security issue. Please
contact your OPEN MIND business partner.
Set up machine simulation
Proceed as follows to set up the machine simulation:
1. Define machine.
2. Create an NC job and insert toolpath.
3. Define the machine simulation conditions. To do this, switch to the Simulation tab in the browser
and specify the required settings.
Machine origin: If you select the Automatic option, the parts used and the toolpaths will
be positioned automatically. Use Machine Setup to define other origins.

Generate report
Generate a report for tool lists, job lists or statistical information (tool movements, dwell times, coolants
and so on) in the formats *.htm, *.rtf, *.txt and *. xml (for Excel 2002).
Proceed as follows to create a report:
1. On the File menu, select the Report entry or select the NC job entry in the browser, right-click and
select the Report option.
2. In the Report dialog, select the required format and a template file.
3. Specify a path and file name and save the file.
For the generated report file to open automatically, you need to select the Show report after generation
option on the Options → General menu.
Reports including statistical evaluations can only be created if in
hyperMILL (job definition > General dialog
page) the Generate NC file option is enabled.
Use a text editor to customize script files ( *.JLR) for modifying the content of report files according to
your individual requirements.
Print information
Print information on the NC file, machine, tool parameters or machining cycles for an NC job.
Define print layout
To define the print and CSV layout:
1. On the Options menu, select the Print and CSV Layout entry.
2. Select the <new layout> option and specify a name.
3. Define the printing values (double-click the Available values column).
4. Use the arrow keys to specify the order of the values.
5. Click OK to confirm the print and CSV layout.
Print
To print the layout:
1. Select Print from the File menu.
2. In the Print dialog, define the printer, print area and layout.
3. Click OK to close the Print dialog.

CSV format: The defined parameters are saved in a text file with comma separators between the values.
This format enables further editing in a spreadsheet program such as Excel.
To generate a file in *.CSV format:
1. Select CSV from the File menu.
2. Select the storage location, file name, file type and layout.
3. Click Save to close the dialog.
Menu functions
File
Open: Open files in the format *.hv or *.hvz. When you open *.hvz files, the files contained in the

not deleted.
Save as: Save a file in the format:
*.hv: With this file type, information about the machine, stock, model and toolpaths is linked to an NC job.
All of the NC jobs in the browser are saved.

data can still be added at a later point.
*.hvz: All of the files associated with a project file (*.hv) are saved together in a ZIP file with the following
file structure:
NC-Job X
- 3DF/
- POF/
- STOCK/
- NC/
NC-Job Y
With postprocessor: Include the postprocessor in the .hvz file. This includes all *.def files that are
located in the same directory as the postprocessor ( .oma file).
With machine model: Include the machine model in the .hvz file.
The options are important for the OPEN MIND support team and are enabled by default.
Unpack Archive: Unpack all the files associated with the project file (that is also contained in the ZIP
archive) to the selected directory.

NCS transformation
Define a predetermined offset for the NCS. First, the rotation is executed, followed by the displacement.
Thus, a displacement refers to the rotated NCS. A warning is issued in this context when loading data in
hyperVIEW and during the postprocessor run.
Select the Enabled checkbox to turn the NCS transformation on. X offset moves the NCS in the direction
of the X axis, Y offset in the direction of the Y axis and Z offset in the direction of the Z axis. A value must
be entered for the required distance. Rotary axis determines the axis of the NCS around which the NCS is
to be turned. Rotation angle defines the value for the rotation. It is applied only if the rotation axis has the
value x, y or z.

14. Appendix
ReportDesigner
Introduction
The OPEN MIND ReportDesigner provides the user with a tool to adjust the display of joblist-based or tool
list-based documentation (reports) from
hyperMILL to the requirements of their particular company.
Content may be adjusted in the sense of the scope of the data to be returned in the report as well as its
sequence, text format, color and other properties regarding the display of this data.
Initial Steps
The user can use the ReportDesigner to prepare a report layout in the form of an XSL file. The report
layout consists of a hierarchical structure of visible elements such as tables, images, text areas, and so on,
and of logical elements such as conditions, loops and placeholders for the actual dataset of the report.
Menu and Toolbar
The ReportDesigner is a typical editor program, i.e. the user uses it to open a file, makes changes to that
file, and then saves the results as a file.
After opening the file, an element must first be selected from the structure. This can then be copied, moved
and removed. Other functions may be possible depending on the currently selected element, such as
editing the specific properties and adding possible child elements.
A separate menu is available to insert specific new elements into the structure, while important elements
can also be inserted directly from the toolbar. The Tools menu item contains additional complex functions
which may become necessary in some situations.
Creating a New Report
A range of report layouts for various types and languages are installed together with
hyperMILL and are
available to the user immediately and directly within
hyperMILL.
It is often sufficient to simply adjust these templates to your company's requirements. However, in some
cases it may also be necessary to design a report layout from scratch.
The dialog for this task can be found in the File > New menu item. The report type, e.g. a joblist report, the
language and the output format, are all specified in this dialog.
Preview Area
The left area of the ReportDesigner is used to display a preview of the report output with placeholders rep-
resenting the actual data. Changes to the structure or properties of an element are updated immediately in
the preview.
Structure View
The right area, known as the structure view, is used to edit a report layout. In this area, the user can select
an element to edit its properties, as well as add new elements if necessary.
The context inside the report dataset, which is referenced e.g. when inserting placeholders, appears above
the tree.
Logical elements, such as placeholders and loops, are highlighted blue in the tree view while visible
elements are displayed in normal black.
It is possible to make direct changes to the properties of visible and logical elements in the lower Proper-
ties dialog.
CAM
1598

-- 1598 of 1632 --

Properties Dialog
The properties of the various elements in the structure of a report layout can be adjusted in the Properties
dialog.
For visible elements ( p, div, span, th, td, ...), it is possible to change text properties such as font, size,
bold/italic, color, margins, borders and alignment. Other visible elements such as tables (table) and images
(img) have other changeable properties.
The CSS Styles tab is additionally available for all visible elements. This tab is used to clearly show and
also, if necessary, change the display of the element.
Logical elements ( xsl:if, xsl:for-each, xsl:value-of, ...) also have specific attributes which can be individual-
ly adjusted here.
Test Execution
Particularly at the beginning, it can make sense to directly test even small changes to the report layout,
that is, generate an actual report using the modified report layout. For this purpose, the File menu contains
the Execute menu item. Enter the path to the Report Generator (
hyperMILL installation directory) and the
report dataset (for a job list, the file extension is .rda) here. Your company may also use a shared image
directory. Specify this directory under Images.
Visible Elements
The visible elements in a report layout correspond to the well-known HTML format. Users familiar with
HTML will quickly come to grips with these concepts.
Text Areas and Properties
The main text area in the ReportDesigner is the paragraph ( p). A paragraph initially only contains the
letters of the text contained inside this paragraph.
The format properties for the paragraph can be displayed and if necessary changed by selecting the p in
the structure view. Note that every change affects the entire paragraph.
If the user wants to highlight a single word in bold or italic, for example, a separate structure element must
first be inserted into a text range ( span) for this specific purpose and then formatted with the bold or italic
property.
Cells in a table or positions in a list can also be regarded as text ranges and their format properties
adjusted correspondingly.
The following displays typical Text properties.
CAM
1599

-- 1599 of 1632 --

Borders
Margins
CSS styles
CAM
1600

-- 1600 of 1632 --

Element properties
Tables, rows and columns
Tables are an important visible element for the display of values in a report. Tables are suitable to
graphically structure the overall output of a report, as well as to list the individual values of a dataset.
Tables ( table) are divided into an optional header area ( thead) and one or more table body areas
( tbody).
The header area can be used to e.g. display the headings of a tabular list, while the values can be
specified as a placeholder using a loop ( xsl:for-each) in the rows ( tr) and columns ( td) of a table body.
In this way, you can generate a tabular list of the used tools with the respective tool properties.
Another function of tables is to specify the display areas inside a page. To do so, the dimensions of the
columns are specified explicitly, e.g. a table with a width of 100% can be divided into three columns with
widths of 25%, 50% and 25%. It is alternatively possible to specify widths in pixels using the abbreviation
px. In this way, the user can divide the page into several display areas and position images or text ranges
as needed. Further structure elements can then be hierarchically created inside the display areas.
Simple and Numbered Lists
The ReportDesigner provides functions for ordered and unordered lists. The difference is simply in the
numbering of the list elements, i.e. ordered lists are automatically numbered as 1, 2, 3, ... or A, B, C, ...
Images and Graphics
Image files in the GIF, PNG and JPG formats can be integrated into the report layout in the ReportDesign-
er as static images ( img). Images can also be dynamically embedded for tools. This means that images of
the tools are automatically created during report generation and shown in the report output.
The difference between static and dynamic images is that the paths to static images do not change
and they can therefore be fixed in the report layout. Dynamic images relate to a specific job or tool, for
example, and are read from the report dataset and entered in the report layout using a placeholder.
Logical Elements
In addition to visible elements, which are used to format the report output, the ReportDesigner also
provides a range of logical elements, which can be used to embed the data from a job list or tool dataset in
the report output.
Note that the underlying dataset of e.g. a job list is hierarchically structured in its own right. The Report-
Designer helps the user insert placeholders and loops by only making properties and possible loops
belonging to the current data element available for selection, depending on the context.
Placeholders
Job lists, jobs, tools and other data elements have specific properties such as designation, numbering,
length, color etc.
CAM
1601

-- 1601 of 1632 --

Depending on the context in the report dataset, the user can insert individual properties of, for example, a
job into the report layout using a placeholder ( xsl:value-of). The possible job properties are made available
in the selection dialog, and are then applied to the placeholder's select attribute.
Placeholders can be inserted from the Insert > Value Of ... menu item.
The possible attributes, in this case those of the tool, are selected depending on the context in the report
dataset.
Sometimes it may be necessary to specifically access properties of the superordinate element or other
elements in the report dataset, or formatting functions. The ReportDesigner uses the xpath query language
for this purpose, which means that the user can enter arbitrary other xpath expressions in the select
attribute with knowledge of the structure of the dataset.
xsl and xpath offer an enormous range of options, which are not described in further detail here. A number
of tutorials and a wide range of documentation are available on the Internet.
Loops and Repetition
Every report dataset is built around a hierarchical structure. A job list, for example, consists of a list of
individual jobs and an additional list of used tools.
A list of jobs can be visualized in a number of ways, e.g. as an overview in a table or as a list of pages,
each of which shows an individual job.
For display, it is first necessary to create a loop to cover all jobs in the job list. In the first example case,
this loop is used to display the table rows.
In the second case, each iteration of the loop displays an entire page. Loops are available under the Insert
> For all ... menu item.
Because tables with a loop structure are required in many cases, the Tools menu contains the Dynamic
table menu item to bring these common steps together in one place.
CAM
1602

-- 1602 of 1632 --

The following structure is inserted:
Conditions
Inside the loop, it may be necessary to only display certain elements, for example jobs with a particular
property. To achieve this, the user can use a condition to filter the output. The Insert > Condition menu
item allows such filters to be inserted.
CAM
1603

-- 1603 of 1632 --

Additional functions
The Tools menu in the ReportDesigner contains a few special functions for the calculation of certain
values.
MinTlength
The MinTlength function is used to output the shortest length of a tool in a job list. If a tool is used several
times, only the tool with the shortest required length will be used. This prevents tools from being output
multiple times.
Zmax-Zmin
Output of the relative and axial heights of a tool path ( z-height).
System Requirements
• Internet Explorer 8
• MS Office 2007 or higher
• Windows XP, Windows Vista, Windows 7
FAQs / Contacting your OPEN MIND partner
The information in this document is addressed to all
hyperMILL users. It provides tips and answers
to questions in the event of unexpected problems that may arise when working with
hyperMILL. The
information also complements the documentation and training materials that you are familiar with.
Frequently asked questions
The first section provides you with additional tips and tricks (divided into subject areas) for the efficient use
of
hyperMILL.
CAM
1604

-- 1604 of 1632 --

If you cannot solve your problem by means of the FAQs, please contact the OPEN MIND support or
your OPEN MIND partner. In order to be able to process your request quickly and efficiently plus resolve
your problem as quickly as possible, we require some information from you, which is summarised in
section ???.
hyperMILL installation
Licensing / Registration
hyperMILL
I purchased a
hyperMILL license, but the
hyperMILL browser cannot be opened and the following mes-
sage appears:
hyperMILL [version] is not licensed on this computer! Unable to execute the requested command!
Make sure the license is intended for the installed version. Make sure the dongle is installed and recog-
nized correctly. Please find information on activating your
hyperMILL license in the installation guide,
chapter 8 Activate and Manage OPEN MIND License Manager Products.
OPEN MIND direct interfaces
I have bought a license for the OPEN MIND direct interfaces, but the toolbar for the interfaces is not
available.
Check on the Activation code tab of your OPEN MIND License Manager whether you have activated the
direct interfaces for your dongle. Please find information on activation in the Activate and Manage OPEN
MIND License Manager Products section of your installation guide.
Post Processors
New post processor
I have got a new post processor. How to proceed?
1. Follow notes
Please pay attention to the notes that are enclosed with the postprocessor delivery. If necessary,
please consult your OPEN MIND partner.
2. Installation
For information on installing a postprocessor, see section Set up machine (page 1569).
3. Adapt configuration file
Before using the postprocessor for the first time, please adapt all parameters of the configuration
file ( *.def file) belonging to the postprocessor that are especially important for your purposes.
The adaptation of the configuration file is a continuous process. Depending on the frequency of
the usage of the postprocessor with different tool path files, this process can take several months,
if necessary.
4. Testing
Please test the new postprocessor with typical toolpaths [according to your usual requirements].
Please don't use a current project for this, but (if possible) please use preferably a workpiece,
which is not used for commercial purposes.
If only a commercial workpiece is available, please only use toolpaths that maintain a defined
distance to the workpiece for testing.
First, please test single toolpaths, i.e., single jobs without tool changes. Afterwards, the testing
procedure can be enhanced and the single jobs tested before, can be tested with machining
priority including tool change.
Post processor update
I have received an update of an post processor. How to proceed?
CAM
1605

-- 1605 of 1632 --

To implement the current changes of your post processor, please proceed as follows:
1. Back up
Please first back up the existing postprocessor files to prevent them from being unintentionally
overwritten by the newly provided postprocessor files. Doing so means that the original postpro-
cessor files will be available as backup files further on.
2. Apply adjustments to update
Please also include the adjustments made to the postprocessor's configuration file(s) in the
postprocessor update. If necessary, please consult your OPEN MIND partner.
The configuration file is a text file. You can compare the updated file with the
existing file und let display the differences into a textfile editor.
3. Adjust specified path
If you saved the updated postprocessor files (oma files) in another directory (different from the
directory usually used) or if you renamed the updated file, you also need to adjust the path in the
machine administration of
hyperVIEW (on the
hyperVIEW menu in Edit → Machine administration
→ New → General → Machine properties → Postprocessor).
Please always save the updated files in a separate directory to prevent them
from being overwritten by accident. Please inform the administrator of your
hyperMILL installation about the updated postprocessor, so that the adminis-
trator can use the latest postprocessor file for subsequent installations, for
example, after a new
hyperMILL release. If the updated postprocessor is used
by a number of people in your company, all the people concerned should be
informed about every update.
4. Testing
Postprocessor updates have to be tested (as is the case with new postprocessors).
Automatic postprocessor updates
Are updates automatically shipped?
No. Updates are neither generated automatically nor shipped. Therefore you should contact your OPEN
MIND partner once a year, to find out about the availability of a postprocessor update.
Adjustments to the postprocessor
I want to have a adjustment of the NC output of the post processor? How to proceed?
Please contact your OPEN MIND partner. The information, named in the following is required for handling
your request:
1. Which postprocessor should be updated?
Please use the function in
hyperVIEW Machine properties → Postprocessor → Info.
You can copy all the information shown in the Postprocessor Information dialog directly to the
clipboard and save it to a text file.
2. Create hvz file (including NC file).
Please generate an hvz file from all operations (jobs) that you have postprocessed together.
Please make sure to generate this hvz file after postprocessing in order to ensure that the
corresponding NC file exists.
3. Document desired changes.
Please document the desired change using a specific
hyperMILL project and inform your OPEN
MIND partner in detail about all functions you wish to have in the new postprocessor.
For this purpose, please generate a new NC file and also a text file that describes the desired
changes (please use the corresponding machine and/or the CNC control manuals, if necessary).
CAM
1606

-- 1606 of 1632 --

Please note: Adjustments to a postprocessor may incur additional fees! Your
OPEN MIND partner will inform you, before expenses are incurred.
4. CAD file
In some cases, the CAD file (including job list) from which you generated the hvz file (see section
b) may be required. Please also provide this data to your OPEN MIND partner on request.
Postprocessor and new
hyperMILL
Do I have to install a new postprocessor after a new
hyperMILL release?
OPEN MIND endeavors to ensure compatibility with existing postprocessors with its new releases. Howev-
er, you can check the behavior of the postprocessors after the introduction of a new
hyperMILL release.
We recommend doing this based on the last project that was edited and postprocessed before the
new
hyperMILL release went live. If the toolpaths are not recalculated in the new
hyperMILL release,
the new
hyperMILL release should generate exactly the same NC programs. Furthermore, OPEN MIND
recommends that you check the toolpaths typically used in your applications.
Examples: If you primarily program 2D toolpaths with
hyperMILL, you should check some of the 2D
toolpaths. If you primarily generate 5X machinings, please compare some 5X toolpaths.
However, if the results deviate from the usual NC output in a new release, please first check if the postpro-
cessor files last provided for
hyperMILL were installed by your administrator when the new
hyperMILL
release was implemented.
Please also contact your OPEN MIND partner and inform him or her about this incompatible behavior fol-
lowing the installation of a new
hyperMILL release. Your OPEN MIND partner will analyze the incompatible
behavior and provide further information.
Furthermore, after installing a new
hyperMILL release, you should check whether a new postprocessor
release is also be available.
Postprocessor and new dongle
What is to consider when exchanging the dongle?
If you don't have new post processor files, please contact your OPEN MIND partner and provide all current
dongle information. Please note: it may take a number of days to provide you with these files.
Contact OPEN MIND partner
If you cannot find a solution for your problem in the FAQ list, please contact your OPEN MIND partner. To
enable us to deal with your request quickly and efficiently, please provide the following information:
Version numbers
Version number of the operating system
You can obtain the version number of your Windows operating system by doing the following:
1. Right-click the Windows Start icon and then select System. Save the Show basic information
about this computer section as a screenshot or
2. enter winver in the input field to the right of the Windows Start icon, start the winver program and
save the screenshot.
Version number of the CAD system
Proceed as follows to obtain the version number of your CAD system:
Click Help → About... on the menu bar of your CAD system. [Name of the CAD system].
CAM
1607

-- 1607 of 1632 --

Autodesk Inventor
SolidWorks
hyperMILL
Proceed as follows to obtain the
hyperMILL version number:
1. On the menu bar, click hyperMILL → Info → About hyperMILL.
2. Afterwards, click the Version details... button and save the verDetails.txt file.
hyperView /OPEN MIND tool database
Proceed as follows to obtain the version number of
hyperVIEW or the OPEN MIND tool database:
Click the question mark on the menu bar and select About hyperView or Information about OPEN MIND
Tool Database.
CAD and hvz file
As a preparative measure, please generate a copy of the corresponding CAD file. In case of large job lists:
adjust them by deleting the non relevant jobs.
Now back up all relevant 3DF, model, stock and, if necessary, NC files by transferring the job to
hy-
perVIEW. To do this, select the job in the
hyperMILL browser and choose the Utilities → hyperVIEW option
on the shortcut menu.
Save the job in
hyperVIEW as an archive file ( File → Save as) in *.hvz format. The files are combined
into a single zip file. Please provide this file to your OPEN MIND partner together with the CAD file.
Please note: A model file ( *.OMX) will only be transferred to
hyperVIEW if you have assigned the file to
the corresponding job list previously in
hyperMILL.
To do so, please highlight the job list and choose the Edit job list... entry. Now select the Part data tab in
the Job list dialog, activate the Defined option and choose the corresponding model file from the list. Exit
the dialog by clicking OK.
Short problem description
When the problem did occur (action) and what happened exactly? It is also helpful to supplement your
description using screenshots (if necessary, also of
hyperMILL messages).

NLopt
README
NLopt is a library for nonlinear local and global optimization, for functions with and without gradient infor-
mation. It is designed as as simple, unified interface and packaging of several free/open-source nonlinear
optimization libraries.
The latest release and a complete manual may be found at the NLopt home page: http://ab-initio.mit.edu/
nlopt
It is compiled and installed with the standard GNU autoconf/automake commands:
./configure
make
make install
See `./configure --help` or the `INSTALL` file for other options. To build the latest development sources:
git clone git://github.com/stevengj/nlopt
cd nlopt
sh autogen.sh
make
(To build from git, you will need GNU autoconf, automake, and libtool installed, along with SWIG and Unix
tools such as m4, perl, and sed.)
Once it is installed, `#include <nlopt.h>` in your C/C++ programs and link it with `-lnlopt -lm`. You may
need to use the C++ compiler to link in order to include the C++ libraries (which are used internally by
NLopt, even though it has a C API).
CAM
1621

-- 1621 of 1632 --

The minimization function, `nlopt_minimize`, is described in the [man page](http://en.wikipedia.org/wi-
ki/Man_page) (`api/nlopt_minimize.3`, which is installed by `make install`. See also the manual on our
web page.
There are also interfaces for Fortran, Python, Matlab, Octave, OCaml, GNU Guile, GNU R, Lua, and Julia.
Interfaces for other languages may be added in the future.
